deck_description:
Welcome to my Fiend Berserker Kuriboh Edison Format deck! This build focuses on a hybrid "Control and Bait" strategy to constantly pressure the opponent while setting up a massive, unexpected OTK.

Core Strategy The main goal is to generate early pressure with aggressive Fiends and -Skill Drain, while setting up our ultimate win condition: the -Kuriboh OTK. By loading -Darkness Neosphere into the GY via -Foolish Burial or using its own summoning condition, we can activate -Berserker Crush to give a tiny -Winged Kuriboh a massive 4000 ATK. When paired with -Staunch Defender, we force the opponent to crash their entire attack position field into our invincible furball.

Key Interactions & Combos The Goblin Bait Engine: -Goblin Elite Attack Force acts as a massive 2200 ATK beatstick. When it attacks and shifts to 1500 defense, it looks like an easy target for the opponent to run over. But when they declare an attack on it, we use it as field fodder (alongside a Fiend in hand like -Kuriboh) to Special Summon -Darkness Neosphere straight from the hand, blocking the attack and dropping a 4000 ATK boss monster on the board. Skill Drain Synergy: With 2x -Skill Drain active, -Goblin Elite Attack Force ignores its negative effect and stays in attack mode as a permanent threat. Meanwhile, the effects of -Giant Germ, -Grave Squirmer, and our Kuribohs all resolve in the Graveyard or hand, completely bypassing our own floodgate while shutting down the opponent's plays.

Main Deck Control Running 2 copies of -Skill Drain in the main deck gives us a massive edge in Game 1. It acts as a continuous floodgate that totally cripples top Edison decks like Blackwings, Machina, and Lightsworn, while we just swing over them with high-ATK beatsticks and our massive boss monster.

The Fiendish Side Deck Tech While our Main Deck focuses on the Kuriboh OTK and Skill Drain beatdown, our Side Deck features incredible Fiend-based utility. We bring in 3x -Possessed Dark Soul as our ultimate tech card. Not only is it a Fiend for our Neosphere discard costs, but it tributes itself to permanently steal the opponent's Level 3 or lower monsters, catching them off-guard and totally shutting down -Dandylion tokens, -Ryko, Lightsworn Hunter, and -Treeborn Frog setups.

Anti-Combo & Anti-Meta Tech The Side Deck is specifically tailored to crush the format's toughest matchups. We run 3x -D.D. Crow for aggressive Graveyard control against Zombies and Vayu Turbo, while -Cyber Dragon allows us to fuse away Machina boards into -Chimeratech Fortress Dragon. Additionally, -Light-Imprisoning Mirror keeps Lightsworn firmly in check, and we can bring in -Royal Decree for Games 2 or 3 to pivot against heavy-trap and Burn decks by swapping out our own -Skill Drain.

Feel free to test it out and let me know your thoughts in the comments!

deck_excerpt: 🌙 “The Moon rises… and your end is near.”
deck_description:
This version of Lunalight is built exclusively with 3 copies of the Legendary Decks ARC-V.

Although Lunalight finished in 2nd place at the 2025 World Championship, the archetype also received new support in the Legendary Decks ARC-V, notably with Lunalight Scarlet Tiger.

This new card is extremely powerful: it not only allows us to extend our combos, but, more importantly, to continue them even after an opponent’s interruption. It therefore gives the deck particularly impressive resilience against disruption.

Tri-Brigade Fraktall, although it is not part of the Lunalight archetype, also fits very well into the strategy. When necessary, it can allow us to start our combos or continue them after an opponent’s interruption. Together with Lunalight Scarlet Tiger, these two engines provide the deck with additional resilience, allowing it to play through numerous interactions and still end on a particularly strong board despite the opponent’s attempts to disrupt us.

The Legendary Decks ARC-V also contain the entire Lunalight engine, allowing access to the archetype’s full strategy with only 3 copies of the product.

The deck’s main objective is to Fusion Summon Lunalight Liger Dancer, our true boss monster. Thanks to the new support, it is now possible to end the turn with up to 3 copies of Lunalight Liger Dancer on the field, along with S:P Little Knight, creating an extremely difficult board for the opponent to break.

Lunalight Liger Dancer has 3800 ATK and is unaffected by the effects of cards that are not “Lunalight” cards. It is therefore particularly difficult to deal with, both through card effects and by battle. Its effect that destroys Special Summoned monsters controlled by the opponent also has a soft once-per-turn restriction: each copy of Lunalight Liger Dancer can use this effect once per turn. Therefore, if several Lunalight Liger Dancers are present on the field, each of them can use its effect, allowing us to generate multiple destructions and making the board even more difficult to deal with.

Lunalight is a combo deck that makes extensive use of its cards’ effects when they end up in the Graveyard. Lunalight Kaleido Chick notably allows us to send cards from the Deck or Extra Deck to the Graveyard in order to prepare different effects and access new combo lines. Its effect also has a soft once-per-turn restriction, which allows us to take advantage of it multiple times during the same turn by Special Summoning it again or bringing it back to the field. This allows the deck to quickly fill the Graveyard and chain together its combos.

Most Lunalight cards have particularly interesting effects when they are sent to the Graveyard, allowing the deck to turn the resources used during its combos into new possibilities for further plays.

Lunalight Gold Leo is the deck’s main starter. On its own, it allows us to start a large number of combos and can lead to a board that is extremely difficult for the opponent to deal with.

The deck also offers a very large number of ways to start its combos, making truly dead hands extremely rare. This multitude of starters and extenders gives the deck particularly appreciated stability and consistency.

Since the Lunalight engine is already quite large and takes up a significant portion of the available deck space, we prioritize essential cards and cards that provide high value to complete the list, such as Fuwalos, in order to maintain maximum efficiency without overloading the deck.

The deck does, however, have a few weaknesses. In particular, it needs to add many cards to the hand during its combos, making it vulnerable to cards such as Droll & Lock Bird. Despite this, it is still possible to establish a decent board even under Droll & Lock Bird.

Cards that disrupt the Graveyard also represent a significant problem, since the Lunalight strategy relies heavily on using and recycling its resources from the Graveyard.

The decklist presented here is a genuinely competitive decklist. Even though some small staples are not available in the Legendary Decks ARC-V, this version can already achieve good results at local or regional tournaments. It is also an excellent foundation for learning the Lunalight strategy and improving your skills with the archetype. With a few modifications and the addition of certain key cards, it is possible to optimize the decklist further in order to obtain a fully competitive version capable of competing with the Meta.

Overall, Lunalight is an explosive combo deck, but also particularly resilient thanks to its new support. With its ability to play through interruptions and build an extremely difficult board to break, the archetype remains an excellent option for players who enjoy Fusion decks and combo strategies.

The decklist presented here is therefore both an excellent foundation for discovering and mastering Lunalight, while also being competitive enough to aim for good results at local or regional tournaments. With a few improvements, it can evolve into a truly Meta-competitive version.

deck_excerpt: A consistent Monarch deck for Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Spirit Caller (NDS).
deck_description:
Deck Description

Spirit Caller Monarch is a Tribute Control deck built specifically for Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Spirit Caller on Nintendo DS.

The deck focuses on the classic Monarch strategy: establish Tribute material, summon a Monarch, resolve its removal effect, and gradually take control of the duel through repeated Tribute Summons.

Rather than relying on a single Monarch or a complicated combo, this build uses several different Monarchs with different forms of disruption, supported by defensive monsters, Tribute-based removal, and a large Spell/Trap control package.

The goal is to survive the early game, establish Tribute material, and turn every successful Tribute Summon into immediate card advantage or board control.

Monarch Lineup

The deck runs four different Monarchs, each serving a different purpose.

2× Mobius the Frost Monarch

Mobius is the deck's primary answer to opposing Spell and Trap Cards.

When Tribute Summoned, Mobius can destroy up to two Spell/Trap Cards on the field. This makes it particularly useful against decks that rely heavily on Set cards.

Mobius is especially valuable before entering the Battle Phase because clearing cards such as defensive Traps can make attacks considerably safer.

A common sequence is:

Tribute Summon Mobius → destroy opposing backrow → attack.

2× Granmarg the Rock Monarch

Granmarg provides another form of backrow removal, but unlike Mobius, it specifically targets Set cards.

This makes Granmarg useful when the opponent is relying on face-down cards and you need to remove a specific threat.

The distinction between Mobius and Granmarg gives the deck additional flexibility:

  • Mobius can destroy up to two Spell/Trap Cards.
  • Granmarg can destroy a Set card.

Granmarg therefore acts as another way to punish defensive boards without depending entirely on Mobius.

2× Thestalos the Firestorm Monarch

Thestalos attacks the opponent's hand rather than their field.

When Tribute Summoned, Thestalos forces the opponent to discard a random card from their hand. If the discarded card is a monster, it also inflicts additional damage based on that monster's Level.

This gives the deck a way to gain advantage even when the opponent's field is relatively empty.

Thestalos is particularly useful when the opponent has accumulated several cards in hand or when removing a card from the hand is more valuable than destroying something on the field.

2× Raiza the Storm Monarch

Raiza provides the deck's most flexible form of single-card removal.

When Tribute Summoned, Raiza can place a card on the field on top of its owner's Deck.

Unlike destruction, this does not simply send the card to the Graveyard. It can effectively remove an immediate threat while also manipulating the opponent's next draw.

Raiza is especially useful against cards that are difficult or undesirable to destroy.

Tribute Engine

The central engine of the deck is based around Treeborn Frog, Soul Exchange, and the defensive low-Level monsters.

Treeborn Frog

Treeborn Frog is the most important recurring Tribute resource in the deck.

Once Treeborn Frog reaches the Graveyard, it can return to the field during the Standby Phase under the appropriate conditions. This allows it to repeatedly become Tribute material for the Monarchs.

This is particularly powerful because the deck does not need to continually spend another card just to produce Tribute material.

The basic game plan is:

Treeborn Frog → revive → Tribute Summon Monarch → resolve Monarch effect.

One important consideration is that Treeborn Frog requires you to control no Spell/Trap Cards when its revival effect activates and resolves. Therefore, you need to manage your backrow carefully when planning to use Treeborn Frog as your recurring Tribute engine.

Soul Exchange

The deck runs 2× Soul Exchange as another way to facilitate Tribute Summons.

Soul Exchange allows one of the opponent's monsters to become Tribute material for your Tribute Summon.

This is extremely useful when the opponent controls a monster that is difficult to remove through normal battle.

For example:

Opponent controls a powerful monster
→ Activate Soul Exchange
→ use that monster as Tribute material
→ Tribute Summon Raiza/Zaborg/etc.

The important trade-off is that you cannot conduct your Battle Phase during the turn you activate Soul Exchange. Therefore, Soul Exchange should generally be viewed as a removal + Tribute setup tool, rather than something to use when you need to attack immediately.

Brain Control

Brain Control provides another way to convert the opponent's monster into Tribute material.

Instead of destroying an opposing monster, you temporarily take control of it and can use it as Tribute material for a Monarch.

This creates a powerful interaction:

Take opponent's monster → Tribute it → summon Monarch → gain additional removal.

This is particularly effective when the opponent has a single strong monster that is difficult to defeat through combat.

Defensive Monsters

The deck uses several low-Level monsters to survive until its Tribute engine becomes active.

Marshmallon

Marshmallon provides defensive value because it cannot be destroyed by battle while face-up.

It can therefore stall stronger monsters while you wait to draw a Monarch or Tribute enabler.

Spirit Reaper

Spirit Reaper serves a similar defensive role.

Its inability to be destroyed by battle makes it useful as a temporary wall, while its direct-attack effect can also force the opponent to discard a card.

This gives Spirit Reaper both defensive and hand-disruption potential.

Penguin Soldier

Penguin Soldier provides additional tempo control.

Its effect can return monsters on the field to the hand, allowing it to remove threats without destroying them.

It can also help clear the field before a later Tribute Summon.

D.D. Assailant & D.D. Warrior Lady

These two provide battle-based removal.

Rather than relying entirely on Monarch effects, the deck can use them to remove opposing monsters through their banishing effects.

This is particularly useful against monsters that are difficult to destroy normally or monsters that have useful Graveyard effects.

Sangan

Sangan provides consistency by searching appropriate low-ATK monsters from the Deck when it is sent from the field to the Graveyard.

It can therefore help find defensive monsters or other small monsters needed to establish the next Tribute Summon.

Breaker the Magical Warrior

Breaker provides another source of Spell/Trap removal while also functioning as a normal attacker.

This gives the deck backrow interaction even when a Monarch is not available.

Morphing Jar

Morphing Jar acts as a hand reset and draw engine.

When its effect successfully resolves, both players discard their hands and draw new cards. This can be useful when the deck has accumulated an awkward hand or when the opponent is holding a large number of cards.

Because this is a high-impact effect, it should be used carefully rather than flipped automatically.

Spell Removal and Board Control

The deck contains a relatively heavy Spell/Trap removal package:

  • 2× Giant Trunade
  • Heavy Storm
  • Mystical Space Typhoon
  • Breaker the Magical Warrior
  • 2× Mobius
  • 2× Granmarg

This gives the deck many ways to deal with defensive boards.

Giant Trunade

Giant Trunade returns all Spell/Trap Cards on the field to their owners' hands.

Rather than permanently destroying the cards, Giant Trunade is primarily used to clear the field and create a safe window for your plays.

For example:

Giant Trunade → clear backrow → Tribute Summon Monarch → attack.

It can also be useful when you need to remove your own backrow temporarily to enable Treeborn Frog.

Heavy Storm

Heavy Storm provides a full Spell/Trap wipe.

It is particularly valuable when the opponent has accumulated several Set cards and you need to clear the field before committing to a major play.

Mystical Space Typhoon

MST provides precise one-for-one removal.

Unlike Giant Trunade and Heavy Storm, MST can be used to remove one specific problematic card without affecting your own backrow.

Nobleman of Crossout

Nobleman of Crossout gives the deck another way to deal with face-down monsters.

This is especially useful when the opponent relies on defensive flip monsters or when attacking a Set monster would otherwise be risky.

Book of Moon

Book of Moon is one of the most flexible cards in the deck.

It can:

  • turn an opposing monster face-down;
  • disrupt a monster's position;
  • interfere with an opponent's setup;
  • protect one of your monsters from certain situations;
  • help create favorable battle situations.

It is therefore useful both offensively and defensively.

Premature Burial

Premature Burial provides additional access to monsters from the Graveyard.

In a Tribute-based deck, reviving a monster can immediately create another Tribute opportunity.

It can also bring back a useful defensive monster or previously used monster when you need to rebuild your field.

Swords of Revealing Light

Swords of Revealing Light provides temporary protection against attacks and reveals face-down monsters.

Its primary purpose in this deck is to buy time.

Monarch decks do not always establish their Tribute engine immediately, so having a card that can temporarily stop the opponent's attacks gives you additional turns to draw into your Monarchs and Tribute resources.

Trap Lineup

The Trap lineup is heavily focused on surviving the opponent's attacks and controlling the field.

2× Dust Tornado

Dust Tornado gives the deck additional Spell/Trap removal while also providing the ability to Set a Spell/Trap from your hand afterward.

This complements the Monarch lineup by allowing the deck to control the opponent's backrow even before a Mobius or Granmarg becomes available.

2× Sakuretsu Armor

Sakuretsu Armor provides straightforward monster removal when the opponent attacks.

It helps protect your Life Points and allows the deck to survive against aggressive decks until it can establish a Monarch.

2× Trap Hole

Trap Hole provides another layer of monster removal by responding to an opponent's Normal Summon.

It is especially useful against powerful monsters that would otherwise establish immediate board pressure.

Mirror Force

Mirror Force is the deck's strongest mass battle-removal option.

If the opponent commits several monsters to an attack, Mirror Force can punish the entire attacking field.

This is especially valuable when the deck is behind on board presence.

Solemn Judgment

Solemn Judgment is the deck's flexible emergency answer.

It can be used to stop an important Summon, Spell, or Trap at the cost of Life Points.

Because of its Life Point cost, it should generally be saved for plays that would otherwise significantly threaten your position.

Jar of Greed

The deck runs 2× Jar of Greed to improve consistency.

Rather than using complicated draw engines, Jar of Greed simply provides an additional card when activated.

This helps the deck reach important cards such as:

  • Monarchs
  • Treeborn Frog
  • Soul Exchange
  • removal
  • defensive cards

It also helps maintain the 40-card deck size without sacrificing access to additional resources.

Overall Game Plan

The deck generally plays in three stages.

Early Game — Survive

Do not rush into Tribute Summons if the board is not ready.

Use:

  • Marshmallon
  • Spirit Reaper
  • D.D. Assailant
  • D.D. Warrior Lady
  • Penguin Soldier
  • Trap Hole
  • Sakuretsu Armor
  • Swords of Revealing Light

to prevent the opponent from gaining too much momentum.

At the same time, try to get Treeborn Frog into the Graveyard.

Mid Game — Establish Tribute Control

Once you have Tribute material available, begin using your Monarchs.

Choose the Monarch according to the situation:

Mobius → remove multiple Spell/Trap Cards
Granmarg → remove a Set card
Thestalos → disrupt the opponent's hand
Raiza → put an important card on top of the Deck

This is the point where the deck begins generating its main advantage.

Late Game — Maintain the Advantage

Once the opponent's resources have been reduced, continue using your Monarchs and defensive cards to keep control of the field.

The objective isn't necessarily to perform one huge OTK.

Instead, the deck wins by repeatedly doing:

Tribute → Monarch effect → remove/disrupt → attack → repeat

Eventually the opponent runs out of monsters, backrow, and cards in hand.

Key Interactions

Treeborn Frog + Monarchs

The most fundamental interaction:

Treeborn Frog → revive during Standby Phase → Tribute Summon Monarch

This gives the deck a renewable Tribute source.

Soul Exchange + Monarch

When the opponent has a problematic monster:

Soul Exchange → use opponent's monster as Tribute → summon the appropriate Monarch

This effectively combines removal with Tribute Summoning.

Brain Control + Monarch

Another way to turn the opponent's monster into Tribute material:

Brain Control → take monster → Tribute it → Monarch

This can generate significant tempo because the opponent loses their monster while you establish a 2400 ATK Monarch.

Backrow Removal + Monarch

The deck has multiple ways to clear defensive cards:

Giant Trunade
Heavy Storm
MST
Dust Tornado
Breaker
Mobius
Granmarg

This allows you to choose whether to remove backrow before or during your Tribute play depending on the situation.

Strengths

Flexible removal:
The four Monarchs cover monsters, Spell/Trap Cards, Set cards, and the opponent's hand.

Strong Tribute engine:
Treeborn Frog and Soul Exchange make Tribute Summoning much easier.

Good defensive capability:
Marshmallon, Spirit Reaper, Sakuretsu Armor, Trap Hole, Mirror Force, and Swords of Revealing Light provide several ways to survive.

Multiple forms of interaction:
The deck can attack the opponent's field, hand, or resources depending on the situation.

No single-card dependency:
Although Treeborn Frog is extremely valuable, the deck can still function using ordinary Tribute material and Soul Exchange.

Weaknesses

The main weakness is that this is still a Tribute-based deck.

Drawing several Monarchs without enough Tribute material can produce an awkward hand. The deck therefore needs to carefully balance aggression with resource management.

Another important weakness is Treeborn Frog's interaction with Spell/Trap Cards. Because Treeborn Frog needs the appropriate empty-backrow condition to revive, you should not blindly Set every Trap when you are planning to use Treeborn as your next Tribute.

Similarly, Soul Exchange prevents your Battle Phase, so it should be used when its removal/Tribute value is more important than attacking that turn.

Recommended Playstyle

This deck is best played as a patient control deck.

Don't try to summon a Monarch every time you have one available.

Instead, ask:

Which Monarch gives me the most advantage in the current situation?

If the opponent has several Set cards:

Mobius

If there is one particularly problematic Set card:

Granmarg

If their hand is large:

Thestalos

If there is a monster or other card that you don't want to destroy:

Raiza

The strength of this deck comes from making the right Tribute at the right time, rather than simply summoning the biggest monster available.

deck_excerpt: If all goes to plan the person across from you will have exactly zero fun :)
deck_description:
This is a variant on the pure Magician decklist I posted a while ago with the new MAMO cards. I was watching an MBT video and he talked about Kali Yuga being a worse Azathot because rank 7s are more clunky to deal with than rank 4s and that gave me a thought. I had a look through the rank 7 pool for generic dark monsters and found exactly one that fits the bill of being able to detach two materials on turn one without running (more) main deck garnets. Voloferniges, the Darkest Dragon Doomrider lets you detach two to pop a face up card and if he has a dragon as material its a quick effect (but we don't care about that). Ideally you want to pop a copy of Double Iris Magician in order to get the search off while also ideally triggering an Astrograph/Starfrost, Star Pendgraph, or both.

 

Once you have a Voloferniges without material you just need to set the Rank-Up-Magic from the deck with Rusty Bardiche who's pretty easy to make. I did play around with Silent Boots rather than Doomed Soleret as the PK garnet because you can then banish him to grab a Fog blade as a backup negate in case the Rank-Up-Magic gets negated but I decided that was a little win-more and the advantage of Doomed Soleret is that if you open him you can just special him out to search the Rank-Up-Magic and then use him as material for Beyond the Pendulum of Override Dragon. Previously when I was testing with Silent Boots you would need to extend into Ignister to spin back the boots and then send with Bardiche which sucked and was generally terrible.

 

The deck is generally still bricky because you need 2-3 engine cards minimum to make plays and a fair few combinations of engine cards just do absolutely nothing on their own (think DA, Star Pengraph, and Harm). The central game plan is to summon horoscope or an Astrograph in order to make a pre pend summon Beyond or Override so we're playing loads of ways to search that.

 

There are two copies of Odd-Eyes Vortex Dragon because if you end on Exceed the Pendulum you can revive a Starfrost Magician from your grave in your opponents main phase which can then fuse itself with the Vortex on field to make a second Vortex and trigger its bounce as well as dodging droplet or imperm if need be.

 

The extra deck is extremely tight, so much so that I side the Zeus cards to swap in for the Kali Yuga BS when you know that you're gonna go second. I'm not all too married to the other side deck cards, the new Odd-Eyes is just a fun OTK tool which has an almost broken search effect that they had to make bad by putting another stupid restriction on. Duster and LS are reporting for duty to help overcome my fear of floodgates and solemns. When you know you're going first Judgement is just fun and Dragon's Mind is just another three Solemns because you typically end on at least one, possibly multiple monsters with exactly 2500 original ATK.

 

The handtraps are just the good ones, Fuwalos because its the best Mulcharmy and we only really have the space for one of them, Ash to kill other peoples Mulcharmies, and Droll because its just a good high impact one that unlike Nibiru you can keep to use when going first. Mulcharmies (other than Meowls enjoy your one draw lmao) are super scary so the Ashes help but Called by and Triple Tac are there for backup, I was playing Crossout but it just feels bad because it doesn't even work against Purulia for us so its basically another called by but only for Fuwa, Ash, and Droll which is maybe worth playing but the amount of non-engine is really pushing Magicians about as far as they can manage while still actually doing something most of the time.

 

To the three people who actually read this somewhat silly late night ramble, please let me know if you have any questions or suggestions because I love this pet deck to bits and can't wait to get my grubby little mitts on the physical copies of Horoscope, Starfrost, and Unicorn Parallel.

deck_excerpt: The deck that keeps on skipping...
deck_description:
The main concept of the deck is simple, keep the game going until you have the card called Magical Merchant on the field. This card has a simple Flip ability, which is that when it is flipped face-up you reveal cards from the top of your deck until a Spell/Trap card, then place the rest of the cards in the GY. This card is simple in just text alone, because what do you do when you Mill your deck, you need to know have a way to win. Even before that, what happens if you don't draw Magical Merchant your opening hand... Simple, delay, control, and search. Many decks in Edison format have a simple way to keep being reliable, which means a skilled pilot must be present for the deck to run well, now I am not the most skilled, or even the best pilot for this deck, but I have fun using the deck to have more of a explosive, usaully definitive win. 

Break Down of the deck...

First the delay portion of the deck
Cards such as Battle Fader and Cyber Valley. These cards simply delay a battle phase, stop it, and then gain advantage, unfortunatly it can't be a bigger package, since for the deck you want to find the Merchant before the opponent develops a board to stop you. 

Second the Control portion of the deck. 
Cards such as, D.D. Crow, Ryko, and Cyber Dragon. Now these control the opponent by stripping them of recources, we want the opponent to waste their larger removal tools to stop the aggression and to allow the plan to go through. D.D. Crow, strips any deck that uses DAD, or any other graveyard tricks to not be able to use them or stop the reallocation of those recources. Ryko gets rid of Monsters in the way, and even acts as removal in a pinch, preventing damage to pilot as much as possible. It removes most things that also control this deck as well. Finally Cyber Dragon, this card simply just removes other monsters and attract removal, this deck would rather not have the Merchant removed, so having the opponent hit the Dragon is a must.

Finally the Search and Win Portion. 
Cards such as Machina Gearframe, Witch of the Black Rose, Scrap Recycler, and Super-Nimble Mega Hampster. All of this cards search either for another piece of the deck, so the control portion, or the win con itself. (Which is Machina Fortress, Gallis the Star Beast and Cyber Eltanin in addition to the merchant.) Machina Gearframe searches for the other parts of the Machina engine, so the Fortress or Force. Scrap Recyler can trade in used or milled copies of the Machina engine to generate more cards, and even on normal summon, dumps the Fortress to the GY for us, which if needed allows the deck to work without being entirly dependant on a good mill, or specific cards to be milled. The Witch of the Black Rose, allows for the deck to have a reliable way to keep drawing deeper, allowing the spells to the grave keeping deeper mills, or searching deeper for any part of the deck, granted this is not a direct search but it does allow for cards to go even on advantage. The Super-Nimble Mega Hampster serves two purposes, there are only a select few cards in the deck that depend on flipping, which is Ryko and the Merchant, so the opponent will most likely want to remove the monster and not attack blindly into face-down cards. The second purpose is to search and dig for Ryko, which allows for even more removal of cards that hurt the game plan of a mostly monster deck. 
The win con of the deck relies on many factors, which is why the deck has multiple ways to win and refresh the deck. The deck does have a glaring weakness, which is drawing the game too long after milling, and then dying due to drawing empty. So there are many ways to force keep cards returning to the deck, and keeping the pilot alive. One of the ways the pilot stays alive is there being two spell cards, so if one gets milled early, you can try again, and second, you are not as likely to mill the entire deck and die before the pilot gets a chance to win. The two spell cards used are Pot of Avarice, which given milling most of the deck not only allows a refil on reliable forms of damage, it also allows the deck to plan a win, the pilot must keep track of what cards are in the deck to ensure even after the win con is attempted, that they can continue with more follow-up. The way to win with Pot of Avarice is to keep filling the deck with high level monsters, only if however, the card Gallis the Star Beast is hand. Gallis allows for the Pilot to keep revealing and milling more high level monsters to burn the opponent out. If Gallis is not in hand and the Machina Fortress is milled, then the high level machine monsters can be shuffled back to ensure the Fortress can keep coming back and placing pressure. The best way to win though is Cyber Eltanin, which turns all the monsters milled, if there is enough, to a win. The Eltanin allows the board to be cleared of monsters and places extreme amounts of pressure to instanly close out a game, although it will be a target of Solemn Judgenments and Bottomless Trap Holes.


The Sideboard is last and it is the hardest to manage based on expierence in the meta and what decks the pilot is expected to face, most of the sideboard is removal and control tools, the deck will remove some of the win-con and search elements to focus on removal of issues. Cold Wave and Ultimate Offering allow the pilot to block out counter play and sometimes, allow for card advantage on opponents turns. Monsters such as Ancient Gear Soldier allow the pilot to force the game win and allow for the game to be shut out during the battle phase and stop the opponents delays.

In Conclusion...
There are some cards I did not mention and those, function similarly to others in the deck, which allows for different plays and more sideboarding efforts without causing the deck to have as many weak points. The deck is very weak to very early aggression, and will have terrible match ups into Frog Monarch along with heavy removal and control decks. Which does not mean an auto lose, but can cause issues if unprepared for the situation. The decks strengths can be early game control, into a near unavioble win. Once a wincon loop or attack is established the deck just takes over games.

Thank you to any pilots that have left public deck lists and spear headed this stratgy, including Federico Mercuri and TimPontes, both deck lists and my local games shapped this deck to what it is now.

deck_excerpt: Clowns can draw up to 11 cards?!
deck_description:
The clowns are in town, and this time they have an arsenal of otherworldly weaponry as their featured performance - the Runicks! 
 
Clown Crew Runick is a GENESYS take on the advantage centred gameplay that Runick decks offer. This strategy cobbles together 3 engines that generate a metric ton of cards - Clown Crew, Runicks and Radiant Typhoon!  Clown Crew offers layered interruption, features a draw 4 with Matinee Operatics and a draw 2 with Biancaviso! It also grants access to a ridiculous instant win button in the form of "The Wicked Avatar," making the one-sided anti-spell lingering floodgate viable! Runicks grant targeting removal with the power of a draw 3 featuring their ace card, Runick Fountain. Finally, the small but powerful Radiant Typhoon engine grants easy access to backrow removal with their Mystical Space Typhoon spam! Fonix shuffles cards from the field into the deck, and Radiant Typhoon Vision is a draw 2! 
 
More often than not, all the draws grant you access to all three engines, drawing you up to 11 cards a turn! Before you know it, you'll have 15+ cards in your possession (full backrow, full field of monsters with 6 cards in hand) all ready to interrupt your opponent! If you're addicted to drawing a bazillion cards like me, drowning your opponent in card advantage and peak midrange gameplay - I suggest you play Clown Crew Runick! 
 
While there are no mainline combos with Clown Crew Runick, Clown Crew does have an optimal combo that it prefers to follow for maximum advantage. Here is the combo with Clown Crew Flair and 1 discard: 
 
  1. Activate Clown Flair to add Clown Crew Rehearsal and discard 1 card from hand. (If you already have Rehearsal set Clown Crew New Face from deck and discard New Face so it places itself on field). 
  2. Activate Clown Crew Rehearsal tributing Clown Crew Flair and adding Clown Crew Malabrisme and Clown Crew Biancaviso.
  3. (Optional, especially when breaking boards) The trigger effect of Flair in the GY activates when it is tributed to either shuffle all ritual monsters back to the deck or to set an opponent's monster to face down defense position. 
  4. Activate Malabrisme to special summon from Extra Deck Clown Crew Fiends and Clown Crew Diabolo. 
  5. Tribute summon Biancaviso by tributing Fiends and Diabolo. 
  6. Activate in CL1 Biancaviso to draw 2 cards, CL2 Fiends to set Clown Crew Matinee Operatics from deck, and Diabolo to set Clown Crew New Face from deck (If you already have New Face set Soiree Operations). 
  7. Activate Matinee Operatics. Use Matinee Operatics' effect so special summon Clown Crew Meteor from deck. 
  8. During the End Phase, draw 3 with Matinee Operatics.
  9. During your opponent's Standby Phase, you can draw 1 by shuffling 3 cards back into the deck with New Face. 
  10. During your opponent's Main Phase, you can tribute summon with Biancaviso to generate interruptions and card advantage. 
 
Have fun clowning on your opponents with Clown Crew Runick and destroy them as you draw into your entire deck! 

GLHF Duelists!

deck_excerpt: Isolde OTK ft. Musical Sumo Dice Games
deck_description:
Hello there! In this deck, you will witness the magnificence of two Warriors building up the funniest win-condition. Let's roll!

 

 

Glossary

  • NS - Normal Summon
  • SS - Special Summon
  • GY: Graveyard
  • MP1: Main Phase 1
  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone
  • EMZ: Extra Monster Zone

 

Gameplan

1) Isolde needs two Warriors. Here are your options to summon her;

  • Sublimation + Squeak
  • Connector + Dolphin
  • SS - Sage + Warrior
  • Warrior + SS - Fire Flint
  • NS - Warrior + SS - Butterspy
  • NS - Marauding/Goblindbergh + SS - Warrior
  • Armageddon >>> Send Cloak/Boots to GY >>> Brigandine

2) Isolde >>> Find Doppel >>> Send Broken + Cursed + Gearblade + Deep-Seated to GY >>> SS - Armageddon

3) Armageddon sends Cloak/Boots/Zephyros to GY >>> Activate Cursed + Gearblade >>> Burning + Gearblade in your hand...

  • If Zephyros is sent to GY, place Burning/Gearblade and return it to hand with Zephyros to SS him.
  • If Cloak/Boots is sent to GY, use them to find Brigandine and SS it.

4) Armageddon + Zephyros/Brigandine = Dugares >>> Dugares revives Armageddon >>> Armageddon sends Monk to GY...

  • Before moving to next step, don't forget to place Burning on the field.

5) Isolde + Dugares = Aleister >>> Aleister + Armageddon = Selene#1 >>> Selene revives Monk >>> Monk finds Uppercutter >>> Uppercutter finds Sparrer >>> SS - Sparrer >>> Uppercutter + Sparrer = Dempsey...

  • While doing this step, make sure Selene#1 is at leftmost EMZ and Monk+Dempsey are in 1st and 2nd MMZ.

6) Dempsey finds Renaud >>> SS - Renaud >>> Find Cursed and play on Selene >>> Activate Burning to skip MP1 of opponent >>> Bounce Burning to hand with Cursed...

  • While doing this step, place Renaud to 5th MMZ.
  • With this step, you will have two spells for two future Monk usages.

7) Selene#2 = Selene#1 + Monk + Dempsey >>> Selene revives Monk >>> Monk finds Ferret >>> Selene + Renaud = Saryuja >>> Ferret = Micro + Gama + Level 4 Springans >>> Replace Saryuja with Zealantis...

  • While doing this step, make sure Selene#2 is at leftmost EMZ and Monk+Ferret are in 1st and 2nd MMZ. Saryuja has to be at rightmost EMZ.

8) Use Zealantis to reset the board. Monster placements are as follows...

  • 1st-3rd MMZ: Micro + Gama
  • 2nd MMZ: Zealantis
  • 4th-5th MMZ: Monk + Level 4 Springans

9) With the board setup you did in #8, Link Summon Protectcode to 1st MMZ via Micro + Gama + Level 4 Springans as materials. This action triggers Micro to let you find Cynet Circuit. Then, use Monk to place 2nd Level 4 Springans monster.

10) Merrymaker = Monk + Level 4 Springans >>> Use Merrymaker to send 3rd Level 4 Springans to GY >>> Replace Merrymaker with Champion and place it to leftmost EMZ >>> Use Champion to find Tally-Ho!

11) Tally-Ho! to detach 3 mats from Champion >>> Add Branga to hand >>> SS - Branga + 2 x Level 4 Springans

12) Gung-Ho! = 2 x Level 4 Springans >>> SS - Sargas >>> Branga + Sargas = Fantasix >>> Fantasix finds Astral Force >>> Zealantis + Champion + Fantasix + Protectcode = Singularity >>> Revive Protectcode...

  • While doing this step; place Protectcode to 1st or 3rd MMZ, Gung-Ho to 4th MMZ and Singularity to leftmost EMZ.
  • If you have done everything correct so far, you can feed Gung-Ho with Main Deck Springans monsters that are in GY.

13) Attach anything you can find to Gung-Ho and play Astral Force to replace it with Sumo Dice on 4th MMZ. Sumo Dice should have 6 materials, if you did everything right. Then, set "Cynet Circuit" from #9 and end your turn.

14) When it's your opponent's Draw Phase, activate "Cynet Circuit" to fill your opponent's 1st-2nd-3rd MMZ and your 2nd MMZ. One of these monsters you are going to give the opponent has to be Gama and has to be in Attack Position, which will force the opponent to be in Battle Phase, thanks to MP1 skip you did in #6. Other two should be harmless monsters, independent of battle position, such as Monk and Dugares.

15) After placing your monster on your 2nd MMZ, Special Summon Doppel to 1st or 3rd MMZ, which you found it via Isolde way back in #2.

16) Due to abilities of Gama and MP1 skip you did in #6, the instant you are in Battle Phase, Sumo Dice will start rolling the dice. Starting from 4th MMZ, whichever place Sumo Dice lands will be instant win for you, thanks to the brilliance of monster placements you did in steps 12-15.

deck_name: Superheavy Samurai Prodigy Wakaushi - Maliss / Mitsurugi
deck_description:
This deck is designed around comboing into established boards by using board breakers and using the deck master, Superheavy Samurai Prodigy Wakaushi, to combo without using the normal summon and offering a free Pendulum Summon. So, if the combo is disrupted, there are still other options to continue.

 

From Superheavy Samurai Prodigy Wakaushi, you can do the full Mitsurugi combo (using King of the Feral Imps), and then the Maliss combo (using Code Igniter, which searches and summons Cyberse Code Magician). Any two Level 4 monsters can reach both of those combos, and with Cyberse Contract Witch you can also add Ame no Habakiri no Mitsurugi, so your pendulum summon can also help you reach those combos if Superheavy Samurai Prodigy Wakaushi is interrupted.

Alternatively, you can also use Superheavy Samurai Prodigy Wakaushi to do a small Sky Striker combo to protect your other plays, if you have starters in hand like Ame no Habakiri no Mitsurugi and Maliss Dormouse. Sky Striker Ace - Camellia sends Sky Striker Mobilize - Engage!, which adds Sky Striker Mecha - Widow Anchor or Hornet Drones, and then you can summon S:P Little Knight.

The chance to draw at least 1 board breaker (including Kaijus) in your starting hand + draw is 60%, without considering the card draw effects and the searches you can do to increase your chances while baiting interactions.

 

Main combo: https://www.masterduelmeta.com/combo/6a9caac33983111f093a9a1e

The endboard consists of 10 interactions and 4 follow-up/protection effects:

Every turn (6): 1 destroy all monsters any opponent controls, 1 non-target banish, 1 targeting banish, 2 bounces (at once), banish up to 3 cards in any graveyard, 1 hand rip (or negate), draw 1, reborn 1 reptile every summon.

Only once (4): 1 omni-negate, 1 link summon using a link monster from 1 opponent, 1 non-target banish, 1 targeting banish, reborn 1 reptile.

 

If you have Decode Talker Integration and Firewall Dragon Singularity on the board, the OTK should be simple to achieve, even against 3 players.

 

Alternatives:

Superheavy Samurai Soulpiercer 

S:P Little Knight 

I:P Masquerena 

Firewall Dragon Darkfluid - Neo Tempest Terahertz, Cyberse Desavewurm, Danmari @Ignister 

You can choose to run I:P Masquerena instead of Decode Talker Integration, so that you can have an extra negate on one of your opponent's turns with W:P Fancy Ball. Or you could also run Firewall Dragon Darkfluid - Neo Tempest Terahertz (there's more than enough bodies to summon it, but it requires more Extra Deck space).

(The effects don't activate though if you send with Kaleido Chick, but Kaleido Chick does take their names, which is helpful for your Fusions. Remember that now). Konami tried to make this deck hard to get your Liger Dancer out by requiring three material and Lunalight Leo Dancer, but this deck doesn't care. Kaleido Chick can send your Leo Dancer to your GY and works as it. Heavy Polymerization can just use your Leo Dancer in your Extra Deck. Lunalight Wolf will just banish the material for your first Liger Dancer and get your second one.

This deck is incredibly meta-resistant. The only real problems are Kashtira's GY ban, Enneacraft running Dimension Shifter, and Exosister's GY moving. Other than that, you either outpower or just ignore any other deck.

INTRODUCTION

A friend and I had the idea of building this due to frustrations we have with Standard format. I won't go into details, but we wanted to play Goat, but also didn't want to leave some of our favorite decks behind. I tried to make sure this would be balanced, doing what I could to ensure this wouldn't surpass the top tiers of GOAT format. As much as we love our favorite decks, it is important to exercise restraint if you want something new to fit in. If anyone has thoughts on my balancing, I would love to hear them!

 

NEW CARDS AND REASONINGS FOR INCLUSION/LIMITATIONS

Laundry: Her effect is luck based, but has very little payoff. I could see some application with Chaos, but I am absolutely NOT going in that direction, as it would be against the spirit of this project. Back on topic, with her power level, it may be fair to allow her to tag out into Ernus with her other effect.

Parlor: While her effect is ordinarily strong, I feel that she is balanced so long I keep Tinkhec and Lorpar banned. This means that she is unable to tag out to anything, not even Ernus as that card is Level 7. She does exist, however, to send Ernus to the Graveyard.

Ernus: I placed a lot of thought into whether or not the 'true forms' of the archetype would be okay here. With a limited lineup, the discard to summon effect appears to be fine, and I made sure that the only card that can tag into this one wasn't anything too powerful. Dragonmaids do tend to excel in recovery, which may or may not be a problem. Part of me thinks this is fine, as I feel my plan of using Masked Dragon into Laundry into Ernus is similar to the existing strategy of Armed Dragons.

House: This may be a controversial one. I'm keeping her limited to 1 even though she appears to be very strong by GOAT format standards. This is something I just have to test out as I'm trying to have some degree of payoff for using the deck. If she ends up being too much, I'll remove her from the deck.

Send-Off: This card is basically a more gimmicky version of Waboku. It is fine.

Welcome: The power bonus is honestly negligible and the recovery effect probably won't do that much given the limitations I have placed on the deck. It is yet another card that exists for flavor.

 

CLOSING THOUGHTS

This deck is still in it's conceptual stages, and I know I am going to have to double check the GOAT format banlist. Even so, I look forward to testing this out with my friend one day. Maybe this may give other people ideas as well, but if it does, please be sure to respect the spirit of the format. Once again, feedback is appreciated! As a recent convert to GOAT, this format looks like it may help me to have fun with this game again!

Greetings! Previously, a crossover with Isolde and Telefon occured to win with C88. This time, we will do the same for Number 88.

 

 

Glossary

  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Gameplan

1) With your Telefon arsenal, place 2 x Telefon on the field, which will cycle with each other. Here are your cards:

  • One for One / Foolish Burial / Small World
  • Machine Duplication / Dimension Dice / Dice Dungeon
  • Naganaki / Gamer / Convex

a) Alternatively, you can also use Schedule cards to unlock Telefon cycle. Here is the pattern...

  • Exceptional >>> Urgent = Babeldecker + Telefon >>> Ballista = Babeldecker + Telefon >>> Ballista finds Gear Box >>> Gear Box searches Convex
  • Use Exceptional in GY to send Ballista to GY and Special Summon Babeldecker >>> Special Summon Convex and set its Level to 10 >>> Flying Launcher = Convex + Babeldecker >>> Launcher finds Telefon

2) With 2 x Telefon and Linkuriboh/Launcher, you can make 2 x Virus, which will be used for Isolde. When Isolde is Link Summoned, add Gardna to your hand. Then, send Gearblade+Horn+Nuzzler+Moon to GY, which enables you to place Armageddon. There, use Armageddon to send Monk to GY and add Gearblade to your hand...

  • If you haven't done so far, place 2 x Telefon to 3rd and 5th MMZ from hereon, which will matter a lot during the following steps. Also, keep 4th MMZ for Monk in the future.

3) By cycling Telefon, Synchro Summon all monsters. Meanwhile, do the followings...

  • Add "Black Garden" to your hand with "Garden Rose Maiden".
  • Play "Black Garden" before placing Dragonshell to 1st MMZ. When there is one Rose token, destroy Garden and said token to place Monk on 4th MMZ.

4) Use Monk to place Ferret on 2nd MMZ. Then, use Traffic Ghost and Saryuja in a way that only these monsters remain...

  • 2nd MMZ: Ferret
  • 4th MMZ: Monk
  • 5th MMZ: Telefon

5) Use Ferret to place Cattycorn + Angel O1 + Brotaur on the field, right under the arrows of Saryuja. Then, replace Saryuja with Zealantis and activate Zealantis to reset the board. Only Cattycorn + Angel O1 + Brotaur + Monk + Telefon will remain and don't place Zealantis by accident.

6) After the placement of monsters in #6, do the following actions...

  • Cattycorn >>> Light World
  • Brotaur >>> Target Angel O1 and discard Gardna >>> The World
  • Monk + Cattycorn = Photon Dragon >>> Queen's Light

7) Activate "Light World" and Tribute Summon World via Angel O1 by getting rid of Photon Dragon + Telefon. Here, choose the outcome as Heads for World to skip your opponent's turn at the cost of sending two monsters you control to GY.

8) When 2 x Telefon + The World + Angel O1 + Brotaur are on the field, apply Queen's Light on World ot make all monsters Level 8. Then, XYZ Summon Number 88 with Angel O1 + Brotaur + Telefon as materials. To win with Number 88, you need to detach 3 materials from Number 88 while placing 3 x Destiny Counters on Number 88. When 3 x Destiny Counters are on Number 88, you win the duel! So, start by detaching Telefon from Number 88.

9) Use Rose Maiden to revive Dragonshell and revive 2nd Telefon. Then, end your turn and skip your opponent's turn with World by sending Dragonshell + Telefon to GY. On your next turn, detach 2nd material from Number 88 and end your turn to skip another turn by sending World + Telefon to GY. Finally, detach last material from Number 88 to win the game!

 

If you wonder how to save up some SR and UR points, I can show you:

- "Traffic Ghost" can be found by completing the tutorial to save 30 UR!

- "Galaxy Photon Dragon" can be collected by purchasing "Origin of the Galaxy" Structure Deck to save 30 SR!

- "Machine Duplication" can be collected by purchasing "Cyber Kaiser" Structure Deck to save 90 SR!

- "Small World" can be found within "Power Up Selection" Timed Pack to save 90 SR!

- "Isolde, Two Tales of the Noble Knights" can be found within "Guided by the Noble Blade" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Summoner Monk" can be found within "True Awakening of the Oathbound Knights" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "Worldsea Dragon Zealantis" can be found within "Raging God of the Sea" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Dice Dungeon" + "Dimension Dice" + "Convex Knight" can be found within "Legacy Pack" to save 180 SR and 90 UR!

- "Exceptional Schedule" + "Urgent Schedule" + "Flying Launcher" can be found within "Dreadnought Advance" Secret Pack to save 150 SR!

- "Ancient Gear Ballista" can be found within "Gargantuan Gears" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "Garden Rose Maiden" + "Black Garden" can be found within "Exquisite Jet-Black Rose" Secret Pack to save 60 SR!

- "Number 88" can be found within "Colossal Mech" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "The World" + "Light Barrier" can be found within "Hand of Fate" Secret Pack to save 30 SR and 30 UR!

 

So, in total, you can save up to 690 SR and 240 UR, if you are willing to spend some gems. Other SR and UR cards I didn't mention are essential.

 

That's all for this one. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Have fun in Master Duel!

deck_excerpt: Break boards with Subspace Shaddoll Train Cyber Ancient Gear
deck_description:
STAGC (Subspace Shaddoll Train Ancient Gear Cyber)

Its too expensive to have both Statue and Advance, so we got with Statue because its very accessible in the deck and also doesn't conflict with the Books as board breakers.

The goal of the deck is to get access to either Statue or Checkker in order to get Dark Golem and push for game. We want our board to have some insulation before we get to this stage which is not hard since our starters can alternativley be used to get to to protection and also board break at the same time.

Wyvern can get Statue to Special Summon or Fortress for protection (or if you choose to play Box and Convex you can get them for a Rank 4 play: e.g. Giant Hand for an on field monster negate).

Subspace Battle (for Carnot and Jizukiru x2) and Shaddoll Fusion (using Genius, Ruinforce and Blue Traveler) will break boards with either a Kaiju or Genius' negate and will also set up a Rank 10 play: either Flying Launcher to search for Statue/Checkker, or Gustav Rocket for a monster negate.

Cyber Jormungardr will set up for a Rank 5 play: either River Stormer to search for Statue/Checkker, or Cyber Dragon Infinity for an omni negate and the removal of an opponent's monster.

We play over 40 cards to avoid drawing the bricks. We have enough starters and board breakers that we are likely to draw enough to play through the opponent's board.

If you want you could remove Commander and Duel from the main deck (so that you have two less bricks) and always just go for Chaos Giant in the initial game; but if you do so you must retain them in the side deck as Duel-amped Ultimate Golem will be better than Chaos Giant in many scenarios and matchups.
Advanced format version of Dark Dragon Magic. Will be swapping out Called By in the sideboard for Dark Paladin - Wave Motion once it drops

deck_excerpt: ZEXAL, anime deck, crossover, Pokémon, Ash Ketchum, Xyz based,
deck_description:
For another Yu-Gi-Oh anime crossover story I'm working on, I plan to bring Ash Ketchum form Pokemon into the world of Yu-Gi-OH ZEXAL. In it, he adapts to Duel Monsters and helps Yuma and Astral track down the 99 Number Cards to not only restore Astral's memories, but also hopefully help Ash find his way back to his own world.

For Ash's deck, though I was originally thinking of one built around Beasts, Beast-Warriors, and/or Winged-Beasts, I found that original idea lacked means of adjusting monster levels, which is what happens in a LOT of Zexal Duels. So instead, I planned on having Ash start out with a simple, starter deck, where he can adjust his monsters levels to make Xyz summoning more convientent, and then upgrade that into a second deck that feels more mixed, but still has plenty of level-adjustments to maek his dueling style feel reactive, creative, unpredictable and so on. That, and if I limited Ash's monsters to a single archetype, attribute, or even monster type, then it just wouldn't feel right; as it would make Ash look like a guy who has favorites or preferecnes in Pokemon types. And if anything, I felt warriors were more simpler, yet also effective and strong in battle, and Dragons to help give our boy a bit of brute force, along with a few other options.

As you can see, I made Ash's first deck inspired by Yusei and Yuma's a bit in terms of monsters, primarily ones that I though would REALLY fit Ash's dueling style. Like Speed Warrior to gain a high ATK boost before charging forward, as Ash favors speed and aggression. Gagaga Magician to adjust its level to anything Ash needs. And so on. And since Ash is going to be Yuma's Number hunting partner, I think its only fair that he gets his share of the spoils. Primarily the Number monsters they win as time goes on. Here are the ones I've chosen to give Ash before the WDC arc and why:

-Number 17: Leviathan Dragon: This is basically Ash's Ace Number monster. Its not only simple and easy to learn for a beginner, but its special ability is effective, as detaching materials makes it stronger and allows it to hit harder. Being able to go from 2000 ATK to eventually 3000 ATK makes it a monster Ash would love using the most, as it makes him think of encouraging a Pokemon to dig deep and eventually help them find the will, courage, and spirit to stay in the fight.

-Number 83: Galaxy Queen: This one is meant to protect Ash's monsters from being destroyed and even dealing piercing damage, which are two things Ash will most certainly love. To him, it'd be like offering protection and support to one of his Pokemon.

-Number 61: Volcasaurus: This one not only fits Ash's style for explosive maneuvers, but its also a great solution for whenever his opponent brings out a REALLY tough threat with 3000 or more ATK points. Basically the literal "Fire powered finisher" of Ash's Number roster.

-Number 12: Crimson Shadow Armor Ninja: The fact that this monster can come back after being defeated is Ash's way of saying, "I'm down, but not out." That, and all while fittng Ash's warrior spirit of being straightforward and quick.

-Number 49: Fortune Tune: This one is meant to be a constant recovery card that always comes back, all while slowly restoring his life points little by little. Again, another way to display Ash's stubborn, never give up, persona.

 

-Number 96: Dark Mist: This number might look weak with only 100 ATK points. But once its uses up an overlay unit, it can half the opponent's monster while making it stronger. A perfect symbol of perseverance for Ash's deck showing his opponent that the longer his battle goes on, the stronger he gets. 

I included Fortune Tune as Fortuno's third Number card that Ash and Pikachu find and obtain before Kite.

And though the deck might not look completely like Ash's style, its not meant to. It's merely to act as a learning curve for Ash until he upgrades it for the WDC and builds it into something MUCH more befitting for him.

And if any of you are questioning why the main deck has Cost Down, I actually wanted to include one of the Yu-Gi-Oh anime's "anime only" cards into Ash's deck that isn't availible in the real-world card game. That card being the Spell "Decrease," which lowers the level of any one monster on Ash's Field by 2. Which can be handy in case he wants or needs to Xyz summon a lower ranked monster, his ace included. Couldn't upload this post until I had 40 cards in the main deck.

So, what do you all think? Let me know your thoughts in the comments below.

deck_name: Caster Slop Domain 6 (Branded, Dark Magician, Dracotail)
deck_description: these are way too fun to build lol

This deck is meant to be a combination of Ryan Yu's list and a mix of changes I made as the format developed. 3 upstart 2 desires was because bricking on 2 desires was common, and I felt that forbidden crown didn't win you matchups, only made matchups you were already winning easier. Other then that the main deck is pretty standard. Only change I would make it to swap hornet drones for a copy of droplet. While I do think hornet drones had its uses this event and it didn't feel bad to play, I wish it was droplet because of the 1 round I lost had it been droplet I would have been likely to win.

 

The interesting part of this deck is the side deck, thank you to Drew for lending me a pot of slot and some extra cards I forgot at home for this event. Nibiru is not very common in striker but I decided to play it specifically for the elfnote matchup, the matchup sucks and is almost unwinnable even with sphere mode if they can go off. However, nibiru turns off all their interaction if they don't have the trap, ty-phon was in the extra deck as a way to remove all monsters from the mmz if I use nibiru. The logic behind the 5 charmies is that the rolad piles win the game if they full combo so you just play the stuff that punishes them for it. I never felt a need for more copies of pot of sloth or evenly, while they would have been nice sky striker has a very limited pool of cards you can take out from the main deck so playing more going second cards is really hard.

deck_excerpt: Claim your birthright while denying your enemies their petty extra deck trics
deck_description:
Archetipical monarch deck, focused on generating advantage by consistently realizing tribute summons every turn, and using the extremely powerful monarch traps and spells to prevent your opponent from performing their gameplan

A stronger version of this deck would defnitely include Tessera the Primal Squire and possibly include Thestalos the Shadowfire Monarch, but that might raise the power level of this deck too much for the games I intend to use it on. And while Thestalos looks cool, Tessera I feel ust outclasses every single vassal and even the other squires, possibly making the deck just less interesting to pilot

A "old style" monarch deck should remove Eidos the Underworld Monarch, as it was released in 2025. It greatly increased the consistency and power level of the deck by allowing you to repeatedly tutor for the spells you need, as well as giving you more bodies. I would not recommend it, as without it the deck is somewhat inconsistent and has a huge problem going first (this version still has, but way less), being simply less fun to play even in a casual enviorment

Open for suggestions of decks and/or archetypes this deck could be paired up with in order to have interesting games in a casual enviorment

Gameplan

Shout outs to Jose Luis Sanchez Corderos for their top 8 list from the Lima Genesys Regional; seeing their list inspired me to run this list at all! Also thanks to LoganJYA over on YouTube for their dedicated Drytron content; thanks for getting me up to speed with my favourite space dragons again!

I love Drytron; bought the deck in paper on release, first list I built when Master Duel launched... Reignited my love of Ritual monsters. Thrilled to see people build around the heavily-pointed Alpha and Mu Beta Fafnir and still play well, so this was a crafting-light list to brew up. Following Jose's list, I ran Stardust Synchrons and a heavy Synchro lineup to make use of them... I didn't understand Bri Synchron other than making your monster 600 ATK bigger? But Drytron doesn't feel lacking for giant monsters to begin with. Running a small Metamorphosis package was pretty sweet; Thousand- and Millennium-Eyes Restricts are both quite strong, but I was an absolute bungler and dusted my MER when scrounging dust for the Mathematicians. :') This is also your notice that Blue-Eyes Alternative White Dragon is not in Master Duel?? This would be my preferred level 12 Metamorphosis target instead of Neo BEUD.

I could have also run 3x Mathematician, but I wanted to give Gadget Gamer a run from my initial attempt at brewing this deck; functionally Foolish Burial for your Drytrons. Sideboard also features Batosbuster and Magikey Unlocking for consistent access to a negate, though this didn't end up feeling necessary for this event. 

As thanks for reading, here's my Drytron effect mnemonic for aspiring star dragon players:
- Alpha Adds your Aces
- Beta Brings from Banish
- Delta Draws from Deck
- Gamma Grabs from Grave
- Zeta Searches 'ze Spell

deck_excerpt: Blue-Eyes as an engine to get The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate and fast enough to negate your opponent and have enough fire power to OTK.
deck_description:
Just a sick joke of a deck that I actually run on locals.

Strategy is simple, you want to take out The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate on first turn (if going first) and prepare your hand for next turn to summon as many Blue-Eyes beat sticks as possible.

Negations with The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate, Effect Veiler and help from Exxod Fires of Rage may stop your opponent plays as much as possible to leave an end board as weak as possible. Then in your turn, if The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate still lives, great, now you can try to get out your Blue-Eyes army and finish the job. 

Blue-Eyes serves as an engine to get The Unstoppable Exodia Incarnate through:

Sage with Eyes of Blue => Maiden of White => True Light => Wishes for Eyes of Blue => Destined Rivals (for negations) AND Priestess with Eyes of Blue to hand => Link Spirit with Eyes of Blue with Sage => Mausoleoum of White => Summon Priestess with Eyes of Blue => Target Priestess with Mausoleum, Priestess goes to Graveyard => Heart of the Blue-Eyes to hand with Blue-Eyes Jet Dragon => Mausoleum resolves, you send a Blue-Eyes White Dragon => With Heart of Blue-Eyes you get Ankh => Use Spirit with Eyes of Blue to summon Heart of Blue-Eyes to have a good 3000 ATK wall => Ankh to summon Unstoppable Exodia => Set Destined Rivals for negations when you summon your Blue-Eyes White Dragon with True Light next turn => Get Exxod for field destruction.

And you're set!

- One non-monster negation with Exodia
- One field negation with Destined Rivals as long as you are able to summon your Vanilla Blue-Eyes
- One chance to destroy all of your opponent's field with Exxod

Then you do your tipical Blue-Eyes shenanigans on your attacking turn and try to win.

I'M SURE THIS CAN BE DONE BETTER. But I still have to get there.

I have been climbing well with this, optimal for going First and Second. Packed with Quick-plays, so Plump are 99% well fed all the time and ready to ExNoir. Hence, chances of successfully bringing out an ExNoir are thru the roof.


Going first, the main objectives would be:
1. Either summoning Plump => ExNoir or ENoir with a Yeap ready for turn 2
2. Setting a Super Poly ready to disrupt

Going Second, you either:
1. Ending with the same end board as first turn
2. OTK with Happiness (when it hits, it HITS)

As for the Extra Deck:
Most of the time, you will only be using Plump, ExNoir, others are situational
The reason why Zeus is not in the Main Deck is because more often than not, it helps the opp more than it helps you. So i switched it for a Lyrilusc-Robin, with less self-harm but equally as disruptive (debatable). Of course the Fusions are there for SuperPoly. Try not to swap out any, cuz i find that those are the most optimal ones.

Side Deck options:
- Fonix: Great choice, it brings extra disruptions, but very inconsistent if you only run 1 MST, consider having 2-3 MST if you want to run Fonix.
- AA-Zeus: As i have said above, it often does more harm than good. But it remains a decent option.
- Forbidden Chalice: See them as budget Forbidden Crown/Droplet, just use them if you don't have enough FC/FD.
- Fuwalos: No need for explanation.
- Dimension Shifter: Sometimes can help you win on turn 0. I do suggest putting it in the main deck, swapping for Forbidden Droplet. However, this is at the cost of having 1 more monster card = less chances of accessing the main combo cuz we play around Quick-plays. Yeh but still, this card is BUSTED going second!

deck_description:
Once, a famous Star Wars villain said "all I'm surrounded by is fear and dead men!" 

Raye says the same thing about her ladder opponents, as she obliterates every strategy she comes across!

Sky Striker's unparalleled grindgame, draw power, spot removal and link toolbox is enough to readily defeat every meta deck this season like Kewl Tune, Mitsurugi, Dracotail, Branded and Radiant Typhoon Zoodiac! With Sky Striker at full power with all it's support and tools at it's disposal in Masterduel (and more indirect support coming out in the future), Raye can overcome every strategy despite being surrounded by the meta!

Raye is extremely resillient, adaptable and verstile, able to answer every handtrap and staple that ladder throws at you! Piloted properly, you can outmaneuver devastating cards like Mulcharmies, Maxx "C," Droll, Nibiru and Dimension Shifter! Established boards also get surgically picked apart with your well-timed handtraps and appropriately targeted Sky Striker quick-play spells! 

The favourable conditions of a meta like the absence of spell/trap negates and fragile mid-range boards gives Raye an incredible advantage. All that's left to do is to outgrind your opponent in a duel where Sky Striker's superior card advantage drowns out your opponent's cards! This leaves the outcome of the duel to the individual pilot's skill playing Sky Striker. Can you strike from the skies with the full power of a Sky Striker Ace? 

Remember - RAYE IS BAE! 1000 YEARS OF SKY STRIKER RAYE!

Greetings! In this deck, combination of Isolde and Telefon leads to victory with "Mikanko Kagura" card. Since Isolde utilizes Equip Spells, this deck fits naturally.

 

 

Glossary

  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Gameplan

1) With your Telefon arsenal, place 2 x Telefon on the field, which will cycle with each other. Here are your cards:

  • One for One / Foolish Burial
  • Machine Duplication / Dimension Dice / Dice Dungeon
  • Naganaki / Gamer / Convex

a) Alternatively, you can also use Schedule cards to unlock Telefon cycle. Here is the pattern...

  • Exceptional >>> Urgent = Babeldecker + Telefon >>> Ballista = Babeldecker + Telefon >>> Ballista finds Gear Box >>> Gear Box searches Convex
  • Use Exceptional in GY to send Ballista to GY and Special Summon Babeldecker >>> Special Summon Convex and set its Level to 10 >>> Flying Launcher = Convex + Babeldecker >>> Launcher finds Telefon

2) With 2 x Telefon and Linkuriboh/Launcher, you can make 2 x Virus, which will be used for Isolde. When Isolde is Link Summoned, don't add anything by accident. Then, send Broken+Cursed+Sparkles+Gearblade to GY, which enables you to place Armageddon. There, use Armageddon to send Monk to GY and add Gearblade+Broken to your hand...

  • If you haven't done so far, place 2 x Telefon to 4th and 5th MMZ from hereon, which will matter a lot during the following steps. Also, keep 4th MMZ for Monk in the future.

3) While building up Synchros with Telefon, do the following actions...

  • Armageddon + Telefon = Rose Maiden >>> Activate "Black Garden" >>> Plant at least three flowers
  • Maiden + Telefon = Dragonshell + Telefon = Ancient >>> Pop Garden >>> Add Prison
  • Sparkles >>> Place on top of Main Deck >>> Ancient + Telefon = Life >>> Draw Sparkles

4) Link Summon Selene with the help of Aleister and keep only 1 x Telefon at either 4th or 5th MMZ. After the revival of Monk via Selene, use Monk to summon Ferret and replace it with Doomdog + Gamer.

5) Link Summon Proxy with Selene + Doomdog. Thanks to Doomdog, you can search Linewalker. After the activation of Prison, you can use Rose Maiden to revive any Dragon Synchro you like, which unlocks Linewalker.

6) When you have placed Linewalker, find Uru and Normal Summon it thanks to Prison. This action allows you to set your opponent's LP to 3000. Next, Fusion Summon Geo Kraken via Proxy, where Linewalker + Uru will be used as materials.

7) When Geo Kraken is placed, search Ritual Sanctuary >>> Ohime >>> Kagura. Then, play Kagura and pop the flowers for the fatal blow. In case you weren't aware until now, costs used for this deck were actually the setup for Kagura. Here is how...

  • Three spells were used. They were Broken + Gearblade + Sparkles.
  • Monk >>> Discard one Spell >>> Broken

Big Branded doesn't want you to know this, but you can play Branded Despia without Branded Fusion, Fallen of Albaz, or Mirrorjade the Iceblade Dragon! This deck focuses on 2-card fusion combos with Despia monsters and Blazing Cartesia, the Virtuous.

Edit: Switched to a Tearlaments package to speed up the deck, help fusion summon, and recycle resources. Also, the Tearlaments monsters are dark attribute, so they can be used as fusion material to summon your Despia boss monsters.

Welcome! In this deck, you see two Warriors telling the tales of stars. Let's hear it!

 

 

Glossary

  • NS: Normal Summon
  • SS: Special Summon
  • MD: Main Deck
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Gameplan

1) Whether you make Isolde with two different Level Warriors or with 2 x Level 3 >>> Invoker + Goblindbergh, send Horn+Broken+Cursed+Gearblade to your GY and SS Armageddon. While getting Broken+Gearblade in your hand, you have two options to do as Armageddon...

  • If you have Brigandine in your hand, send Zephyros to GY. There, use Equip Spell and return it to hand with Zephyros to SS him.
  • If you don't have Brigandine in your hand, send Cloak/Boots to GY. Then, use them to find Brigandine and SS it.

2) Armageddon + Zephyros/Brigandine = Dugares >>> Dugares revives Armageddon >>> Armageddon sends Monk to GY

3) Isolde + Dugares = Aleister >>> Aleister + Armageddon = Selene >>> Selene revives Monk >>> Monk finds Blastfan >>> Blastfan finds Oracle >>> SS - Oracle

  • While doing this step, make sure that Selene#2 has three free arrows.
  • If you haven't noticed until now, these steps were done to make sure there are no Spells or Traps in Main Deck.

4) Selene#2 = Selene#1 + Monk + Oracle >>> Selene revives Monk >>> Monks finds Ferret >>> Ferret = Gallis + Meiru >>> Selene + Oracle = Zealantis

5) Use Zealantis to reset the board. Here, Gallis + Meiru are unlocked and you can reuse Blastfan to find Birdman.

6) With no Spells or Traps in your Main Deck, Gallis will be safe. Bounce Gallis with Birdman and place Gallis to burn your opponent. Repeat this step until your opponent is dead.

 

Tips and Tricks

While the usual Isolde generation can be seen in this guide, you can also do it with 2 x Level 3 thanks to Invoker. Here are all options you can do for Invoker:

  • SS - Terrortop + SS - Taketomborg
  • NS - Blossom >>> SS - Scorpio (MD) >>> SS - Lilizard (MD)

deck_description:
A custom version of Pegasus deck from Season 1 Duelist Kingdom. 

I've included cards that he either used in anime and manga or cards that I thought would make sense for him to have. 

And I've played tested the deck against the Kaiba and Yugi Duelist Kingdom decks I've made. Overall, it feels strong but not TOO strong or unbeatable.

deck_description:
So, I have been recently utilizing Telefon with Schedule cards like in this deck, where Flying Launcher grants you Telefon cycle access if not interrupted. I decided to revise this deck, which is also an introduction as to how to use Schedule cards and Flying Launcher. Let's get into it!

 

 

Glossary

  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone
  • EMZ: Extra Monster Zone
  • SS: Special Summon
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Guide

1) When you get Exceptional, find Urgent and SS a token to opposing side, which lets you play Urgent. When you play Urgent, SS - Soulpiercer + Babeldecker. Don't do anything with Babeldecker if asked. Then, Link Summon Ballista with these two as materials.

2) Trigger Ballista to find Gear Box. Same will be done for Soulpiercer to get Scales. After finding Gear Box, search Convex Knight.

3) Use Exceptional in GY to replace Ballista with Babeldecker. Here, Babeldecker can SS - Gear Box. Also, SS - Convex to make it Level 10 by targeting Babeldecker and send Telefon to GY with Convex.

4) XYZ Summon Flying Launcher with Babeldecker + Convex as materials and search Telefon. Here, you will have two Normal Summons ready to be used.

5) Use first Normal Summon for Telefon, granted by Launcher. With infinite Telefon cycle, start making Clockwork Knight and Gear Box + Telefon = Librarian#1. When Gear Box is in GY, use Clockwork to get rid of Launcher and revive it. Then, empty your EMZ by Link Summoning S:P with Clockwork + Telefon as materials and target S:P herself. You can place Librarian#2 at EMZ with Gear Box + Telefon as materials.

6) If you have done everything correct so far, these should be 3 x MMZ free. You can use second Normal Summon Scales, which lets you SS - Soulpiercer afterwards. Thanks to infinite Telefon cycle, this lets you place Librarian#3 with Scales/Soulpiercer + Telefon as materials and you can start building up Synchros from the remaining Level 4 Superheavy monster and Telefon.

7) Each Synchro Summon will net you three cards thanks to 3 x Librarian present. You may draw your whole deck and setup your endboard.

 

Gameplan

1) Use Rose Maiden to revive Dragonshell and Synchro Summon Rose Dragon with Maiden + Telefon as materials. After clearing the board with Rose Dragon, place Emperor + Kendo to Pendulum Zones and activate "Light Barrier".

2) Pendulum Summon Telefon + Shaman + World and choose Heads for World via Barrier to skip your opponent's turn at the cost of sending two of your monsters to GY, which shouldn't be a problem thanks to Telefon cycle. Pop Barrier with Emperor and activate Resort. Also, set Destiny Board. Then, end your turn to skip your opponent's turn via World and don't forget to use Resort to not deck out...

  • While using Resort, don't shuffle Telefon at all by accident.

3) When it's your turn, activate "Destiny Board". Also, Normal Summon Qardan to set and activate Sentence of Doom. You can place letters with Sentence and bounce Qardan back to hand with Shaman. End your turn to skip your opponent's turn via World and use Resort to not deck out.

4) Repeat what was explained in #3 until you win the duel with Destiny Board!

 

If you wonder how to save up some SR and UR points, I can show you:

- "Convex Knight" + "Ravenous" can be found within "Legacy Pack" to save 30 SR and 30 UR!

- "Exceptional Schedule" + "Urgent Schedule" + "Flying Launcher" can be found within "Dreadnought Advance" Secret Pack to save 150 SR!

- "Ancient Gear Ballista" can be found within "Gargantuan Gears" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "The World" + "Light Barrier" can be found within "Hand of Fate" Secret Pack to save 30 SR and 30 UR!

- "Archfiend Emperor" can be found within "The Cost of Dark Powers" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Duelist Genesis" can be found within "Evoked Dragon of Miracles" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "SPYRAL Resort" can be found within "Secret Fighters" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "Destiny Board" can be found within "The Trap in the Wicked Castle" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "Storm-Bane Dragon Destorbim" can be found within "Kaiser on the Stage" Timed Pack to save 30 SR!

- "Synchro Creed" + "Garden Rose Maiden" + "Black Rose Dragon" + "Kuibelt the Blade Dragon" can be found within "Radiant Inferno" Secret Pack to save 90 SR and 30 UR!

- "T.G. Hyper Librarian" can be found within "Futuristic Creatures" Secret Pack to save 90 UR!

- "S:P Little Knight" can be found within "Space-Time Transcendents" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

 

So, in total, you can save up to 450 SR and 240 UR, if you are willing to spend some gems. Other SR and UR cards I didn't mention are essential.

 

That's all for this one. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Have fun in Master Duel!
