deck_excerpt: Skip your opponent's turn - in style
deck_description:
Arcana Force, ft. Melodious

MELODIOUS COMBO (side engine used to get Vortex out):

  • Ostinato into Bacha (sending 2 Refrain)
  • Bacha eff summon third Refrain
  • Refrain eff add Couplet
  • Couplet eff on add to summon 1 Refrain from GY
  • Scale Couplet, and activate eff to add Concerto
  • Concerto to summon 2nd Bacha using Couplet and Refrain
  • Couplet & Refrain eff to scale themselves
  • Overlay both Bacha into Odd-Eyes Absolute
  • Link summon Cross-Sheep using Refrain & Absolute
  • Chain 1 Bacha, chain 2 Absolute, chain 3 Concerto
  • Concerto put to bottom of deck and draw 1, Absolute summons Odd-Eyes Vortex (onto Cross-Sheep arrow) and Bacha summons out a refrain
  • Cross-Sheep eff to summon refrain
  • Link Exceed the Pend using Cross-Sheep and both Refrain (you can alternatively XYZ a rank 4 monster using the 2 Refrain on board, or just summon S:P)
  • Exceed eff to add 1Refrain sent back to hand (you can then use Exceed eff to summon Refrain and link climb)

ARCANA FORCE COMBO:

  • Play Light Force, activate then discard eff to add 2 AF monsters to hand (Sun and Fiend)
  • Fiend eff, discarding to add Light Barrier, then activate Barrier
  • Special Sun, eff to set Reading, then activate it, adding Hierophant (alternatively if you Melodious combo'd, you can add The World and pen summon it!)
  • Normal Hierophant, eff to summon The World to opponent's side
  • Contact fuse Chaos Ruler using all AF monsters on board
  • Chaos Ruler eff to add Arcana Spread
  • Activate Spread and summon The World
  • The World eff to skip turn by sacking 2. You should have enough in your next turn to 'OTK' (or is it 2TK? or 1.5TK?)

It's vunerable to Droll and a hand full of handtraps, but it's stupid fun and very enjoyable to watch your opponent get very confused very quickly!

deck_description:
Hello there! In this deck, we will burn the opponent with Wonky. If you don't know how to utilize Telefon and Launcher, check this deck.

 

 

Glossary

  • EMZ: Extra Monster Zone
  • MD: Main Deck
  • ATK: Attack
  • DEF: Defense

 

Gameplan

1) At one point, shuffle back 5 x MD monsters with Pot of Avarice. When your MD is empty, XYZ Summon Trapeze to EMZ by using 2 x Librarian as materials. Then, activate Light Barrier besides Forbidden Lance targeting Trapeze.

2) Activate Dark Hole to clear all monsters. Fortunately, Trapeze will remain thanks to Lance. Next, place Emperor + Kendo to Pendulum Zones and Pendulum Summon Telefon + Yado + Level 4 + World in Attack Position. Here, choose Heads for World via Barrier to skip your opponent's turn at the cost of sending two of your monsters to GY, which shouldn't be a problem thanks to Telefon cycle.

3) Activate Burner to change the position of Yado from ATK to DEF position, which lets you shuffle remaining MD monsters from hand to MD with Yado for guaranteed Wonky action. So, you can XYZ Summon with Yado + Level 4 as materials to feed Wonky. Also, set Tornado.

4) With your setup done in #3, Wonky is guaranteed to stay at your side. Not to mention, burn effect is directed at your opponent thanks to Trapeze. End your turn with World to send 2 x Telefon to GY for turn skip.

5) Thanks to Burner being sent to GY in #3, you can fetch it to your hand to skip your draw. When it's your Main Phase, activate Burner on Telefon and use Tornado to fill your MD.

6) Repeat what was explained in #4 while using Burner from GY to not draw anything and Wonky feeding itself for constant burn via Trapeze.

deck_description:
Welcome! In this deck, we will use Fusion Gate to FTK the opponent while finding combo pieces naturally in a way that you feel you were playing in Fusion Gate event. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide! However, there are few differences from the original guide...

 

  • Ferret has to find Lilith + Raven + Brotaur, not Lilith + Lonefire. Therefore, Lonefire + Cattycorn are cut but we can find Fusion Gate with Proxy + Saurus altogether. Simply put, Link Summon Proxy F with Zealantis + Raven and start from there.
  • After Selene#1 and before Selene#2, Uppercutter + Sparrer = Dempsey >>> Renaud will do, in order to recover a Spell for Monk.
  • To form Zealantis, Selene + Renaud is your new equation. Selene + Uppercutter/Sparrer combination won't apply.
  • Rest of guide is same as before.

 

 

Glossary

  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone
  • GY: Graveyard
  • LP: Life Points

 

Gameplan

1) After placing Isolde and sending Horn+Sparkles+Cursed+Gearblade to GY besides placing Armageddon, you should get Broken+Gearblade to your hand. While making your path to Selene#1, you should do Monk >>> Uppercutter + Sparrer = Dempsey >>> Renaud play. Here, place Renaud and fetch any Equip Spell to your liking.

2) When Selene#2 = Selene#1 + Monk + Dempsey is present, place Monk to either 1st or 2nd MMZ and place Ferret. Then, Link Summon Saryuja with Selene + Renaud and use Ferret to place Brotaur + Raven + Lilith. Afterwards, replace Saryuja with Zealantis.

3) Reset the board with Zealantis. Here, use Brotaur and Lilith. Brotaur is here to find Gandora by discarding the Warrior you have drawn via Isolde and Lilith is here to find Chain Material. Besides, you can Link Summon Proxy F with Zealantis + Raven as materials.

4) Play Monk >>> Mark >>> Temple pattern, which lets you unlock Chain with Temple and you can Fusion Summon Saurus via Proxy F by using Brotaur + Kaitoptera as materials, in order to unlock Gate. While placing Gate via Saurus, you must Special Summon Kaitoptera.

5) Place Mudragon via Gate by using Proxy F + FIRE as materials. Here, you should have 4 x Level 4 materials for Alembertian to find Reversal Quiz. After placing Magellanica, you may Tribute Summon Gandora thanks to Saurus. Just use Alembertian + Magellanica.

6) Use Gate to place Contrast + Lacrima. There, use Contrast to negate Gandora and get Raven to your hand via Lacrima. Next, spam Gandora to halve your LP until your LP is less than 1200.

7) Place Sparkles on top of your deck by tributing Saurus and activate Reversal Quiz. Since you know the answer, opponent will have less than 1200 LP. Now, you may deal the fatal blow with Lacrima.

A 'Hot Potato' of a format where you definitely do not want to draw a Paracite!

I am limited by YgoProDeck's 60 card limit, but you can certainly play with any size deck. Top of the deck cards are good, piercing is good, shuffling/searching is interesting but can be time consuming. 

Format Rules:

- Play with ~20% of the deck being Parasite Paracide (10-12 in a 60% card deck)

- Play as if ALL Parasite's have already been flipped once and have been shuffled back into the deck. Keep them face down for ease of play

GX: Uria, Lord of Searing Flames, Hamon, Lord of Striking Thunder, e Raviel, Lord of Phantasms.

🛡️ Pilares do Arquétipo

Deck Overview: This is the ultimate, most dominant OTK (One Turn Kill) strategy available in Yu-Gi-Oh! GX Tag Force 1 (PSP), built strictly around the historical September 2006 Banlist format. It completely bypasses traditional slow-paced resource management by turning your entire deck into raw fuel for a game-ending strike.

Core Strategy & Combos:

  • The Future Overload Loop: The centerpiece of the deck relies on Future Fusion and Overload Fusion. By activating Future Fusion, you can declare Chimeratech Overdragon and instantly dump every single Machine monster from your deck into the Graveyard. Immediately follow up with Overload Fusion to banish them all, summoning a monstrous Chimeratech Overdragon with an attack power ranging from 8,000 to over 16,000 ATK, capable of wiping out the opponent's entire board and life points in a single turn.

  • The Backup Protocol (Cyber-Stein): If you don't open with your fusion spells, Cyber-Stein acts as a lethal alternate win condition. Pay 5,000 Life Points to drop Cyber Twin Dragon or Cyber End Dragon directly from the Extra Deck, equip Megamorph (which doubles your ATK since you have fewer Life Points), and secure the match instantly.

  • Board Clearing: Before executing your combo, the deck runs maximum backrow-clearing utilities like Heavy Storm, Giant Trunade, and Mystical Space Typhoon to ensure your opponent's Mirror Force or Sakuretsu Armor won't stop the lethal push.

deck_description:
DISCLAIMER : I use AI for formatting only; deck idea is written by me. I will rewrite this as I play more.

Toon Striker — Midrange OTK Deck Guide

 

PLAYSTYLE

This is a Midrange OTK deck that builds strong half-boards on Turn 1 and closes games with powerful follow-up on subsequent turns. The Toon engine provides consistency and resilience, while the Sky Striker package supplies draw power, board-breaking tools, and flexible Extra Deck access.

Going second, the deck excels at clearing established boards with Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons and multiple board breakers, pushing for lethal damage, and setting up disruptions if you cannot OTK.

 

STARTERS (16 ONE-CARD STARTERS)

This deck runs 16 one-card starters, giving you an exact 91.4% probability of opening at least one starter in a 5-card hand:

• Toon Table of Contents (3)

• Toon Bookmark (2)

• Toon World the Perfect World (3)

• Funny Dark Rabbit (3)

• Comic Cat (2)

• Rainbow Bridge Bifrost (2)

• Terraforming (1)

 

CORE CARD RATIOS

Monster:

• Evil Box (1) — Sets Toon Terror from deck; can be flickered for an extra attack during OTKs.

• Funny Dark Rabbit (3) — Starter.

• Dark-Eyes Illusionist Faceless Mage (1) — Places Mind Scan face-up.

• Comic Cat (2) — Starter.

• Droll & Lock Bird (2) — Oppressive floodgate handtrap that wins games.

• 0x Raye / Roze — Omitted because this deck uses the Striker package strictly as an engine via Linkage and Hornet Drones for draw power and board breaking; you will summon Amatsu with Linkage using Zero.

Spell:

• Toon Table of Contents (3) — Starter.

• Toon Bookmark (2) — Starter.

• Toon World the Perfect World (3) — Starter; dodges Impermanence-like handtraps and resets Funny Dark Rabbit against Ash.

• Rainbow Bridge Bifrost (2) — Starter; banishes Legatia and Chaos Angel.

• Terraforming (1) — Starter.

• Sky Striker Mobilize - Engage! (3) — Draw engine; loops with Linkage and Hornet Drones for card advantage.

• Sky Striker Mobilize - Linkage! (3) — Finds Engage; locks you into Sky Striker cards — be mindful of sequencing.

• Sky Striker Mecha - Hornet Drones (1) — Finds Engage to start the Striker loop.

• Sky Striker Mecha - Widow Anchor (1) — Primary Engage payoff; one copy is sufficient in testing.

• The Fallen & The Virtuous (3) — Utility going both first and second, allows for grind game with Albion reset.

• Spatial Trunade (3) — Board-breaking; can also return your own Funny Dark Rabbit and Toon World for reuse and punishes turn 0 plays from opponent.

• Forbidden Droplet (3) — Board-breaking + good going 1st.

• Triple Tactics Talent (1) — Dual utility going 1st and 2nd: going 1st rips a card, going 2nd you can draw into board breakers or take a monster.

• Sky Striker Special Maneuver - Lemnisgate! (1) — Going 1st endboard and recursion.

 

Trap:

• Mind Scan (1) — Reveals the opponent's hand to improve your interruption sequencing; can function as a soft floodgate against cards that require revealing; name-call omni-negate.

• Toon Terror (1) — Omni-negate; set directly from deck via Evil Box.

 

EXTRA DECK BREAKDOWN

• Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons (1) — Primary board-clear and OTK tool; destroys opponent's cards by targeting your own protected cards for additional pops.

• Chaos Angel (2) — Dual utility — serves as a Rainbow Bridge Bifrost target and as a Synchro target of Evil Box + Funny Dark Rabbit.

• Albion the Branded Dragon (2) — The Fallen & The Virtuous target.

• Evilswarm Ophion (1) — Floodgate; summoned off Dark Rebellion to lock opponents out of Level 5+ Special Summons.

• Centur-Ion Legatia (1) — Rainbow Bridge Bifrost target.

• Prototype Sky Striker Ace - Amatsu (1) — Endboard piece; summoned off Sky Striker Ace - Zero.

• Sky Striker Ace - Camellia (1) — Bridges into Sky Striker cards.

• Sky Striker Ace - Kagari (1) — Re-add used Engage.

• Sky Striker Ace - Kaina (1) — Link target to fill up Lemnisgate requirement.

• Sky Striker Ace - Zero (1) — Linkage target; searches Engage for Linkage.

• Swickelavee the Brilliantly Crowned Heavy Cavalry (1) — Summon on a used Comic Cat for an additional 2000 damage.

• Divine Arsenal AA-ZEUS - Sky Thunder (1) — Board wipe; overlay onto any Xyz that battled, if you cannot kill the opponent.

• Super Starslayer TY-PHON - Sky Crisis (1) — For last resort plays.

 

GAME PLAN

 

Going First:

The standard endboard consists of:

• Comic Cat — Non-targeting tribute (Monster effect)

• Evil Box — 2× shuffle (Monster effect)

• Toon Terror — Omni-negate (Counter Trap)

• Mind Scan — Information advantage and omni-negate (Continuous Trap)

Alternative: Summon Evilswarm Ophion in place of Comic Cat to floodgate Level 5+ Special Summons instead.

If you have Striker cards, you can add Lemnisgate and Amatsu for a double non-targeting bounce and 2000+ ATK monster negate.

 

Going Second:

The deck shifts into board-breaking mode:

• Use Spatial Trunade and Forbidden Droplet to dismantle the opponent's board.

• Chain Toon Table of Contents searches to load 3+ spells into the GY, enabling Engage to draw additional cards.

• Clear remaining threats with Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons and push for lethal.

• If you cannot OTK, you can set up a full endboard to try to OTK again.

 

STRENGTHS & WEAKNESSES

 

Strengths:

• Handtrap resilience — Toon World the Perfect World dodges Impermanence-like handtraps and can reset Funny Dark Rabbit when hit by Ash Blossom. The deck plays through most disruption cleanly.

• Mind Scan — Reveals the opponent's hand, allowing you to sequence your interruptions optimally. Functions as a soft floodgate against decks that require revealing to activate an effect.

• Dark Rebellion OTKs — Clears established boards and enables lethal pushes; can also transition into Ophion to floodgate the opponent.

• 16 one-card starters — Extremely consistent opening hands.

• Follow-up — If the opponent breaks your board but doesn't OTK, the deck has enough resources to rebuild and threaten lethal on the following turn.

• Layered endboard — Toon Terror, Mind Scan, and Lemnisgate are Spell/Trap-based disruptions so it is hard for board breakers to hit both.

• Immune to Dark Ruler No More and Forbidden Droplet — You can flicker the monster to dodge/remove the negate.

 

Weaknesses:

• Anti-Search Effect (like Droll & Lock Bird) — The deck searches extensively; Anti-Search Effects are devastating. Prioritize getting Evil Box first if holding 2+ Toon cards to generate plays under Droll.

• FTKs — Limited interaction going second against decks that can kill before your first turn.

• Unaffected monsters — This deck has no innate outs to towers.

• Sphere Mode / Gordian Slicer — Tributes and bounces remove Toon World or your Toon monsters, turning off both Toon Terror and Mind Scan.

 

TIPS & TRICKS

• Linkage locks you into Sky Striker cards which will lock you out of Dark Rebellion Xyz Dragon, Four Heavenly Dragons. However, it is correct to Linkage first so you can find board breakers to win; you can OTK without Dark Rebellion.

• Swickelavee + Comic Cat — Summon Swickelavee onto a used Comic Cat for an extra 2000 damage. Relevant for reaching lethal thresholds.

• Flicker Evil Box — Flickering Evil Box grants an additional attack. Keep this in mind when calculating OTK damage.

• Evil Box + Funny Dark Rabbit = Chaos Angel — Rarely comes up but useful if you need a banish to win the game.

• Dark Rebellion pop targets — Use your own cards to fuel Dark Rebellion's destruction effect for additional board clears: a set Toon Terror (placed by Evil Box), Toon World (protected by Bookmark), or any Toon monster (target it, then flicker).

• Droll counterplay — If you have 2 or more Toon cards in hand, prioritize resolving Evil Box first. This allows you to have Evil Box + Toon Terror under Droll.

• Spatial Trunade can return your own Funny Dark Rabbit and Toon World to hand, allowing you to reuse their effects.

• Opponent's Mulcharmy Fuwalos — Pure Toon lines give 0 draws to opponent's Fuwalos (no Extra Deck summons required), ending safely on Comic Cat + Evil Box + Mind Scan + Toon Terror.

 

MATCHUPS (Work in Progress)

vs. Rolad Pile — Favorable. Dark Rebellion clears their board, and Ophion shuts down the Rolad loop by preventing Level 5+ Special Summons. The combination of board-clearing and floodgate access gives this deck a strong edge in the matchup.

 

SIDE DECK (Under Revision)

• Artifact Lancea (3) — Forces combo decks (Toon, Elfnote, Rolad Pile) to commit to weaker half-boards you can break.

• Mulcharmy Fuwalos (3) — Same role as Lancea — disrupts opponent's combos and forces incomplete boards.

• Mulcharmy Purulia (3) — Draw into answers, for when Fuwalos doesn't give draws.

• Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring (3) — General-purpose handtrap for going first.

• Solemn Accusation (3) — Going-first option (placeholder — under testing).

Going 1st you can side out Spatial Trunade for Ash Blossom, Lancea, or Solemn Accusation.

Do not side out Toon Terror going 2nd.

Side out Mind Scan and Lemnisgate going 2nd.

 

FLEXIBLE SLOTS & CUSTOMIZATION

Board breakers: Forbidden Droplet, Spatial Trunade, and The Fallen & The Virtuous can be replaced for something else based on your meta.

Guide is actively being updated as testing continues.

deck_description:
Virus turbo + hand rip central it's soooo fun.

If you're using this on Master Duel, you 1000000% want to run at least 2 copies of Dimensional Barrier AND Maxx "C", it is criminal that neither of them are banned and you definitely want to be using them, or you'll intentionally be putting yourself at a disadvantage. Even though it puts you at 43 cards it's worth it, trust me.

Feel free to swap Crimson Call for Soul Resonator or to just run them both if you don't mind 41 cards, I've been using soul without call for a bit now and find it to be quite bricky and often finding soul at inconvenient times. Side out songs for charmies, do NOT run monster hand traps and songs in the same deck you will NOT have a good time. Also feel free to swap any side cards for hand traps of your liking, do keep in mind most staple monster hand traps have negative synergy with dominus cards as they lock you out of activating effects of specific monster attributes when activating from your hand, however, it is important to remember that you can still special summon cards like Incredible Ecclesia, the Virtuous even if you activated Dominus Impulse from your hand since it's not considered an activated ability. This is extremelyyyy important as she is a level 4 tuner and one of the only two tuners in the deck, allowing you to synchro her with either lady for a level 12, Arianna for a level 8 or any furniture piece for a level 5, 6, or 7 respectively.

The extra deck is free for you to change to your liking, the only important cards there are Muckraker From the Underworld, Chaos Angel, and maybe Rahamu, Envoy of the Sacred Tome though she only fits the extremely niche scenario of you drawing both Lovely Labrynth of the Silver Castle and a way to easily get two bodies on the board. Note that normal summoning Fallen of the White Dragon does not lock you into fusions and synchros and still allows you to special summon ecclesia.

YES, this deck doesn't run either Ariane or Arias. With a deck as frail as Labrynth, often losing the game on the spot to a single well timed Ash and a bad hand, Ariane and Arias provide unnecessary points of interaction that raise more risk than the level of reward I'd like. Feel free to run them if you'd like. If you're extremely lucky Arias can pull off some disgusting plays like a turn 0 virus if you top deck her, Lady and any virus.

All of the fusion monsters are Dogmatika Punishment targets all fit to niche scenarios, feel free to drop them if you drop punishment, though remember to include some sort of way to save either lady on the off-chance that the opponent manages to banish them, either in your main deck or extra deck.

Fallen of the White Dragon synchros into The Crimson King then searches Crimson Gaia (or Vision Resonator) to search for either Arianna the Labrynth Servant or whatever piece of furniture you're missing that works with whatever hand you have at the moment (Labrynth Stovie Torbie is often the best all-rounder).


Some niche scenarios off the top of my head that are good to have at the back of your mind:

LOVELY IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS DECK. KEEP HER AS SAFE AS POSSIBLE. 

If you have either welcome labrynth trap set and plan on summoning Lady Labrynth of the Silver Castle and know the opponent does not have Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring in their hand, you almost always want to summon Arianna the Labrynth Servant instead, THEN search Lady via Arianna's on summon effect, then SS Lady from the hand. Sure this drops lady down in defense but that barely matters as it opens you up to a few very strong lines:
- You can link into Muckraker From the Underworld to discard and reborn either Lovely or the same Lady that you just used to make Muckraker. Note that Muckraker TARGETS for cost, not discards, meaning you don't discard if the effect is negated. Unfortunately this does not activate Labrynth Cooclock's reborn effect but there's rare cases where you already have Lovely on the field.
- Make any link 2 (remember that Welcome Labrynth locks you into fiend monsters for 2 turns if you just used it)
- If ecclesia, vision or Labrynth Chandraglier are on the field, you can make whatever matching synchro you want with them, or a rank 4 xyz, or Chaos Angel using Chandragalier + either Lovely or Lady.  

Labrynth Labyrinth is suuper strong here as it allows you to instantly reborn whatever card you tributed for any virus card within the same chain and allows Welcome Lab to pop a card and trigger Lovely's pop effect. While it is strong and I prefer to keep it in, it isn't mandatory and can be ditched.

When going first, if you top deck both Labrynth Cooclock and another piece of furniture and you didn't draw Arianna the Labrynth Servant, activate Cooclock's ability from the hand first then activate the furniture's effect from the hand 2nd or in a new chain, this allows Cooclock to SS ITSELF TO THE FIELD (do NOT add it to the hand) and use itself as the required "Labrynth" monster on the field to activate the Big Welcome Labrynth that you set with the other furniture. You almost always want to SS Lovely Labrynth of the Silver Castle via this line and recycle big welcome from the gy via her effect.

While it is rare to summon RDA via Crimson King's effect, if it manages to survive until your battle phase you've basically won the game. It isnt extremely important though, feel free to ditch it for something else.

Omega is there to give you another hand rip in the event that you top deck both Walbaz and any way to get into Labrynth lines, this often leads to you getting 3 hand rips before your opponent gets to their first main phase.

If you're going second and top deck both a furniture piece and Songs of the Dominators, you're able to chain your furniture piece to songs and discard another trap to apply the second effect, allowing you to search your deck for another dominus card (usually Impulse). However songs can be ash'd even if you don't have a trap in your gy, heartbreaking stuff.

If you're using this on Master Duel and manage to get both Lady and set either Welcome Lab trap on turn 1, do NOT activate it until the opponent uses their first card and reveals what deck they're playing. When they do, you want to activate the set trap, chain Lady to it and set D-Barrier. It's super toxic, I know, but it's what you have to do to survive when using rogue decks. If the set card was:
- Welcome Lab: SS Arianna, then search Cooclock, then activate Cooclock's effect from hand, then activate D-Barrier and ban whatever ED type their deck focuses on.
- Big Welcome Lab: You can either SS Arianna and bounce either another monster you don't need to be on the field (or bounce Lady and SS herself from the hand) and follow the same line as Welcome Lab, or you can SS Cooclock and bounce itself, OR if you manage to reborn Cooclock prior to this you can SS Lovely to bounce Cooclock and get a free pop.
^ This is rare but usually an instant win against decks like KT, Elfnote, and any deck that heavily relies on the ED to get an end board that doesn't fall over to a stiff breeze.   

This was me intentionally trying to keep this brief and I'm already over 1400 words... lol. As you can probably tell, I LOVE this deck and would love to talk more in-depth about it.

First of all, if you're still here, thank you! If you'd like to ask questions, chat about the deck or are just looking for some advice on it (or if you have some advice for me!) feel free to hit me up on discord! @mankanshoku (same as my username here).
If you would like to add me on Master Duel and see the deck in action, my ID is 021-418-829. More times than not I will be using Labrynth if you see me in a duel and want to spectate. (Yes, I do sit around plat-diamond, I am too lazy to submit myself to the rng hell master rank grind.)

deck_description:
Greetings! This deck was made as a tribute to Jeff Leonard, who won with Exodia utilizing Isolde in a clever way. Here, you can see a different take. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide!

 

 

Gameplan

1) Find the following combo pieces with these cards:

  • Mark >>> Temple
  • Lilith >>> Chain Material
  • Catty >>> Fusion Gate

2) Activate these three, so that "Fusion Gate" can also use your Main Deck. Meanwhile, Link Summon Singularity with Zealantis + Monk/Mark + Cattycorn as materials and place Idaten via Gate by using Dynasty + War Chief as materials. Use Idaten to discard your hand in a way that you would have only one card in your hand.

3) Link Summon Selene with Singularity + Idaten + Monk/Mark as materials, then revive Monk/Mark with her. Next, place Gaia by using Stratos + EARTH as materials...

  • You don't have to strictly use Gaia. You can use any Elemental HERO Fusions to your liking in "Side Deck". Since they are SR to craft, it would be wiser to use what you have.

4) Link Summon Darkfluid with Selene + Monk/Mark + Gaia as materials. Then, count how many cards you have in your Main Deck. Similar to this deck, here are your equations which leads to your victory...

  • If Clock Wyvern was in your hand, (Main Deck - 28) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.
  • If Clock Wyvern was in your deck, (Main Deck - 29) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.

5) So, let's assume Main Deck has 33 cards and Wyvern was in Main Deck. After Wake Up is present, that means you should have 29 x Main Deck cards. So, you have to banish 4 x Warriors from your Main Deck but there is a catch due to UI of Master Duel...

  • First, pick Gaia.
  • Second, don't pick anything from Main Deck. Only hand or GY.
  • Third, count only 4 x Warriors from Main Deck and don't pick anything extra.

6) After the revision of Main Deck amount, Fusion Summon Cyberse Clock Dragon via Gate by picking up Wyvern first and all Links at last. If you have done everything correct in #4 and #5, Clock Dragon should empty your whole Main Deck. Afterwards, use Keldo+Mudora to shuffle back Exodia pieces into Main Deck...

  • Whether you have milled your deck via Clock Dragon or used Idaten in #2, what matters the most is getting rid of Keldo+Mudora+Cross+Rollback+3 x Housekeeping cards.

7) Finally, place Gaia again by using Wake Up + EARTH as materials. With what you have done in #2 and #6, Cross and Rollback+Housekeeping can be activated to draw all pieces of Exodia for the victory!

deck_excerpt: New Daedalus support with Primite, they both like normal monsters.
deck_description:
The new Daedalus support is in arm's reach so I made this deck where it's mixed with Primite. 

Cards like Fish Sonar are now much stronger since they can search any card that mentions umi, which is now every main deck monster in the new archetype since they treat themselves as umi. Fish Sonar also gives you a free normal monster upon use. And other cards like Kairyu-Shin's Dark Reef can now be used to not only fill your board with up to 5 cards in one trap, but also instantly activate Ocean Dragon Lord - Kairyu-Shin's floodgate effect by summoning it as well as any monster that treats itself as umi. And all those monsters will act as more link material, which is what this deck is trying to get anyway.

Primite cards are added in so your normal monsters will have more value than just those two cards, so it can all work together better.

To bridge the gap between Daedalus and Primite, I've found Cartorhyn the Hidden Gem of the Seafront, who is essentially the glue that holds these two archetypes together. It gives you a free extra normal summon for an earth or water monster, then can special summon itself after if you have an earth monster and a water monster on field, which will give you more material for link summons. As far as I could find, this was the most fitting deck for it since most other decks that use it are just earth or just water, this one lets it shine. It's like it was made for this.

Frostosaurus can be switched out for Neo Aqua Madoor if you want a better defensive wall to work with primite cards like Primite Lordly Lode that only summon in defence mode. Or if you want both attack and defence you can use Gogiga Gagagigo but he's unable to be summoned by Fish Sonar or by Kairyu-Shin's Dark Reef. Just pick whichever works best for you. Attack, Defence, or a balance that's a bit harder to summon.

2 Fieldspell since you can hit it in combo if you are in a dire spot with the banish effect of the Power Patrons

2 Vidolium since you cant really go through him more than once in a combo anyways and there are other search targets if drawn

Super Poly suite and Chaos Angle can be used instead of the W:P and Access code one in the extra deck 

 

Generall strategy:

Deck plays very non-linear depending on your hand

One of the best opener if you have follow up  is to use any spell/trap and Nervedo to get to Non-finito and set the trap, this gives you handtrap protection (from monsters) that can hardly be interacted with (veiler and imperm) since it sets

Usually you want to go through the power patron part of the deck first since the Artmage fieldspell locks you out of certain lines (primary the pendulum stuff)

Endboards should always contain at least: Varudras, Non-Finito, the trap, some sort of artmage setup ( either Diactorus, or Finmel and litera on board)

Briding isnt really necessary since Nervedo is both an artmage and a power patron, medius can go into both lines depending on your needs

Generally dont shy away from summoning Medius without the extra normal of the fieldspell since you hardly ever need the normal summon in this deck anyways

My version plays breakers in the main deck to compensate for the lack of handtraps and Pot of sloth

With the fieldspell you can turn any spell/trap into an artmage body so drawing them going first in the first game isnt the end of the world and going 2nd first game is insane with drnm into evenly.

Side Decking:

Going first after siding gives you a couple of options: I usually keep PBS/FNV since it can be used as an interuption on the opponents turn; i side out -3xfuwa -3xdrnm -3xevenly and add +called by +triple tactics talent +2xdroll +both solems +ddg +2xthrust

Except for droll, the same reasoning as for evenly and drnm applies, turn any unwanted cards into artmages even though your going first tools tend to be too good to pass up on

If you can get into a reasonable combo + DDG or Solemns you usually win the game instantly since hardly any deck can play through a omni negate ( and 1 onboard omni, and 1 monster omni) and a floodgate/solemn

Going 2nd you can side out pendulum treasure for sphere mode and if you feel like you need ash in the matchup, side out Shade the obscure, the 2nd copy of Jupredo and the Power patron field spell

The deck has a lot of power but is quite hard to play correctly since the power patrons enable so manny lines

The deck profits quite hard from knowledge about your opponents deck: If you know its a breaker deck, play way more greedy and dont go for Non-Finito handtrap isulation, If your opponent is on handtraps, abuse Non-Finito and talents and thrust to win

deck_excerpt: Live life on the edge, and protect the weak
deck_description:
Join the Domain Format discord server for information on rules and deckbuilding: https://discord.gg/jGkRCJkt3d

Myriaday Dragon is a monster that can reach 10,000 ATK if you and an opponent have a life point difference of 10,000 life points. Instead of doing the reasonable thing and building this as a life gain deck, I've done the opposite! Using Transaction Rollback, you can pay half your life points and go to 4000, and copy the effect of Hatsugai, which lets us pay 3000 more life points, and if an opponent agrees to it, they gain 3000 life points. So in total, we would go down to 1000 LP, while that opponent would be at 11000 LP, which is a difference of 10,000! 

But this isn't a boring OTK deck. I have built the deck to play very low to the ground and defensive, using Bystials, Blue-Eyes and Primite to gather card advantage and have some small interruptions. The goal is to protect the weakest players in the duel, and stop the strongest players from taking over the game. We will save up our interactions to protect other players, using cards like Terrors of the Afterroot and Gigantic Thundercross that can stop the strongest player's plays, or support the weak players to help them catch up! Then, using the Fiendsmith engine, we can summon Beatrice, Lady of the Eternal to mill Rollback and Hatsugai, allowing us to do our 10,000 ATK combo and take out our strongest opponent with one single attack! From there, we will fight fairly against the remaining players, hopefully keeping Myriaday Dragon on the field so we can kill another opponent on our next turn, and hopefully win the game from there.

Glossary

8) Use Reprodocus to change the Type of Dullahan to Winged Beast. This allows you to use Sanctuary, where you can feed Dullahan with Assembled.

deck_description:
Welcome! In this deck, we will use Fusion Gate to FTK the opponent while finding combo pieces naturally in a way that you feel you were playing in Fusion Gate event. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide! However, there are few differences from the original guide...

 

  • When Isolde sends Cursed to GY, find Burning rather than Broken.
  • After Selene#1, when Monk + Uppercutter + Sparrer are present, make Dempsey to find Renaud.
  • Rest of guide is quite similar.

 

 

Gameplan

1) When Isolde sends Cursed to GY, find Burning via Cursed. When Dempsey >>> Renaud is here, use Renaud to find Cursed. Then, play Burning >>> Cursed to skip your opponent's Main Phase 1 via Burning and bounce Burning via Cursed.

2) When Selene#2 is present, Cursed can fetch Broken. After Monk >>> Ferret = Lonefire + Lilith play, use Selene + Renaud = Zealantis and reset the board.

3) Find the following combo pieces with these cards...

  • Monk >>> Mark >>> Temple
  • Lonefire >>> Cattycorn >>> Fusion Gate
  • Lilith >>> Chain Material

4) Before activating combo pieces in #3, XYZ Summon Photon and search Queen's Light. After the activation of combo pieces, use Gate to place the following monsters with these as materials...

  • Shining = Photon + Stratos
  • Idaten = Chief + Dynasty
  • Gigant = Tune + Titano

5) Before placing Wake Up, count how many cards you have in your Main Deck. Here are your equations for the calculations...

  • If Clock Wyvern was in your hand, (Main Deck - 14) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.
  • If Clock Wyvern was in your deck, (Main Deck - 15) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.

6) So, let's assume Main Deck has 33 cards and Wyvern was in Main Deck. After Wake Up is present, that means you should have 15 x Main Deck cards. Therefore, you have to banish 18 x Warriors from your Main Deck but there is a catch due to UI of Master Duel...

  • First, pick Shining.
  • Second, don't pick anything from Main Deck. Only hand or GY.
  • Third, count only 18 x Warriors from Main Deck except A/D and don't pick anything extra.

7) After the revision of Main Deck amount, Fusion Summon Cyberse Clock Dragon via Gate by picking up Wyvern first and all Links at last. If you have done the calculations correct in #6, Clock Dragon should empty your whole Main Deck. Also, use Idaten to send combo pieces which were have drawn to GY except Queen's Light.

8) With five monsters present, apply Queen's Light on Gigant to make them all Level 12, which lets you XYZ Summon C1000 by using them as materials. Next, use Rollback+Reuse to place Vindictive as face-down. Then, use A/D to make Vindictive face-up. Since the effect of Vindictive is mandatory and C1000 is your only monster, it will be destroyed.

9) By destroying C1000, you can place IC1000. When you end your turn and it's the opponent's Standby Phase, use Rollback+Ruler to not have Battle Phase. According to rules of Yugioh, Main Phase 1 will be jumped to End Phase, if there is no Battle Phase.

10) Congratulations, you win the duel with IC1000!

HAVE FUN ^^

Highly versatile Zombie deck that has many ways to come back and scale down enemy boards.
It's been able to beat some Snake-Eyes, Yummi and Sky Striker decks, getting Top 3 in locals.

For first turn you may want to bring out Zombie World and Doomking Balerdroch or Skeletal Dragon Felgrand with a monster that can trigger an effect at will like Officiator of Doom Samuel, Red-Eyes Zombie Dragon Lord or Necroworld Banshee in the Graveyard. This can trigger Balerdroch's second effect and banish at will any monster from the opponent or Felgrand's negation effect.

 

 

# Safety mechanisms you want to have

For your opponent's turn you don't need much preparation to defend your board. It mostly centers on stopping their plays and if they destroy any of your pieces, no worries, as you can recover next turn pretty easily. You can expect to loose some LP at the end of your opponent's turn at the worst with really good decks:

 

- Alghoul Mazera ready on hand or graveyard for **destruction protection**.

- Vampire Fraulein on hand for **battle protection**.

- A way to suddenly special summon Stare of the Snake Hair (Red-Eyes Zombie Dragon Lord, Officiator of Doom Samuel, Call of the Haunted...) for effect **negation**.

- Doomking Balerdroch on field for effect **negation**.

- Yuki-Onna, the Absolute Zero Mayakashi can **negate** face-up monster effects and reduce their ATK to 0 after GY effects or special summons from the GY are activated/done.

- Officiator of Doom Samuel can revive a Zombie monster from the GY and **negate** the effects of a monster with less ATK.

- Skeletal Dragon Felgrand you can **negate** a monster's effects for a turn after a monster is revived from the GY.

 

 

# Board destruction

There's a bunch of ways to start tearing apart your opponent's board, many of these require targeting but they mostly banish. They also can target GY monsters:

 

- Doomking Balerdroch **banishes** as quick effect to any zombie activated effect.

- Vampire Sucker through Zombie World you can **Tribute Summon** any of your many +5 level monsters **using your opponent monsters**.

- A way to suddenly special summon Greal Mammoth of the Netherworld for card **destruction**.

- Vampire Fascinator can sacrifice herself or another Vampire to **take control of an opponent monster** for a turn.

- Dhampir Vampire Sheridan can **send a monster to the GY** and then revive it to your field.

- By Summoning Skeletal Dragon Felgrand you can **banish** a monster from your opponent's field or GY.

- Pumpking The Great Ghost King can remove a material to send 2 cards on field to hand.

 

 

# Generating resources on your hand or field

You have MANY options to get monsters to your hand or the field, which is necessary for Extra-Deck summoning:

 

- Vampire Fraulein can special summon herself during a battle step involving a zombie monster.

- If you Normal Summon Vampire Voivode, you can revive 2 of your opponent monsters to your field.

- Glow-up Bloom can give you a level 5+ zombie monster from your deck to your hand, and if you have Zombie World on the field, it can be special summoned.

- Alghoul Mazera can revive itself after an attempted destruction of one of your Zombie monsters. It banishes itself and then it revives. You can even banish it yourself for self revival with Changshi the Spiridao or Curse of the Ancient Turtle.

- Doomking Balerdroch just revives itself from GY in every Standby Phase (yours and your opponent's) if there's a field card face-up in any of the fields. Ready to protect.

- Vulcarrion the Rotting Phoenix is amazing for extending. As a first effect, if you have a zombie on field it can special summon itself. Being a Tuner, you can do some Synchro summons thanks to it. As a second effect, you can return it to hand from field and special summon any zombie from your hand.

- Mad Mauler can revive itself from GY if you reduce 2 levels from a face-up zombie monster with level 6+.

- Changshi the Spiridao can revive herself from banishment when sent there if you banish another zombie from grave.

- Gozuki, when sent to the grave, can summon a zombie from your hand if you banish another Zombie from your GY. There's a cool synergy with a GY Chanshi the Spiridao where Gozuki sends Changshi to banish and then Changshi can revive herself by banishing Gozuki or any other Zombie from grave.

- Hublot, Shadow of the Dark Directories, apart from being a level 6 that can normal summon himself without sacrificing, when summoned it can send a level 6+ zombie from the deck to the GY and then you CAN get any level 6+ zombie from the grave to your hand. This guy is amazing fro starting a combo with Pumpking the King of Grave Ghosts.

- Mezuki can banish itself to revive any zombie from grave. You can send him to grave with any of the "Foolish Burial" Zombies.

- Pumpking the King of Grave Ghosts can send itself from hand to GY to set and be able to activate a Call of The Haunted form Deck. Then use COTH to summon any monster from GY. You normally want to revive Pumpkin again to activate its second effect, where you can summon any level 6 zombie monster (not being 1950 ATK). Which then can be used to normally XYZ summon any of your great zombie XYZ monsters.

- Curse of The Ancient Turtle can banish any zombie from field or hand to send a Zombie from Deck to GY. This can trigger the effect of Changshi if banished netting you a good combo and almost 0 resources lost. Curse can also summon any 2000 DEF or less zombie monster from Deck if, being in the GY, a Zombie monster is destroyed.

- Monster Reborn, Premature Burial and Call of The Haunted revives a monster.

- There's a great and OG synergy with Premature Burial and Pumpking The Great Ghost King where you can use one of your 2 selected cards to send to hand to send Burial back to your hand to use it again. 

- Salamangreat Almiraj can be summoned by sacrificing Glow-up Bulb and activating its effect on grave.

- Vampire Sucker can revive an opponent monster on their side of the field and through her effect you can sacrifice zombie monsters from either side of the field for a Tribute summon.

- Dharc the Dark Charmer, Gloomy can revive a dark monster from the opponent's GY to your side of the field (to any of the positions he points to, actually)

- Vampire Fascinator, on summon, can revive an opponent's monster to your side of the field

- Officiator of Doom Samuel can revive any of your zombies at the cost of 1 material.

- Wollow, Founder of the Drudge Dragons can revive an opponent monster to your filed at the cost of 2 materials. (Or you can set a card from your opponent's GY)

- Dhampir Vampire Sheridan can revive an opponent monster to your field after a monster destruction. (Be mindful of Glow-Up Bloom's Zombie lock before hand)

- The Zombie Vampire can send the top 4 cards from each of the decks to the GY and revive any monster that was sent there.

- Immortal Dragon can revive itself from grave after one of your zombies is destroyed by battle.

- Red-Eyes Zombie Dragon Lord can revive one of your GY monsters as a Quick Effect during your opponent's turn.

- Flying Mary, The Wandering Ghost Ship can bring back a LV5+ Zombie from banishment or GY and destroy an opponent monster that has less attack than a selected Zombie in your field.

 

# Getting stuff to the GY.

MANY of your loops start by sending cards to the GY like Glow-up Bloom, Necroworld Banshee, Alghoul Mazera, Doomking Balerdroch, Mad Mauler, Eldlich The Golden Lord, Gozuki, Mezuki, Stare of the Snake Hair, Wandering Titan Of Tartarus, etc. Having shit in your graveyard is your fuel. So here's a list of IDEAL starting card so you can start your motor:

 

- Uni-Zombie

- Gozuki

- Curse of the Ancient Turtle

- Immortal Dragon

- Changshi the Spiridao

 

 

# OTKs

The main ways to OTK through this deck involve having a final board with Wollow, Founder of the Drudge Dragons, The Zombie Vampire, Doomking Balerdroch, and Red-Eyes Zombie Dragon Lord and Vampire Fascinator. In a couple of turns it's possible to arrive to a variation of this endboard. Thanks to the effect of Wollow, Founder of the Drudge Dragons, all monsters in your field gain 100 ATK for every card in your opponent's GY. This coupled with the effect of The Zombie Vampire which adds 4 more. Add to this the possibility of getting resources on your field thanks to The Zombie Vampire and Vampire Fascinator's effect and making more Extra Deck summons, it's more than feasible to end the duel in 2 or 3 of your turns.

 

# Main Combos

**Turn 1**

Zombie World on field thanks to dumping Banshee to GY and activating her effect.

 

Dump Glow-up to GY => Get Balerdroch to field

Dump Glow-up to GY => Get Pumpkin to hand or field and activate his effect.

 

 

Extras: Get any of your *Safety mechanisms* ready through any means you can

 

**Turn 2+**

 

Get access to Pumpkin to hand => Activate Pumpkin, dump Pumpkin and use Call of the Haunted to revive Pumpkin => Pumpkin searches and summons Changshi => Changshi dumps Mad Mauler to GY => XYZ summon Samuel => Use Samuel's effect to dump Changshi to GY and revive here => Activate Mauler's effect to revive and drop 2 levels from Changshi => Synchro summon Immortal Dragon => Sump Gozuki to GY and activate it's effect banishing Changshi to summon a zombie from hand => Changshi can banish Gozuki, Mauler or any other zombie from grave to revive herself => Do whatever you want with Changshi and the newly special summoned Zombie from hand and Immortal Dragon.

 

From Changshi / Immortal Dragon => you can also send Eldlich to grave and dump your Call of the Haunted from field to GY to special summon him with 1000 extra ATK points.

 

From Changshi / Immortal Dragon => you can also send Mezuki to GY and revive any zombie you need.

 

If you have spare monsters already you can Link summon Dharc, revive a Dark opponent monster and summon Fascinator

 

From Fascinator you can revive an opponent monster => Link Summon Yuki-Onna 

 

From Fascinator => If you already have a LV8 zombie you can XYZ that and the revived monster to summon The Zombie Vampire => activate effect and dump 4 cards from each deck and revive one of the candidates (Here maybe you can trigger a GY effect already) => With the extra body you can attack or extend more summons.

 

 

# Conclusion

This is a deck with many branching options and easy access to many kinds of effects to deal with a lot of situations. 

Through testing I've seen bricking possibility is kinda low, so it's great as rogue deck material in tournaments.

Anyways. HAVE FUN!

 

 

# Alternate cards to use in the deck (look at Side Deck and Watchlist)

 

- By summoning Vampire Scarlet Scourge you can special summon from GY any Vampire monster (Vampire Voivode, Vampire Fraulein, Vampire Sucker, Vampire Fascinator or The Zombie Vampire) ------- In the end, after much testing, I concluded having 2 Changshis was a better combo extender than having just one, and I never found myself looking for Scarlet actively.

- Wandering Titan of Tartarus through its first effect, if you send it to the graveyard from the Deck, you can, at the cost of your own field cards, **send as many of your opponent cards to the GY**. This is mostly as a last resort, but the possibility is there. ----- It's been moved to Side Deck to deal with BIG hard to break boards and force the opponent to reset their plays. Normally you don't want to do this, but if you have knowledge of big bottle necks to deal with big unbreakable synergies, add it on 2nd game of match and manage.

With M-X-Saber Invoker finally released from the purgatory of the ban list, the "black sheep" option from the Legendary Modern Decks once again has access to one of its best cards, giving it even greater access to the possibly the best piece of legacy support it could have ever asked for in X-Saber Pellina. The problem: outside of the other phenomenal legacy support card in X-Saber Bruno, the Deck lacks an easy or consistent way in archtype of getting two Level 3's on the field to make Invoker. Enter the Assault Mode cards, which like X-Sabers received some incredible support earlier this year but also failed to make any real impact on the game at large following the new cards' release. Despite this sad reality, the synergies between these two Synchro-centric archtypes is undeniable, and uninterupted, the Deck is able to produce end boards capable of dealing with pretty much anything your opponent might throw at you, including multiple Summon negates between Halberd Cannon, Axon Oracle, and Saber Hole; essentially infinite Spell negates from Naturia Beast, and pops/banishes off Psychic Blaster and Vengeance Dragan.

With that said, I'd like to highlight a few interesting techs that I've included that I think really help the Deck along.

  1. Scrap Warrior and Junk Signal
    1. Being easily accessible off a single activation of Duel Evolution-Assault Zone, Scrap Warrior provides the Deck a much need Level 3 body that doesn't take up the Normal Summon to make going into Invoker much easier. That alone would have made it an acceptable inclusion in the Deck, but the fact that it also searches Junk Signal, which can either give you access to additional body for synchro plays by tributing a spent Invoker, prevent your opponent from interupting your Synchro monsters' effects, or give your broad protection from destruction by Special Summoning back Stardust Dragon after it's been tributed for its Assault Mode counterpart, makes it more than worthy of its spot in the list.
  2. Small World
    1. This probably isn't too shocking, given that the card WAS included in the LMD, but I don't think I can stress enough just how well Small World works in this Deck. The fact that every monster in the list is some combination of Earth, Warrior, and/or Psychic without conflicting Levels or ATK/DEF stats means that basically everything in the list is searchable with just this one card.
  3. Serene Psychic Sorceress
    1. With fairly easy access to Level 6 Synchros, Serene Psychic Sorceress provides the Deck access to two powerful end board pieces in the form of Pyschic Blaster MK-II, ideally synching itself off with Bruno either on your turn or your opponent's with Bruno's effect, and Axon Kicker Oracle via Teleport Fusion.

Of course, as with every strategy, this Deck isn't without its issues. 

  1. Droll & Lock Bird/Ash Blossom and Joyous Spring/Mulcharmy Fuwalos/Nibiru
    1. So...yeah. This Deck NEEDS to be able to search cards, whether it's Assault Mode Activate, Saber Combination, or Scrap Synchron, which mean Droll and Ash can kill your turn pretty quickly. Likewise, given how much the Deck needs to summon to get to its desired end board, an untimely drop of Fuwalos or Nibiru will likewise stop you in your tracks.
  2. Zone Placement
    1. Like most Synchro strategies, this Deck can have a real problem keeping enough zones open to continue synchroing, which can severely hamper your potential end board if not managed properly.
      1. Helpful Suggestion: ALWAYS summone Invoker and Sorceress into the Extra Monster Zone, or they will 100% clog your board mid-combo.

Despite these downsides, the Deck can be quite fun to play and can provide a decent test of your ingenuity and resource management.

Note: I fully recognize that this particular build lacks any going second tools or handtraps in the Main Deck and therefore can't be considered "competitive". I've included what'd probably be the best choices to include should you be looking to make this Deck "meta-viable". As to what you should cut, I'd say your best choices would be two Garsem, two Faultroll, one Gottom's Second Call, one Combination, one Psi-Reflector, and Darksoul for whatever combination you'd like in the Main and Crimson Blader and Juraishin in the Extra.

I LOOOVE MACHINA!

Here's an Earth Machine deck I've been playing in Genesys recently. I'm still not too sure about the side deck but its what I've got and what I figured would be decent enough. As for the main deck its pretty standard with the inclusion of the Machina cards since I know quite a few decks don't run them and instead run non-engine which is fair but you know I love those guys and they're one of my favourite archetypes. Opting to play the trap in this one though that's one card that completely optional and you really don't gotta play at all. Again the rest is fairly standard with another inclusion of Double Wild which is a card I've found has been doing great things for me in this deck more often than not. A final thing I'd like to address is that yes we're playing only two Exceptional Schedule since you know... No link monsters in Genesys so turn one there's not really much you can do with that card besides maybe get some kinda starting play going if your hand is otherwise a brick. Doesn't happen very often so I've hoenstly considered cutting Exceptional Schedule entirely out of the deck for Genesys but yeah I mean sometimes it can get you like a rank 5 play going if you have a level 5 Infinitrack in hand and nothing else I guess. It can help for sure I've just found that opening Gearframe/Redeployment or even better Harvester/Heavy Forward is basically a 1 card starter to a full board. Now I need you to understand due to the fact there's no links in this format you will be left with ONE guy on board that does functionally nothing (that usually being River Stormer) so I opt to actually use the Road Roller for its materials so that AT LEAST it forces your opponent to put guys in defense if you go first until they remove it.

But yeah, that's it, if anyones got any tips or anything let me know.

deck_excerpt: Isolde Burn ft. Wonky + Fusion Gate
deck_description:
About a while ago, I made a deck to win with Wonky featuring Telefon. Here, you will see a different take. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide! However, there are few differences from the original guide...

 

 

  • Ferret will bring Lilith + Petit + Brotaur instead of Lilith + Lonefire. Therefore, Saryuja is needed in order to place all three monsters.
  • Rather than relying on Gusto for 3rd Monk usage, Petit can supply "Machine Angel Ritual" to let Monk discard it.
  • Rest of guide is quite similar.

Glossary

  • EMZ: Extra Monster Zone
  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone

 

Gameplan

1) When Saryuja and Ferret are present, place Lilith + Petit + Brotaur on the field and replace Saryuja with Zealantis. You may reset the board with Zealantis to unlock the abilities of Lilith + Petit + Brotaur.

2) Activate these trio to find the followings...

  • Lilith >>> Chain Material
  • Petit >>> Machine Angel Ritual
  • Brotaur >>> Petit >>> Discard Warrior drawn by Isolde >>> The Sun

3) After playing Monk >>> Mark >>> Temple combination, activate Chain Material and Link Summon Proxy F by using Petit + Brotaur as materials. There, Fusion Summon Saurus via Proxy F by using Kaitoptera + Brotaur/Saryuja as materials. Next, activate Saurus to place Gate to unleash the potential but don't bring Kaitoptera.

4) Fusion Summon following monsters via Gate...

  • Zealantis + Proxy + 2 x Time = 2 x Tomorrow >>> Trapeze into EMZ
  • 2 x Prisoner = Geo Kraken >>> Light Barrier
  • Kraken + Ferret = Berfomet >>> Send Bone to GY

5) If you have done everything correct so far, there should be one free MMZ for The Sun. So, activate Light Barrier and play The Sun >>> Arcana Reading >>> The World combo. Then, use Reading in GY to Normal Summon The World and pick the outcome as Heads to skip the opponent's turn by sending two of monsters you control to GY.

6) Special Summon Bone from GY by getting rid of Barrier. Then, end your turn to skip your opponent's turn with World but don't send Monk/World/Trapeze by accident. When it's your next turn, on Draw Phase, use Spirit Burner to not draw anything at all. You will always activate the ability of Burner henceforth.

7) Use Monk to discard Burner and place Cattycorn, which will search Delta. Use Delta to send Eldlich to GY and revive Eldlich by sending Delta to GY. You have to get Delta back to hand or you will lose access to Delta-Eldlich loop. Then, end your turn.

8) On next turn, use Monk to discard Burner and place Doriado. Activate Doriado to place four monsters on top of your deck and XYZ Summon Wonky with Monk+Doriado as materials. Thanks to Doriado, it's guaranteed Wonky will have 5 monsters as materials, which prevents him from switching sides. Normally, Wonky would pop itself. However, Trapeze prevents it from ever happening and as a bonus, the damage you would take is redirected back at your opponent.

9) Use Delta-Eldlich loop and send Temple to GY for Bone to revive Bone+Eldlich. Note that Burner will be used for Bone after this. Bone+Eldlich will be used for World while not drawing thanks to Burner and Wonky feeding itself during each of your Standby Phases besides burning your opponent.

10) Repeat step #9 until you win the game!

Deck Techs of import include Statue of Anguish Pattern and Kashtira Ogre. For Anguish pattern, our Ashtra traps and Angel Statue - Azurune trigger its effect for extra disrutpion it also can combine with our Ashtra traps to synchro summon since it's level 7! Gameplan

  • Lonefire >>> Cattycorn >>> Fusion Gate

2) Before activating combo pieces in #3, XYZ Summon Photon with Monk/Mark + Cattycorn and search Queen's Light. After the activation of combo pieces, use Gate to place the following monsters with these as materials...

  • Gigant = Avian + Lancep
  • Idaten = Chief + Dynasty
  • TDM = Monk/Mark + DM
  • Shining = Photon + Stratos

3) Before placing Wake Up, count how many cards you have in your Main Deck. Here are your equations for the calculations...

  • If Clock Wyvern was in your hand, (Main Deck - 14) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.
  • If Clock Wyvern was in your deck, (Main Deck - 15) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.

4) So, let's assume Main Deck has 30 cards and Wyvern wasn't in Main Deck. After Wake Up is present, that means you should have 14 x Main Deck cards. Therefore, you have to banish 16 x Warriors from your Main Deck but there is a catch due to UI of Master Duel...

  • First, pick Shining.
  • Second, don't pick anything from Main Deck. Only hand or GY.
  • Third, count only 18 x Warriors from Main Deck except A/D and don't pick anything extra.

5) After the revision of Main Deck amount, Fusion Summon Cyberse Clock Dragon via Gate by picking up Wyvern first and all Links at last. If you have done the calculations correct in #4, Clock Dragon should empty your whole Main Deck. Also, use Idaten to send combo pieces which were drawn to GY except Queen's Light.

deck_excerpt: Revolver's Return με New Support Borrel & Rokket
deck_description:
Design

With the exception of "Borrelcode Dragon" (which has more elements in common with Cyberse monsters rather than "Borrel" Dragon monsters), all "Borrel" monsters have a mechanical appearance, with gun barrels and revolver cylinders built into them, as well as having pieces of metal armor reminiscent of barrel shrouds. The "Borrel" Link Monsters are mostly colored red and dark gray, whereas the non-Link "Borrel" Monsters also have an additional coloring based on their summoning method. Additionally, parts of the names of the non-Link "Borrel" monsters are an abbreviation of their respective summoning method. In addition, each "Borrel" monster has a different wing color (except for the wingless "Borrelcode Dragon"): "Borreload Savage Dragon" and "Borreload Riot Dragon" share the same wing color as "Borreload Dragon", and "Borrelend Dragon" has the wings of multiple "Borrel" monsters.

Playing style

All "Rokket Dragon" monsters share the following two only once per turn effects:

  • When a Link Monster's effect is activated that targets this face-up card on the field (Quick Effect): You can destroy this card, then [...]
  • During the End Phase, if this card is in the GY because it was destroyed on the field by battle or card effect and sent there this turn: You can Special Summon 1 "Rokket" monster from your Deck, except [a card with the same name].

The most basic gameplan of the Deck is to use the "Borrel" (such as "Breechborrel Dragon") and other Link Monsters to target "Rokket" monsters the player controls, which in turn would activate their effects. The effects of Link-4 and higher "Borrel" monsters cannot be chained to, allowing the player to reliably trigger the effects of their "Rokket" monsters without mid-Chain interruptions from the opponent.

  • "Anesthrokket Dragon" renders a face-up monster unable to attack and negates their effects.
  • "Autorokket Dragon" sends a Spell/Trap on the field to the Graveyard.
  • "Exploderokket Dragon" inflicts 2000 damage to both players.
  • "Hollowrokket Dragon" excavates up to 6 cards from the top of your opponent's Deck and banish 1 excavated card, and then place the rest on top of the Deck in the same order.
  • "Magnarokket Dragon" sends a monster to the Graveyard.
  • "Metalrokket Dragon" destroys the opponent's cards in the same column.
  • "Shelrokket Dragon" destroys a monster in the same column, along with all monsters in its adjacent zones.
  • "Silverrokket Dragon" looks at the opponent's Extra Deck and banish 1 monster from it.

Supports from Structure Deck: Rokket Revolt solidifies the Deck's swarming capabilities and their gameplan, which is necessary to Summon their "Borrel" monsters. In particular, "Rokket Tracer" is now the focal point of the Deck, with its effect to Summon more "Rokket" monsters simply by destroying a face-up card the player controls. "Absorouter Dragon" can also Special Summon itself if there's a "Rokket" monster on the player's field, while also searching another "Rokket" when it's sent to the GY by any means. "Quadborrel Dragon" can also destroys a Link Monster on the field (including itself) to revive more "Rokket" monsters from the GY; it is especially powerful when used alongside "Dillingerous Dragon" (which can revive itself when a "Rokket" is Special Summoned to the player's field). "Striker Dragon" searches the all-important "Boot Sector Launch", while it can also recover "Rokket" monster from the GY to be Summoned via "Boot Sector Launch".

Rokket Dragon Link

Though the archetype is designed with the "fire and reload" mechanic (self-destruction effect) in mind, the archetype's ability to swarm DARK Dragon monsters means that the Deck is more optimally, and more popularly, played as a Dragon Link Deck, and is in general one of the most popular and efficient engines within Dragon Link Deck builds. In Dragon Link Decks, the "fire and reload" mechanic is entirely ignored in favor of swarming as many Dragon monsters as possible to perform consistent combos and fill the board with generic boss monsters and disruptions, using generic Dragon support such as the "Guardragon" Link Monsters to swarm the field even further.

With the release of "Bystial" archetype and new "Chaos" support, both of which features focus on DARK monsters and banish-oriented gameplay. Dragon Link Decks can effectively uses both themes to further support the playstyle. With the "Bystials" providing extra consistency boost by searching and/or summoning various easy-to-summon Dragon monsters as well as providing various form of interruption, whereas "Chaos" support aims to exploit both the banishment effect of the "Bystial" and the large number of DARK monsters to further boost the consistency.

deck_description:
Greetings! Long ago, I won by using Morphing Jar as Telefon. Here, you will see how to do it with Isolde. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide! However, there are few differences from the original guide...

 

 

  • You will only make 1 x Selene instead of usual 2-3 x Selene. Since Lonefire brought Catty and Saurus can do the same to fetch Gate, Ferret = Lilith + Level 3 can work instead.
  • Rest of guide is quite similar.

 

Glossary

  • ED: Extra Deck
  • BZ: Banish Zone
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Gameplan

1) When you place Isolde, fetch a Warrior such as Captain. After Selene and Monk >>> Ferret = Lilith + Level 3 play, Link Summon Saryuja#1 with Selene + Level 3 as materials and replace Saryuja#1 with Zealantis to reset the board. After reset, play "Monk >>> Mark >>> Temple" and "Lilith >>> Chain" setup.

2) After the activation of Temple + Chain, Link Summon Proxy F with Monk + Mark as materials. There, Fusion Summon Saurus with Kaitoptera + Giant Rex as materials. Next, use Saurus to place Gate onboard and revive Kaito + Rex with their abilities. Thanks to more monsters, you can Link Summon Singularity with Zealantis + Saurus + Kaito/Rex as materials.

3) Use Gate to place following monsters...

  • Idaten = Dynasty + War Chief >>> Find Cavalier >>> Idaten discards all but Captain + Cavalier
  • Absolute = Stratos + Dolphin/Fountain

4) Link Summon Saryuja#2 by using four monsters onboard. Then, before placing Wake Up, count how many cards you have in your Main Deck. Here are your equations for the calculations...

  • If Clock Wyvern was in your hand, (Main Deck - 27) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.
  • If Clock Wyvern was in your deck, (Main Deck - 28) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.

5) So, let's assume Main Deck has 35 cards and Wyvern was in Main Deck. After Wake Up is present, that means you should have 28 x Main Deck cards. Therefore, you have to banish 7 x Warriors from your Main Deck but there is a catch due to UI of Master Duel...

  • First, pick Absolute.
  • Second, don't pick anything from Main Deck. Only hand or GY.
  • Third, count only 7 x Warriors from Main Deck except Cross + Liquid and don't pick anything extra.

6) After the revision of Main Deck amount, Fusion Summon Cyberse Clock Dragon via Gate by picking up Wyvern first and all Links at last. If you have done the calculations correct in #5, Clock Dragon should empty your whole Main Deck. However, Deep-Seated will be shuffled back into Main Deck, which matters a lot down the line.

7) Place Dogma via Gate to shuffle Saryuja + Absolute from BZ into ED. Next, use Rollback + Jar of Avarice combination to shuffle Reload + Hooking + Reverse + All-Out + ED monster and draw 1.

8) Resummon Saryuja with four remaining monsters to draw 4 and shuffle 3. Keep Deep-Seated in hand and send Temple to GY with Eldich to revive him. Then, resummon Absolute via Gate by using Liquid + WATER as materials.

9) When Absolute is placed, Cross and Liquid will ask you to use their abilities. Simply put, use them both in a way that your Main Deck will be empty and Deep-Seated is discarded. Then, Deep-Seated will be the only card remaining in Main Deck.

10) Set all cards from #7 and end your turn. When it's your opponent's Draw Phase, activate these cards in the exact order as explained below:

  • Igknight Reload
  • Double Hooking >>> Discard Cavalier and revive Wattfox
  • Rollback + Give and Take >>> Revive Wanghu and target Eldlich
  • Reverse Reuse >>> MJ #2 as face-down and MJ as face-up
  • All-Out Attacks

11) So, here is what is going to happen...

  • In the first two actions, "Igknight Reload" has been activated to not let you draw any cards via MJ. Even though you couldn't reveal Pendulum Monster in your hand to shuffle it and draw cards due to "Double Hooking", game considers "Igknight Reload" as perfectly resolved.
  • As for the rest; Wanghu destroys Wattfox, which shuts down anything your opponent can try to break you, including hand-traps. Then, via All-Out Attacks, MJ #2 will flip face-up and you can start milling your opponent with MJ.

12) After everything is done in #10 and #11, rather than both players drawing 5 cards via MJ, only your opponent can thanks to "Igknight Reload". This step will go on until your opponent has nothing to draw and you win the game!

A pure Angelechy deck for people who blew their budget on a playset of Strategy Score and E4. 

Sample combo, requires 1 extra spell/trap in hand:

- Opposition, summon Senechal, place Destrier. Senechal summons Basion, Destrier adds Problem

- Activate Problem effect, discard ???, summon Enlisted (main monster zones for Senechal), place Bastion.

- Bastion place Shatranga, Shatranga effect add E4.

- OPTIONAL: Enlisted effect target Senechal to banish (return to Extra), it stays on your field because it didn't actually banish.

- Bastion+Enlisted = Synchro summon B2B.

- Set E4, pass.

- Standby, activate E4, summon Destrier, place Castellan, place Endgame Problem. Castellan trigger send Verdict.

- Still Standby, Endgame Problem draws 1.

----

Endboard's a bit funky, but B2B is a floodgate +2 interruptions from either recycling Veiler, or using Enlisted + Destrier to climb into Susanoo (guaranteed at least 1 E4 for the nontarget banish) and then Juraishin. Shatranga and Castellan are floodgates, Destrier burns, and there's enough backrow for Endgame Problem to banish an inherent summon. Verdict in grave can replace a floodgate if one gets outed; you can send the field spell if you've already banished an inherent summon. 

If you have Verdict or E4 in hand and don't have to toss it for Problem, then instead of using Problem to place Bastion, you can place Shatranga directly to add Verdict/E4, set both, then use E4 to Bastion > 2nd Shatranga on your opponent's turn. You get everything + Verdict negate or mass banish, and can cycle 2nd Shatranga into placing Castellan using Verdict's banish effect.

Thrust/Talent are consistent extenders/ceiling thanks to Opposition summoning Senechal for a mandatory trigger, or they can be disard fodder for Problem, or you can get handtrapped > Thrust for E4 > pass and at least not be completely screwed.

In theory you could be running a Dominus package and/or Harmonias, but those cost money. FTK package is in the side deck, but that strategy's completely married to resolving Witness, and you need multiple Synchro 8 packages with all their bricks to make it consistent, which in turn dilutes the crap out of any extenders you might want to run.

deck_name: Old Z-Arc in the Modern Era
deck_excerpt: Nostalgic Pendslop with a new coat of paint.
deck_description:
We have the new Pend stuff from MAMO, and Advanced being a bit of a cesspit RN means I may as well mess around and have some fun.  This deck looks to use the best of what we have in the new tools, while also using the best PendMagician stuff from the last decade to set up a durable board.  The most notable upgrades being Horoscope Sorcerer being another starter, vastly increased acces to Astrograph Sorcerer as well as its retrain, Astrograph 2 making easier access to Vortex Dragon so you no longer need to go into Absolue and then link it off, so you're much less vulnerable to Nib. Naturally Clear Wing and Starving Venom, and probably Supreme King Dark Rebellion will be immediatly replaced with their Heavenly Dragons retrains when we get them, but until they they're filler to get us to Z-Arc for the prior two, and a decent rank-4 if we brick going second for the latter.

One of its biggest weaknesses is the lack of playable high-Scales.  Pendulum Witch is something i'm experimenting with, but realistically I'm really coping on a Timegazer Magician retrain around the corner. Additionally, as with most decks this old, Droll eats me alive.

I'm well aware this isn't exactly going to tear up any regionals or anything, and I'm running some cards that have realistically been crept for quite some time, but it's good enough to break even at locals while playing some weird jank.  A lovely time.

Fun fun. The side deck can be whatever you want but in playtesting i've found that dragonrulers and dragonmaids actually meld pretty well with amorphage. Maids offer good tribute fodder, rulers can help make odd eyes absolute which you can link away to spheres to pull out vortex to use already expended amorphages to fuel its omninegate and pull whatever one you need out with spheres. Laundry is actually pretty clutch in the deck, milling 3 when 37/40 cards can be used in the gy in some capacity is actually pretty huge, and by extension we get to run nudyarl which has a quick effect to either just put something irrelevant back just to get it into the gy to go into lady's or actually function as disruption to spin something away from the opponents gy. Nurse is probably the weakest link as it does nothing by itself as an opening play but is such an amazing extender (as well as ernus, quick effect SS of a little maid to further lean into making plays on the opponents turn) that it's hard not to include her. Besides she helps round the attribute soread out, though since everything is a dragon attirbutes hardly matter. The attribute spread is a very nice 3/3/6/6/6/6 Light/Dark/Earth/Water/Fire/Wind respectively. Although, If I'm being honest, my first cuts for side boarding are always 2 hospitality, 2 tidying, and 2 changeover, and as far as the creatures go, are laundry and nudyarl, nurse and earnus, and 1 copy of chamber make for 13 total cards cut to swap in every single amorphage. As far as extra deck goes, the swaps are 1 sheou and 1 eclipse. Sometimes you might want to keep both copies of spirit since just linking to it and then going into spheres with some other expendible can put 1 more additional dragon body into the gy which can mean the difference between being able to go into disaster or not.

deck_excerpt: Isolde FTK ft. Lycoris + Fusion Gate
deck_description:
Greetings! In this deck, we will exchange with our opponent some burn. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide! However, there are few differences from the original guide...

 

 

  • You will only make 1 x Selene instead of usual 2-3 x Selene. Since Lonefire brought Catty and Saurus can do the same to fetch Gate, Ferret = Lilith + Level 3 can work instead.
  • Rest of guide is quite similar.

 

Glossary

  • ED: Extra Deck
  • BZ: Banish Zone
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Gameplan

1) After Selene and Monk >>> Ferret = Lilith + Level 3 play, Link Summon Saryuja#1 with Selene + Level 3 as materials and replace Saryuja#1 with Zealantis to reset the board. After reset, play "Monk >>> Mark >>> Temple" and "Lilith >>> Chain" setup.

2) After the activation of Temple + Chain, Link Summon Proxy F with Monk + Mark as materials. There, Fusion Summon Saurus with Kaitoptera + Giant Rex as materials. Next, use Saurus to place Gate onboard and revive Kaito + Rex with their abilities. Thanks to more monsters, you can Link Summon Singularity with Zealantis + Saurus + Kaito/Rex as materials.

3) Use Gate to place following monsters...

  • Idaten = Dynasty + War Chief >>> Find Kendo >>> Idaten discards all but Kendo
  • Gaia = Stratos + Ferret/Captain/Goblindbergh

4) Link Summon Saryuja#2 by using four monsters onboard. Then, before placing Wake Up, count how many cards you have in your Main Deck. Here are your equations for the calculations...

  • If Clock Wyvern was in your hand, (Main Deck - 27) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.
  • If Clock Wyvern was in your deck, (Main Deck - 28) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.

5) So, let's assume Main Deck has 33 cards and Wyvern was in Main Deck. After Wake Up is present, that means you should have 28 x Main Deck cards. Therefore, you have to banish 5 x Warriors from your Main Deck but there is a catch due to UI of Master Duel...

  • First, pick Gaia.
  • Second, don't pick anything from Main Deck. Only hand or GY.
  • Third, count only 5 x Warriors from Main Deck except Cross + Liquid + BLS and don't pick anything extra.

6) After the revision of Main Deck amount, Fusion Summon Cyberse Clock Dragon via Gate by picking up Wyvern first and all Links at last. If you have done the calculations correct in #5, Clock Dragon should empty your whole Main Deck. However, Deep-Seated will be shuffled back into Main Deck, which matters a lot down the line.

7) Place Dogma via Gate to shuffle Saryuja + Gaia from BZ into ED. Next, use Rollback + Jar of Avarice combination to shuffle BLS + ME-PSY-YA + Primal Seed + Nightmare + ED monster and draw 1.

8) Resummon Saryuja with four remaining monsters to draw 4 and shuffle 3. Next, place BLS with his ability to unlock Primal Seed loop. Then, resummon Gaia via Gate by using Liquid + Saryuja as materials.

9) When Gaia is placed, Cross and Liquid will ask you to use their abilities. Simply put, use them both in a way that your Main Deck will be empty and Deep-Seated is discarded. Thus, you have drawn everything from #7.

10) Activate ME-PSY-YA + Nightmare + Kendo. Meanwhile, use Snow as many times as possible but the aim is to clear Temple + Gate while banishing Primal Seed + Exchange + 3 x Lycoris + Nightmare + Light Stage. You can also banish Snow with BLS.

11) Retrieve cards which were listed in #10 from BZ via Primal Seed loop. Activate Nightmare + Light Stage while holding Primal Seed + Exchange + 3 x Lycoris. Then, Pendulum Summon 3 x Lycoris, which lets Kendo return to your hand.

13) Repeat what was explained in #12 until you win the game.
