deck_description:
The Secret Crane Princess Who Returns A Favor is a board breaker as a DM. The main combo is Constellar Tellarknights by using Tellarknight Constellar Caduceus with two level 4 monsters, but alternatively, the deck can use the Fiendsmith combo. The best starters are the White Forest cards, which end on the strongest boards. This deck could also be built focusing on Winged Beasts, but I found them a lot worse, so I only included a small package with Painful Choice.

One interesting tip is that you can use Ultimate Offering to break boards multiple times over the course of multiple turns (or in the same turn). You can set it with Knightmare Gryphon co-linked with Fiendsmith's Requiem. To send it to the graveyard, you can use Beatrice, Lady of the Eternal, or a Painful Choice search by Verre, the Maid of Endymion, and return it with Diabell, Queen of the White Forest.

 

Main Deck Alternatives:

Child's Play: Good if you plan to use Ultimate Offering multiple times.

Constellar Sombre

Skill Drain, Imperial Order: Floodgates to set with Knightmare Gryphon (searchable by Painful Choice). 

Pot of Avarice, Pot of Acquisitiveness

Double Summon: Any extra Normal Summon effect is another chance to combo or to break boards.

 

Extra Deck Alternatives:

Stellarknight Constellar Diamond

Silvera, Wolf Tamer of the White Forest 

Cyber Dragon Nova, Cyber Dragon Infinity

Constellar Pleiades: With Constellar Castor as material, it's a bounce + spell negate.

Eclipse Twins 

Number F0: Utopic Future Zexal: Good alternative to Number F0: Utopic Future + Number F0: Utopic Draco Future.

Selene, Queen of the Master Magicians 

 

You may want to cut Number 16: Shock Master, Simorgh, Bird of Sovereignty, Knightmare Gryphon. It's also possible to cut the Fiendsmith package, but I do not recommend it.

Hey everyone!

This is my budget version of Branded Genesys, without White Albaz and Synchro Ecclesia.

I built it mainly using 2 copies of the Structure Deck from the Chronicles product, which I originally bought to get Fallen and Virtuous for Advanced. I ended up buying a few extra copies of cards like Aluber, Black Albaz and Branded Opening, but most of the deck is played with only 2 copies of each card.

One less obvious tech I’ve been enjoying is using Keurse to Fusion Summon Albion and then revive it by tributing the Albion on the field. It works somewhat like a Bystial Lubellion, giving you another way to get value from Albion while setting up your board.

The deck is mainly built to be cheap and playable. It definitely struggles a bit against the current meta, but I’ve been getting some good games with it, especially if you don't want to invest too much into Branded Genesys right away.

Here’s the list I’ve been testing:

Magistus is a deck of Level 4 Spellcasters, while Vaalmonica can Pendulum Summon Level 4 monsters and has a Spellcaster.

The deck takes advantage of The Three Champions of Swordsoul, which can search any Level 4 Spellcaster with ATK = DEF, including both Selettrice Vaalmonica and Spenta Magistus.

The Vaalmonica bridge

Once you have Selettrice, Angello, and Dimono on the field and enough counters:

  1. Turn Dimono into Requiem and Special Summon Engraver.

  2. Attach the Requiem from the GY to Engraver.

  3. Make Magistus Chorozo using Selettrice and the Requiem in the Spell & Trap Zone.

  4. Synchro Summon The Three Champions of Swordsoul using Chorozo and Angello, and add Spenta.

From there, you can add Crowley and, using him and The Three Champions, make Fusion Zoroa. Use Spenta in the GY to equip Aiwass to Engraver, make Necroquip, and finish the Fiendsmith line.

You will be missing a body for Zebufera, so either you have to Pendulum Summon an extra monster (a Charmy or a Vaalmonica body), or find another way to provide the additional body.

The Magistus bridge

  1. You can add Zoroa with Spenta in hand.

  2. Normal Summon Zoroa.

  3. Use its effect to Special Summon Spenta, then Synchro Summon The Three Champions of Swordsoul using both monsters to add Selettrice.

  4. You can then use Spenta in the GY to equip Artemis to The Three Champions and add Crowley to finish the Magistus line.

For this bridge to work, you need to already have access to the Vaalmonica Pendulum scales. Vaalmonica doesn't have a one-card starter, so bridging into the deck is kind of complicated.

The Vaalmonica line is a little different because you don't have your Normal Summon available, so you have to Pendulum Summon Selettrice and use Invitare to Special Summon from the Deck (so you can't do the Fiendsmith line because of the lock).

Of course, if you have access to both engines, it's much better. You can use Spenta to add Zoroa, do the classic Vaalmonica line, and when you reach the point where you Pendulum Summon, you can also Pendulum Summon Zoroa so that you can continue both lines.

Is that deck meta-relevant? Absolutely not.

But is it a valid alternative to Vaalmonica Fiendsmith? Maybe.

I just added some non-engine cards that I like to finish the deck. I don't think they're optimal, so feel free to experiment with them as you like.

deck_excerpt: New year, new meta! Let's see what freebies we got this format!
deck_description:
Here's some free staples and tech for the September-October 2026 Genesys format. These cards cost 0 points and can be used in almost any deck. Check out more in my previous list here:

https://ygoprodeck.com/deck/genesys-format-free-staples-and-tech-september-2025-647344

This decklist also uses the Genesys points update for Beyond the Brave's initial release seen here:

https://yugiohblog.konami.com/2026/genesys/beyond-the-brave-initial-genesys-points/

The Ashtra archetype hasn't been released yet in the TCG, but it has been accounted for.

Side Deck Tech

Gravekeeper's Watcher is a hand trap that can negate and destroy an opponent's card that could make them discard a card when it resolves. In this format, Gravekeeper's Watcher is used to negate Ritual of Light and Darkness decks' Mind Shuffle and most of the Sacred Beast decks' searchers.

Quadogmatika Beast can revive any monster from your graveyard or banished zone by sending a monster with equal or greater attack from your extra deck or a Dogmatika monster from your deck to the graveyard. However, you cannot special summon from the extra deck until the end of the next turn after this card resolves. It provides recovery for decks that don't rely heavily on their extra deck. You can send Dogmatika Lawbringer from your deck to your graveyard to revive any monster with 2000 attack or less, then activate Lawbringer's graveyard effect to add Quadogmatika Beast from your graveyard to your hand.

Mutually Affured Destruction and The Eye of Truth are counters to any deck that must reveal cards in their hand to activate their effects, such as Blitzclique and Sacred Beasts. Unlike The Eye of Truth, Mutually Affured Destruction only lasts 1 turn, but it's less prone to spell and trap removal.

Dominus Spiral, Interrupted Kaiju Slumber, and Pair Bear Scare!! give players more access to monster removal. Pair Bear Scare!!, in particular, can create meta games of Chicken where each player must decide whether to remove the card from their decks or keep it for free non-targeting destruction.

Ryu-Ge Realm - Wyrm Winds is a budget version of Dimensional Fissure that banishes any monster that would be sent from the field to the graveyard during your opponent's turn. It gives you control over the field with fewer opportunities to accidentally banish your own monsters.

Fog King is a monster alternative to Mask of Restrict that prevents either player from tributing cards. Normal summon him to shut down Clown Crew decks. You can search for Fog King with Piri Reis Map.

Decisive Battle of Golgonda can protect your monsters from card effect or battle destruction by sending a fusion monster that mentions Fallen of Albaz from your extra deck to your graveyard. If you send Alba-Lenatus the Abyss Dragon, then you can protect your board and search for a Polymerization normal spell or a Fusion normal spell during the end phase.

Engine Tech

The Ashtra Engine

A small engine consisting of 2 Akasuna the Battle Ashtra, 1 Ashtra's Howl, and 1 Ashtraja Susanoo can provide more extension and disruption for trap-based decks. The general idea behind this engine is:

1. Akasuna can special summon himself from your hand by returning a set card you control back to your hand.

2. During your end phase, Akasuna can set Ashtra's Howl from your deck.

3. Ashtra's Howl can special summon itself as a level 1 tuner, then allows you to synchro summon on your opponent's turn.

Ashtra's Howl + Akasuna = Any level 9 synchro

You'd synchro summon Ashtraja Susanoo in this combo.

4. Because Ashtraja Susanoo was synchro summoned, you can banish traps from your graveyard, then banish that many cards on the field.

5. Activate Ashtraja Susanoo's end phase effect to recycle your Ashtra cards and potentially repeat this combo.

The Revolution Synchron Engine

Tuning + Revolution Synchron is a small engine any deck with level 4 monsters can add to make level 7 or 8 synchros. Tuning searches for Revolution Synchron. A Revolution Synchron in your hand can be used as material for a level 7 dragon synchro.

1 level 4 monster on your field + Revolution Synchron = A level 7 dragon synchro

Some of the best level 7 synchro dragons to summon are Black Rose Dragon, a board wipe, Ancient Fairy Dragon, an extender that can also destroy and search for field spells, and Clear Wing Synchro Dragon, which can negate level 5 or higher monster effects on the field. If you still control a level 7 dragon synchro, then, once per duel, you can special summon Revolution Synchron from your graveyard as a level 1 tuner to make a level 8 synchro. One of the best level 8 synchros to summon is Crystal Wing Synchro Dragon who can negate monster effects regardless of their level or location.

Ultimate Slayer Tech

The extra deck contains some monsters that work well with Ultimate Slayer. One card of note is Predaplant Chimerafflesia who has a similar, but more powerful graveyard effect to Alba-Lenatus the Abyss Dragon. During the standby phase of the next turn that it was sent to the graveyard, you can search for any Polymerization or Fusion spell including a quick-play spell like Super Polymerization.

deck_description:
Main Deck Monsters (12)

• 3x Maha Vailo — The premier scaling boss. Gains +500 ATK/DEF natively per equip card on top of the card's actual boosts.

• 3x Armed Samurai Ben Kei — The multi-strike boss. Gains an additional attack per battle phase for every single card equipped to him.

• 3x Cyber Dragon — Your ultimate going-second bait card. Clears the way, absorbs enemy targeting traps, and boosts United We Stand.

• 3x Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring — Your only main-deck defensive handtrap to stop the opponent from setting up a game-ending board on Turn 1.

 

The Bamboo Draw Engine (6)

• 3x Cursed Bamboo Sword — The core engine piece. Gives a minor stat boost but lets you search another "Bamboo" card when sent to the Graveyard or bounced to the hand.

• 3x Golden Bamboo Sword — The ultimate draw spell. If you control a Bamboo equip, you immediately draw 2 cards with zero restrictions.

 

Power & Protection Equip Spells (11)

• 3x Mage Power — Stacks exponentially. Grants +500 ATK/DEF for every Spell/Trap card you control. Always play this card last.

• 3x Power of the Guardians — Your life insurance. Builds counters every time a battle occurs (+500 ATK) and removes counters to prevent card destruction.

• 3x Moon Mirror Shield — The battle bypass. Ensures your equipped boss will automatically match the ATK/DEF of whatever it fights and beat it by exactly 100 points.

• 2x United We Stand — Grants an explosive +800 ATK/DEF for every monster you control. Perfect alongside Cyber Dragon.

 

Board Clearers & Search Support (9)

• 3x Giant Trunade — The deck's undisputed MVP. Bounces all Spells/Traps on the field to ensure a 100% safe battle phase while allowing you to replay your own Cursed Bamboo Sword for multiple draws.

• 2x Pot of Extravagance — Run at 2 copies to avoid clogging your hand. Banishes 6 random cards from your unused Extra Deck to draw 2 fresh cards instantly.

• 2x Twin Swords of Flashing Light - Tryce — Grants a double attack. Maha Vailo's passive effect completely cancels out this card's 500 ATK penalty.

• 1x Heavy Storm — Clears out the entire opponent backrow in one click if you need raw destruction over bouncing.

• 1x Reinforcement of the Army (ROTA) — Instantly searches Armed Samurai Ben Kei from your deck to your hand.

 

Backrow & Response Traps (2)

• 2x Royal Decree — Continuous protection. Flips face-up to permanently freeze all other trap cards on the field, letting you attack blindly without fear.

 

The "Ammunition" Extra Deck (15)

• 15x Any Random Monsters (Purely used as fuel to be banished by your Pot of Extravagance).

 

How the Turn-2 Winning Loop Works

1. Special Summon Cyber Dragon for free if your opponent controls a monster to bait out any face-down removal cards.

2. Equip Cursed Bamboo Sword to Cyber Dragon and activate Golden Bamboo Sword to draw 2 cards.

3. Activate Giant Trunade to clear the opponent's entire backrow. This also bounces your own Cursed Bamboo Sword back to your hand.

4. Re-equip Cursed Bamboo Sword and activate a second Golden Bamboo Sword if you drew into one. You have now thinned your deck by 4–6 cards without using your Normal Summon.

5. Normal Summon Maha Vailo or Ben Kei. Stack your Equip Spells one by one, saving Mage Power for last to maximise its exponential attack boost.

6. Swing for Game.

If you plan on testing this out against your friends, let me know:

 

The Side Deck

 

Anti-Going First / Survival (6 Cards)

• 3x Threatening Roar — The ultimate "turn-skipper". If your opponent makes you go first, set this and pass. Activate it the second they enter their Battle Phase. They cannot attack, completely wasting their turn and handing the momentum right back to you.

• 3x Solemn Judgment — Your emergency panic button. Pay half your life points to negate any spell, trap, or monster summon that threatens to destroy your hand or field before you can combo off.

 

Heavy Board Breakers (4 Cards)

• 2x Lava Golem — Tributes 2 of your opponent's most annoying, invincible monsters to summon a giant clunker to their side of the field. It completely bypasses card immunities, and your bosses equipped with Moon Mirror Shield can easily destroy it.

• 2x Dark Ruler No More — Completely blanks and negates the effects of every face-up monster your opponent controls for the turn. They cannot respond to this card with monster effects, leaving them totally defenceless.

 

Backrow & Floodgate Removal (5 Cards)

• 3x Cosmic Cyclone — Pay 1000 LP to permanently banish a problematic face-down trap or an annoying continuous floodgate (like Gravity Bind or Skill Drain) so they can't recover it from the graveyard.

• 2x Lightning Vortex — Discard 1 card to instantly destroy all face-up monsters your opponent controls—ideal for clearing out a massive wall of defenders before dropping your boss.

 

The Side Deck Swap Guide

Scenario A: You won Game 1, and your opponent forces you to go FIRST

Peeps will try to mess up your Turn-2 strategy by forcing you to take the first turn, leaving you unable to attack.

• 📥 Side IN: 3x Threatening Roar, 3x Solemn Judgment

• 📤 Side OUT: 3x Cyber Dragon, 2x Twin Swords of Flashing Light - Tryce, 1x Power of the Guardians

• The Strategy: Set a single trap (Threatening Roar or Solemn) and pass. When they try to push for an aggressive OTK on their turn, flip Threatening Roar to freeze them out. On Turn 3, it is effectively your "Turn 2" again, and you can safely drop Maha Vailo or Ben Kei to wipe them out.

 

Scenario B: Your opponent plays giant monsters or annoying negations

If they manage to set up a massive field of high-ATK monsters or annoying quick-effects.

• 📥 Side IN: 2x Lava Golem, 2x Dark Ruler No More

• 📤 Side OUT: 2x Royal Decree, 2x Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring

• The Strategy: Drop Dark Ruler No More to shut off all their monster effects so they cannot stop your spells. Alternatively, melt their two best monsters into a Lava Golem. Execute your turbo-draw loop, drop your boss, and let Moon Mirror Shield effortlessly crush their board.

 

Scenario C: Your opponent is playing a heavy Stall/Trap deck

If your opponent is hiding behind classic defensive walls, battle-faders, or endless face-down traps.

• 📥 Side IN: 3x Cosmic Cyclone, 2x Lightning Vortex

• 📤 Side OUT: 3x Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring, 2x Twin Swords of Flashing Light - Tryce

• The Strategy: Ash Blossom is weak against stall decks that don't search. Trade her for Cosmic Cyclone to snipe their hidden backrow threats alongside your Giant Trunades, and use Lightning Vortex to clear out annoying defensive walls before you attack.

deck_description:
The Monsters (16 Cards)

• 3x Dark Magician: Your ultimate boss monster and the primary target for your resurrection loops.

• 1x Dark Magician Girl: Pairs with your support cards and acts as a required material for The Dark Magicians Fusion.

• 3x Apprentice Illusion Magician: Discards itself or others to search for a Dark Magician, or discards mid-battle to give a Spellcaster a massive +2000 ATK/DEF boost.

• 2x Magician of Dark Illusion: Special Summons itself from your hand and revives a Dark Magician from your Graveyard whenever you activate a Spell/Trap on your opponent's turn.

• 3x Magicians' Souls: Sends Dark Magician directly from your deck to the Graveyard as a cost to Special Summon itself instantly.

• 3x Magician's Rod: Your primary searcher. Normal Summon it to instantly grab any Dark Magician Spell or Trap from your deck.

• 1x Timaeus the United Dragon: Discards a Spellcaster to Special Summon itself, then acts as a required material for The Dark Magicians the Dragon Knight Fusion.

 

The Spells (17 Cards)

• 3x Soul Servant: Stacks your deck, then banishes itself from the Graveyard to let you draw up to 3–4 cards at once based on the Magicians in your Graveyard.

• 1x Illusion of Chaos: You never summon this. You reveal it in your hand to search your deck for Magicians' Souls or Magician's Rod, guaranteeing a perfect opening turn.

• 1x Upstart Goblin: Gives your opponent 1000 LP to let you draw 1 card, effectively shrinking your deck to 40 cards for maximum consistency.

• 2x Dark Magical Circle: Looks at the top 3 cards of your deck when played. While on the field, whenever you summon Dark Magician, it lets you target and permanently banish one card your opponent controls.

• 2x Magician's Salvation: A Field Spell that automatically plays Eternal Soul straight from your deck to the field on Turn 1.

• 2x Dark Magic Expanded: Quick-Play protection that makes your Spells and Traps completely immune to destruction by your opponent's card effects for the turn.

• 2x Secrets of Dark Magic: A Quick-Play Fusion spell used to fuse Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl together during your opponent's turn to disrupt their plays.

• 2x Mystical Space Typhoon: Classic Quick-Play destruction to snipe annoying enemy backrow before making your plays.

• 1x Raigeki: Completely destroys all monsters on your opponent's side of the field.

• 1x Harpie's Feather Duster: Completely destroys all Spells and Traps on your opponent's side of the field.

 

The Traps (8 Cards)

• 3x Eternal Soul: The anchor of the deck. Once per turn (on either player's turn), it lets you Special Summon a Dark Magician from your Graveyard, and makes him completely immune to all card effects.

• 2x Magicians' Combination: Continuous Trap that lets you tribute a Dark Magician to negate any card effect, then instantly brings out a Dark Magician Girl from the Graveyard to replace him.

• 3x Solemn Judgment: Pays half your Life Points to completely negate absolutely any card or summon your opponent tries to play. Your ultimate safety net.

 

The Extra Deck (6 Cards)

• 3x Dark Magician the Dragon Knight: Fused using Dark Magician + Timaeus. While on the field, his name counts as "Dark Magician", so Eternal Soul makes him immune to all card effects. In return, he protects Eternal Soul from being destroyed, creating an unbreakable wall.

• 3x The Dark Magicians: Fused using Dark Magician + Dark Magician Girl. Lets you draw a card whenever anyone plays a Spell/Trap. If it dies, it splits open and instantly Special Summons both Dark Magician and Dark Magician Girl from your Graveyard back onto the field.

 

The Side Deck (15 Cards)

Swap these cards in between games to counter your friend's specific strategy.

• 3x Skill Drain: Continuous Trap that negates the effects of all face-up monsters. Because Dark Magician has no card effects, your 2500 ATK beatsticks remain fully functional while your opponent's strategy grinds to a halt.

• 2x Lava Golem: Tributes 2 of your opponent's monsters to summon itself onto their side of the field. Bypasses all protections and burns them for 1000 damage every turn.

• 1x Soul Drain: Stops monster effects from activating in the Graveyard or while banished. Devastating against decks that like to recycle dead cards.

• 2x Anti-Spell Fragrance: Forces both players to Set Spells for a turn before playing them. This leaves your face-up cards intact while letting your Dark Magical Circle banish their Spells before they can ever activate them.

• 2x Dark Bribe: Counter-Trap that negates any opponent's Spell or Trap card, but lets them draw 1 card. Extra protection to stop cards like Harpie's Feather Duster from hitting your Eternal Soul.

• 1x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell: Discard a Spell to negate an opponent's Spell. It completely forbids them from playing that specific Spell card for the rest of the duel.

• 1x Dark Hole: Wipes out all monsters on the board. Perfect for clearing the field when you are forced to go second.

• 3x Cosmic Cyclone: Pays 1000 Life Points to banish an opponent's Spell or Trap card, preventing them from destroying your backrow or triggering effects in the Graveyard.

 

Main Deck Strategies & Combos

1. The Core Engine: The Turn 1 Graveyard Setup

Your primary goal on Turn 1 is to get Dark Magician into the Graveyard and Eternal Soul onto the field.

• The "Chaos-Souls" Search: Reveal Illusion of Chaos in your hand → search your deck for Magicians' Souls → place 1 card from your hand back on top of your deck.

• The Dump: Activate Magicians' Souls → send Dark Magician straight from your deck to the Graveyard to Special Summon Souls to the field.

• The Trap Fetch: Activate the Field Spell Magician's Salvation → its effect automatically triggers to Set Eternal Soul directly from your deck to your field.

• The Result: You have successfully set up your infinite revival loop before your opponent even gets a turn.

2. The Banishing Disruption Loop

This is how you systematically dismantle your opponent’s board during their turn.

• Prerequisites: Dark Magical Circle face-up on the field, and a face-down Eternal Soul.

• Execution: During your opponent's Main Phase, flip Eternal Soul → Special Summon Dark Magician from your Graveyard.

• The Payoff: This triggers Dark Magical Circle, allowing you to target and permanently banish any card your opponent controls (monsters, spells, or traps) before they can use it. Because Eternal Soul can be used during either player's turn, you can repeat this every single turn.

3. The Unbreakable "Dragon Knight" Lock

This strategy secures an automatic win against most casual decks by completely protecting your backrow.

• Execution: Use Timaeus the United Dragon or Secrets of Dark Magic to fuse Dark Magician + Timaeus (or any Dragon) into Dark Magician the Dragon Knight.

• The Lock:

1. While on the field or in the Graveyard, Dragon Knight’s name is treated as "Dark Magician". Therefore, Eternal Soul makes him completely immune to all of your opponent's card effects.

2. In return, Dragon Knight’s effect states that your opponent cannot target or destroy your Spells and Traps.

3. The Result: Your opponent cannot destroy Eternal Soul, and Eternal Soul ensures your Dragon Knight cannot be touched. They must defeat a 3000 ATK monster by battle alone. If they somehow do, Eternal Soul just brings him right back next turn.

4. The Soul Servant Mega-Draw

This is your replacement for Pot of Greed, capable of drawing up to 4 cards at once.

• Execution: Once you have copies of Dark Magician, Dark Magician Girl, or The Dark Magicians spread across your field and Graveyard, activate Soul Servant's second effect by banishing it from your Graveyard.

• The Payoff: You instantly draw cards equal to the number of those specific names in play/Graveyard. It completely refills your hand mid-game to ensure you never run out of counter-strategies or Solemn Judgments.

Side Deck Strategies & Counters

The Side Deck is used between games to specifically counter whatever deck your friend is playing.

Scenario 1: Against Heavy Monster Decks (Blue-Eyes, Chaos, Beatdown)

If your friend plays massive monsters with high ATK or powerful on-field monster effects, you want to bring in your board-clearers and effect-negators.

• Cards to SWAP OUT (Remove from Main Deck):

• 1x Upstart Goblin (You don't want to give a beatdown deck extra Life Points)

• 2x Dark Magic Expanded (Raw battle protection is less useful when you can just negate or destroy their monsters instead)

• 2x Mystical Space Typhoon (Monster-heavy decks don't run enough backrow to justify these)

• Cards to SWAP IN (Add from Side Deck):

• 3x Skill Drain (Completely turns off their big monsters' effects, while your normal Dark Magician is untouched)

• 2x Lava Golem (Tributes their two biggest monsters away before they can even attack)

• The Tactical Goal: Reduce the duel to a pure battle of raw ATK points, where you hold all the advantages.

• How to Play It:

1. Drop the Golem: Use Lava Golem to tribute two of your opponent's most threatening boss monsters. This forces it onto their side of the field, completely bypassing any "cannot be destroyed/targeted" protections they might have.

2. Flip Skill Drain: Once your own Dark Magician or Dark Magician the Dragon Knight is on the field, flip Skill Drain.

3. The Beatdown: Because Dark Magician is a Normal Monster, he keeps his full 2500 ATK. Meanwhile, your opponent's monsters are reduced to useless vanilla bricks. Even the Lava Golem you gave them loses its effect, meaning it can no longer burn you for 1000 damage, leaving it as a sitting duck for you to banish with Dark Magical Circle.

 

Scenario 2: Against Spell-Heavy Decks (Fusion, Ritual, or Modern Spells)

If your friend relies heavily on Spells to summon their monsters (like Polymerization or Ritual Spells), you want to completely lock down their ability to play Spells.

• Cards to SWAP OUT (Remove from Main Deck):

• 1x Raigeki (Spell decks usually do their damage via Spells before summoning, making a slow monster-wipe less effective)

• 1x Magician of Dark Illusion (Trims the deck slightly to prioritize pure spell denial)

• 1x Upstart Goblin (Speeds up their deck by giving them breathing room; remove it to focus strictly on control)

• Cards to SWAP IN (Add from Side Deck):

• 2x Anti-Spell Fragrance (Forces them to set Spells and wait a turn, allowing your Dark Magical Circle to banish them first)

• 1x Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell (Negates a core Spell like Polymerization and bans them from using it for the rest of the game)

• The Tactical Goal: Slow the speed of their deck down to a crawl so your banishing loop can intercept their plays.

• How to Play It:

1. Set the Trap First: Activate Anti-Spell Fragrance as early as possible (ideally on your very first turn or right at the start of their Draw Phase).

2. The Banish Window: This forces your opponent to Set any Spell card face-down and wait an entire turn before they can activate it.

3. Execute: During their turn, use Eternal Soul to resurrect Dark Magician. This triggers Dark Magical Circle, allowing you to target and banish their face-down Polymerization or Ritual Spell before they ever get the chance to flip it up and use it.

4. The Ultimate Lock: If they do manage to activate a crucial Spell, chain Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell by discarding a Spell from your hand. Not only is their spell negated, but they are physically banned from activating any other copies of that specific card for the rest of the entire duel.

 

Scenario 3: Against Trap-Heavy or Defensive Decks (Control, Burn, Stall)

If your friend plays a lot of face-down Traps, Mirror Forces, or cards that try to destroy your Eternal Soul backrow, you need maximum protection and destruction.

• Cards to SWAP OUT (Remove from Main Deck):

• 1x Raigeki (Useless if they aren't summoning many monsters)

• 1x Apprentice Illusion Magician (You don't need the +2000 ATK boost if you aren't fighting big monsters in battle)

• 2x Magician of Dark Illusion (Too slow when you need instant backrow removal)

• Cards to SWAP IN (Add from Side Deck):

• 3x Cosmic Cyclone (Aggressively banishes their annoying Traps so they can't trigger them later)

• 1x Dark Hole (An extra safety net to clear whatever small defensive monsters they put up)

• The Tactical Goal: Blindside their defensive "Mirror Forces" or "Torrential Tributes" before they can punish your attacks.

• How to Play It:

1. Banish, Don't Destroy: When facing heavy backrow, use Cosmic Cyclone instead of Mystical Space Typhoon. Paying 1000 LP to banish a card completely prevents your opponent from retrieving it from the Graveyard or activating annoying "when this card is destroyed" effects.

2. Bait and Switch: If you suspect they have a battle trap set, do not summon your main monsters right away. Use Dark Hole first to force out any protective cards they might be holding.

3. The Safe Push: Once you have cleaned out their threats, safely summon Dark Magician and push for direct damage without the fear of running into a hidden trap.

 

Scenario 4: Against Graveyard-Reliant Decks (Zombies, Phoenix, Recyclers)

If your friend plays a deck where monsters constantly jump out of the Graveyard or trigger effects when they die, you want to freeze the Graveyard completely.

• Cards to SWAP OUT (Remove from Main Deck):

• 2x Dark Magic Expanded (Does nothing to stop Graveyard triggers)

• 1x Upstart Goblin (Gives them too much time to set up their Graveyard)

• Cards to SWAP IN (Add from Side Deck):

• 1x Soul Drain (Completely stops any monster effects from activating in the Graveyard)

• 2x Dark Bribe (Negates any spell or trap they try to use to revive their monsters)

 

• The Tactical Goal: Sever the link between their field and their Graveyard so their dead monsters stay dead.

• How to Play It:

1. Flip Soul Drain: Unlike Skill Drain (which affects the field), Soul Drain requires a 1000 LP payment to completely stop monster effects from activating in the Graveyard or while banished.

2. The Lockdown: Flip this the moment a monster hits their Graveyard. This completely paralyzes decks like Zombies or monsters that trigger "when this card is sent to the Graveyard" effects.

3. Protect the Lock: Use your Dark Bribe copies strictly to protect Soul Drain and Eternal Soul from being destroyed by cards like Harpie's Feather Duster. Your opponent gets to draw a card, but it won't matter because their entire Graveyard engine is completely frozen.

Glossary

  • MMZ: Main Monster Zone

Guide

1) Have 2 x Level 3 monsters onboard to place Gabonga. You can look as to how to do in "Openings" section. Then, find Dugg and place it onboard to search Grand Entrance.

2) Play Grand Entrance to search Mean and place it onboard. With another 2 x Level 3 monsters, which are Dugg + Mean, XYZ Summon Zenmaity#1 to EMZ. Here, detach Mean specifically to place Rat from hand or MD. Since Mean is in GY, you have to detach Dugg to revive Mean.

3) Use Rat + Mean to make Zenmaity#2. Detach whatever to place Magician#1 from hand or MD. After that, use Zenmaities to place Zenmaintenance to EMZ. Zenmaintenance can search a Spell for Monk usage, which is "Wind-Up Key".

4) After the usage of Zenmaintenance, Magician#1 can trigger. Accept it to place Magician#2 from MD and clear Magician#1 via Zenmaintenance to place Magician#3 onboard. This leads into triggering Magician#2 to place Shark#1 from MD. Finally, use Shark#1 to trigger Magician#3 and place Shark#2 from MD. Here is the summary in case you were lost...

  • Zenmaintenance >>> Magician#1 (U) + Magician#2 (A) >>> Zenmaintenance clears Magician#1 >>> Magician#2 (A) + Magician#3 (A) >>> Use Magician#2 >>> Shark#1 (A) + Magician#2 (U) + Magician#3 (A) >>> Use Shark#1 + Magician#3 >>> Shark#1 (U) + Magician#2 (U) + Magician#3 (U) + Shark#2 (A)

5) XYZ Summon Alembertian by using 3 x Level 4 to find Monk. Use Magician#2 + Magician#3 + Shark#2 as materials. Then, Link Summon Saryuja by using Zenmaintenance + Gabonga + Alembertian as materials. Depending on the setup, you can also use Shark#1 as material.

6) Special Summon Monk with Saryuja. Then, proceed according to "Gameplan" you have.

 

Gameplan

1) Before getting rid of Gabonga, don't forget to replace it with Fortress to get second Spell for Monk usage, which is "Unveiling Mail".

2) Use Monk to place Blastfan, which finds Birdman for you. Next, XYZ Summon Dugares with Monk + Blastfan as materials and use Dugares to revive Monk and use it again.

3) Place Ferret with Monk but make sure Saryuja has two free MMZ arrows. Use Ferret to place Doom + Gallis to where Saryuja points to. Then, replace Saryuja with Zealantis.

4) Reset the board with Zealantis to unlock Doom + Gallis. Thanks to Doom, Gallis and Birdman combination is an infinite loop. Place Gallis to burn your opponent and use Birdman to bounce Gallis and try again. Since Birdman is DARK monster, it can only bounce a monster as cost but it can't place itself as effect.

5) Repeat what was explained in #4 until the opponent is dead.

The Hand-Rip "Trinity" Package (3 Cards)

Going-Second Board Wipers & Punishers (6 Cards)

• 3x Triple Tactics Talent — If hand-trapped, look at their hand and rip another card, or draw 2.

 

The Hyper-Fast Spell Engine (9 Cards)

• 3x Toon Table of Contents — No once-per-turn limit. Searches any Toon card to thin your deck.

• 3x Toon Bookmark — Searches Toon Kingdom and banishes itself from the GY to protect it.

• 3x Toon Page-Flip — Quick-Play spell that reveals 3 Toons for an instant, random free summon.

 

The Castle & Finisher Spells (5 Cards)

• 2x Toon Kingdom — Gives your Toon monsters complete targeting and destruction immunity.

• 3x Shadow Toon — Deals effect damage equal to a target's ATK (3000 burn straight to the face on Lava Golem).

 

Hand Traps & Counter Negation (7 Cards)

• 2x Infinite Impermanence — High-impact monster negation from the hand.

Extra Deck (15 Cards)

Level 4 Metamorphosis Targets (Tribute Toon Mermaid or Toon Harpie Lady)

• 3x Dark Blade the Dragon Knight — Attacks directly under Toon Kingdom to banish 3 monsters from their GY [yugipedia.com].

 

Level 5 Metamorphosis Targets (Tribute Toon Cannon Soldier)

Side Deck (15 Cards)

The Fusion Tool (3 Cards)

Anti-Blowout & Floodgate Counters (6 Cards)

The Final Tactical Playbook: Core Combos

Turn-1: The Hand-Lock Castle (Going First)

Your objective is to exploit your high statistical chance (approx. 33.8%) of opening with a "Trinity" card to shred your opponent’s hand before they ever reach their Main Phase.

1. Deconstruct their Hand: Lead immediately with Delinquent Duo, Confiscation, or The Forceful Sentry before casting anything else. Stripping their hand traps (Ash Blossom) clears a safe path for your spell engine.

2. Thin the Deck: Activate Toon Table of Contents. Chain all copies into one another, using the final copy to grab Toon Bookmark.

3. Establish the Shield: Activate Toon Bookmark to search and activate Toon Kingdom. Exile the top card of your deck for the cost. Your Field Spell is now live, and Bookmark is sitting safely in the Graveyard to absorb any destruction effects.

4. Cheat the Field: Activate Toon Page-Flip from your hand. Reveal Toon Dark Magician, Toon Black Luster Soldier, and Toon Cannon Soldier.

• If you hard-drew Toon Mermaid: Special Summon her for free since Toon Kingdom is active to create instant tribute fodder.

5. Lock the Door: Search or set your remaining cards to put Toon Terror face-down. Your opponent starts their turn with a gutted hand against an untargetable fortress backed by an omni-negate counter trap.

 

Turn-2: The Lava-Burn OTK (Going Second)

If your opponent goes first and sets up a field, you dismantle it instantly without ever entering the Battle Phase.

1. Clear Their Board: Tribute two of your opponent's highest-threat interaction monsters to Special Summon Lava Golem to their side of the field. This cannot be negated as it is a summon cost.

2. Punish Interruption: If they try to use a monster effect or hand trap to stop your searches, immediately activate Triple Tactics Talent to look at their hand and discard their remaining response options.

3. The Shadow Strike: Activate Shadow Toon targeting the Lava Golem you just gifted them. Inflict 3000 effect damage instantly.

4. The Meat Grinder Loop: Normal or Special Summon Toon Cannon Soldier. Use your Toon engine (Page-Flip, Dark Magician, Harpie, Mermaid) to flood your board with Toon monsters. Tribute every single Toon monster sequentially using Toon Cannon Soldier's effect (500 damage per click) to burn away their remaining 5,000 LP entirely inside Main Phase 2.

 

How to Use the Extra Deck (The Metamorphosis Lines)

Because you do not run classic Polymerization, your Extra Deck is purely accessed via the Side Deck card Metamorphosis. You tribute a monster on your field to cheat out a Fusion monster of the exact same level.

• Tribute a Level 4 Monster (Toon Mermaid or Toon Harpie Lady) ➡️ Summon Dark Blade the Dragon Knight

• The Play: When playing against graveyard-reliant decks (like Lightsworn or Tearlaments), summon Dark Blade. Because your Toons can attack directly under Toon Kingdom, it is incredibly easy to inflict battle damage and instantly banish 3 core monsters from their Graveyard.

• Tribute a Level 5 Monster (Toon Cannon Soldier) ➡️ Open the Strategic Toolbox

• The Play (Anti-Spell): Choose Dark Balter the Terrible if you need to shut down your opponent's Spell cards. Pay 1,000 LP to negate any Normal Spell they activate.

• The Play (Anti-Trap): Choose Ryu Senshi if your opponent is playing a heavy Trap-based deck. He is completely unaffected by Normal Traps (like Torrential Tribute) and negates targeting spells.

• The Play (Hand Destruction): Choose Reaper on the Nightmare to attack them directly under Toon Kingdom and rip a final card from their hand on hit.

• Tribute a Level 7 Monster (Toon Dark Magician) ➡️ Summon Cyber Blader (The Perfect Field Lock)

• The Play: Use this line when your opponent has exactly 3 monsters on the field (or exactly 1 monster plus the 2-monster Lava Golem you gifted them).

• The Result: While they control exactly 3 monsters, Cyber Blader negates every single card effect your opponent controls [fandom.com]. This freezes their entire field, allowing you to execute your burn spells with zero fear of interruption.

 

How to Use the Side Deck & Anti-Blowout Tech

The Side Deck is explicitly designed to completely change gears when you know you are being forced to go second in Games 2 or 3, or when you need hard counters to game-ending floodgates.

• The Strategy Shift: Hand-ripping cards (Duo, Sentry, Confiscation) lose massive value when your opponent has already played their hand onto the field.

• Going-Second Configuration:

• SWAP OUT: 3x Hand-Rips, 1x Toon Terror, 2x Toon Cannon Soldier

• IN: 3x Evenly Matched, 2x Lightning Storm, 1x Harpie's Feather Duster

• The Play: Enter your turn, immediately skip to the end of your Battle Phase, and drop Evenly Matched. This forces your opponent to banish their entire board face-down until they control only 1 card. You can then safely set up your castle in Main Phase 2 against an empty field.

• Beating Backrow/Floodgates: If your opponent relies on traps like Anti-Spell Fragrance, drop Red Reboot directly from your hand to freeze their traps for the turn. If they side in heavy backrow removal for Toon Kingdom, side in Solemn Judgment to say "No" to any card that threatens your field.

Summon Winda, the main goal of the Shaddoll Deck since its release of Duelest Genesis, and 12+ years later, that's still basically the goal. That said, the new toys the Deck has received in the intervening years, especially those provided by Glorious Gallery, have made this end goal far easier to achieve. 

Now, you're probably looking at this assemblage of 60 cards and thinking to yourself that it's probably not any kind of serious threat. After all, 60 cards rarely work out in this day and age unless they're just a massive pile of syngergistic engines all cobbled together, but I'll ask you to keep an open mind as I explain some of my choices, inclusions, and exclusions.

  1. The Nemeses cards
    1. Because the main game plan of the Deck is to summon El Shaddoll Meshachrer through a combination of Squamata's send effect and Grysta's banish to fuse effect on your turn and El Shaddoll Winda on your opponent's turn by banishing the materials from your GY with Schism, you wind up with a lot of your resources stranded in your Banishment, which can be a bit annoying if you're forced to banish one of your singleton cards like Beast, Hedgehog, or Apkallone. The Nemeses monsters resolve this issue, allowing you to recur these resources and return them to the Deck while also providing you with the necessary typings to summon El Shaddolls Grysta and Anoyatyllis to help your Winda fully lock your opponent out of Special Summoning.
      1. Flag is undoubtedly the best of the bunch, being the searcher for the archtype, while Umbrella and Keystone...while not as strong as Flag...both have their utilities. Then, in Games 2 and 3, you can bring in Eschatos from the Side Deck once you know what your opponent's playing and lock them out of Summoning any type of monster.
      2. Sadly, Corridor didn't make the cut for this list, which is unfortunate because I think its ability to add back one of your banished Nemeses monsters would be beneficial. However, because the Wind Shaddoll fusions aren't as strong as the other elements...and because Lev Shaddoll Fusion locks you into specifically Shaddolls, meaning no Thunder Dragon Collosus...I ultimately don't think it's worth playing. If at some point in the future another wave of support gives us a better Wind Fusion or some method of making the existing ones more worthwhile to summon, I'd likely reconsider its inclusion.
  2. King of the Swamp and Fusion Substitute
    1. Because both Shaddoll Fusion and El Shaddoll Fusion have hard once per turns on their effect to Fusion Summon, there are situations where you can find yourself needing to bring out more Fusions from the Extra Deck but have used both spells and can't use them again until your next turn. This is where having extra, generic fusion spells comes in handy, and I find the King of the Swamp "engine" fulfills this role quite nicely.
      1. King of the Swamp serves a double function as both a fusion spell searcher and a Water monster to Summon Anoyatyllis, while Fusion Substitute allows you to return your spent Fusion monsters back to the Extra Deck and gives you an extra card to boot.
      2. A lot of Shaddoll lists I've seen choose to run Dracotail Faimena as their Water monster with Fusion capabilities of choice, but I'm less keen on this choice because the only viable targets for its actualy effect in the Extra Deck are Apkallone and Winda. To me, Apkallone seems like a better send off Lev Shaddoll Fusion...especially since its negation effect can't realistically be activated in response to your opponent's actions...and Winda seems like a better Schism target.
        1. I did consider running Mixousia the Confounder as a potential Super Poly target, which would undoubtedly make Faimena a better inclusion, but the Extra Deck is so tight that I don't know what I'd cut to include it. The most likely option is probably Elder Entity N'Tss, but I like having her as a Turn 3 send off a fresh copy of Lev Shaddoll Fusion to pop the opponent's Normal Summon and leave their field wide open for a direct attack.
  3. Small World
    1. Because the Deck boasts a wide selction of Types, Attributes, Levels, and ATK/DEF stats, Small World essentially lets you search whatever you need in any given situation. 
      1. Small World also makes the inclusion of King of the Swamp, Umbrella, and Keystone a bit more defendable, as each of them can bridge into most of the Shaddolls through Mathemetician since King and Umbrella are both Level 3's and Keystone is an Earth. Here again though, Flag proves to be the best of the bunch as, provided you still have Falco in the Deck, you can search Armegeddon Knight, which is arguably the best starter in the Deck.
  4. Sol and Luna
    1. Admittedly, this is probably the weakest inclusion in the Deck, like everything else, it has its merits. Because all of the Main Deck Shaddolls are Flip monsters...and those Flip Effects can be as strong or in some cases stronger than the "sent to GY" effects...being able to flip them up/down can net your a fair bit of advantage, while flipping your opponent's Normal Summon face down means that...on top of not being able to Special Summon for the rest of the turn...they won't be able to attempt to beat over any of your Shaddolls during their Battle Phase.
      1. In opening hands that include Sol and Luna, making one of the last Shaddoll effects you activate be either Wendi's or Falco's means that this card will be live on your opponent's turn. Likewise, there are situations where you end up having your second copy of Construct stranded on the field with zero attack because you Summoned it with the effect of Lev Shaddoll Fusion, in which case Sol and Luna can help you reset Construt's attack and give you another strong body to attempt to leathal your opponent on Turn 3.

Of course, as is always the case, the Deck isn't without its downsides.

  1. Ash Blossom and Droll
    1. Big surprise, right, that the Deck that needs to able to search cards and aims to add to Hand several times doesn't little zombie girls and terror bird aficianados...not sure what kind of bird the Lock Bird is supposed to be, but it kind of reminds me of a terror bird, so we'll go with that.
  2. The Summon Locks
    1. While the new support from Glorious Gallery was undeniably strong and helps out the Deck a lot, the fact that both Tolshaddoll Grysta and Lev Shaddoll Fusion lock you into only summoning Shaddolls when you use either of them really puts a hamper on the Deck's ability to pair it with other Fusion based strategies...I get the sentiment, but can you imagine a world where these locks weren't included and you could combine this Deck with Invoked or Branded or both...Best Deck, anyone?

Overall, the Deck can be quite rewarding to play, and I'd highly recommend picking it up if you'd like to test your skills a bit.

Hello! It's time to mill the opponent with an unforeseen method. If you don't know how to play Isolde decks, you can check this guide! However, there are few differences from the original guide...

 

  • When Isolde sends Cursed to GY, find Burning rather than Broken.
  • After Selene#1, when Monk + Uppercutter + Sparrer are present, make Dempsey to find Renaud.
  • Rest of guide is quite similar.

 

 

Glossary

  • ED: Extra Deck
  • BZ: Banish Zone
  • GY: Graveyard

 

Gameplan

1) When Isolde sends Cursed to GY, find Burning via Cursed. When Dempsey >>> Renaud is here, use Renaud to find Cursed. Then, play Burning >>> Cursed to skip your opponent's Main Phase 1 via Burning and bounce Burning via Cursed.

2) When Selene#2 is present, Cursed can fetch Broken. After Monk >>> Ferret = Lonefire + Lilith play, use Selene + Renaud = Zealantis and reset the board.

3) Find the following combo pieces with these cards...

  • Monk >>> Mark >>> Temple
  • Lonefire >>> Cattycorn >>> Fusion Gate
  • Lilith >>> Chain Material

4) After the activation of combo pieces in #3, Link Summon Singularity. Then, use Gate to place the following monsters with these as materials...

  • Idaten = Chief + Dynasty
  • Absolute = Stratos + Aqua-Dolphin

5) Before placing Wake Up, count how many cards you have in your Main Deck. Here are your equations for the calculations...

  • If Clock Wyvern was in your hand, (Main Deck - 24) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.
  • If Clock Wyvern was in your deck, (Main Deck - 25) equation gives you how many Warriors you need to banish from Main Deck for Wake Up.

6) So, let's assume Main Deck has 32 cards and Wyvern was in Main Deck. After Wake Up is present, that means you should have 25 x Main Deck cards. Therefore, you have to banish 7 x Warriors from your Main Deck but there is a catch due to UI of Master Duel...

  • First, pick Absolute.
  • Second, don't pick anything from Main Deck. Only hand or GY.
  • Third, count only 7 x Warriors from Main Deck except Cross + Liquid and don't pick anything extra.

7) After the revision of Main Deck amount, Fusion Summon Cyberse Clock Dragon via Gate by picking up Wyvern first and all Links at last. If you have done the calculations correct in #6, Clock Dragon should empty your whole Main Deck. After depleting your Main Deck, Laundry Trap should ask you to add a card to your hand, which should be Wanghu and nothing else...

  • If, in case you had Laundry in your hand, use Idaten to discard your whole hand. Then, use Laundry to get Wanghu.

8) Use Mudora to shuffle Amethyst + Black Garden + Legend of Heart and fetch Amethyst + Black Garden via Rainbow. Then, utilize Rollback + Jar of Avarice to shuffle Mystic Box + Bistro + Patrician + Unleashed + ED monster and draw 1. Don't forget to use Shadow's Light to have extra Normal Summon for Bistro.

9) Place Dogma to shuffle Saryuja + Absolute back into ED and resummon Saryuja to draw 4 and shuffle 3. Then, resummon Absolute via Gate by using Liquid + Wake Up as materials to draw the remaining combo pieces with Cross + Liquid and get rid of Amethyst.

10) Activate Black Garden and Legend of Heart to place Critias. Next, Special Summon Wanghu with Saryuja. Since Laundry blocks Wanghu, it won't detonate any future flowers you will plant. Then, Link Summon Rahamu by using Saryuja + Dogma as materials. Here, you can place Patrician via Rahamu and Bistro via Shadow's Light.

11) Gift Wanghu to the opponent with Mystic Box and set Unleashed. When it's your opponent's Draw Phase, activate Unleashed and Rollback + Front to revive Wattfox. By letting Wattfox destroyed thanks to Wanghu, your opponent won't be able to do anything to disrupt your setup, be it hand-traps or whatever.

12) To mill your opponent with Bistro, you have to let your opponent's monster redirect to Butcher thanks to Patricia. However, if your opponent runs out of monsters, Battle Phase can be concluded. To workaround, when your opponent has at least one monster, redirect to Critias and reuse Front time and time again to revive Scrap Shark. Thanks to Shark planting monsters to opposing side via Garden, you can redirect to Butcher again.

13) Repeat what was explained in #12 until opponent runs out of cards.

deck_excerpt: Make Electrumite = win, Electrumite negated = tears and sadness.
deck_description:
Calling this deck a "Magician" deck is really quite a stretch given we're only playing two Magician monsters and an honourary Magician, in Astrograph Sorcerer. The philosophy that underlies this deck list is pretty much that making Electrumite enables everything that you could ever want and also that Supreme King Gate Magician is the best card to build a deck around in order to facilitate that with the fewest cards most consistently, which in turn allows you to cram as much non-engine as a pendulum deck can possibly manage.

 

Pendulum summoning has a few major weaknesses, firstly you need to have two cards on the field that do basiclly nothing other than enable summoning, secondly its very difficult to make many plays without committing to the board. This deck is just meant to get as many free +1's as possible and use that advantage to build a field of powerful boss monsters that can be enabled by the material we have access to. It is not a very layered type of interaction as the ideal endboard is just three ommnis, a bounce, and an IP into SP for the double banish, but it can absolutely still win games.

 

As far as engine ratios go I will explain my thoughts here. Skullcrobat Joker is the best normal summon as he can get you a +2 with Monkeyboard and also set your scales. He's a level 4 non-tuner that can be used to make Savage Dragon and also just an effect monster for generic links and a Pend body for Electrumite and friends. Since we're not running any other normal summons I think three of him is justifiable.

 

Darkwurm is the other "normal summon", I put quotation marks there because he is absolutely a soft garnet that is not a part of any of your best hands. Ideally you send him off of Shrine or Foolish as a starter cos he searches Gate Magician while also providing a free body on board. I'm playing two because it turns him from a hard garnet to a soft garnet, eg drawing your one darkwurn completely shuts down any shrines whereas if you have a second copy in deck you can still use shrine.

 

Celestial Magician is another soft garnet. He's fine to normal summon if you absolutely have to but generally I use him as a scale to search with either Monkeyboard or Skullcrobat Joker since he's the best 8 scale Performapal, which you need to make sure Monkeyboards scale isn't 4, while also having both a scale and monster effect that can come up. Definitely only need the one as drawing him at all is just eh.

 

Lightwurm the decks tuner that allows you to access Savage Dragon and Baronne. He's fine, usually the search target for Gate Magician. His Pendulum effect will never come up but he is the other high scale in the deck and his monster effect has come up a few times for me. Playing two is fine because he's a potential normal summon when paired with a hard drawn Gate Magician where you use the Gate Magicians pend effect to pop himself then normal the Lightwurm to add him back and activate in hand to summon and search. The main reason though that we play two is because it allows us to pop him with electrumite then search the second copy with Astrograph to use him as both a scale and a tuner in the same turn.

 

Kirin is just a fun inclusion to be honest, its yet another soft garnet that we typically either search with Beyond the Pendulum or add to extra with Electrumite in the situation that Astrograph was in the opener. You usually want to pend summon for five and use them all as material before then summoning Kirin with Exceed or if you used her effect for extension, summoning him at the start of your opponents main phase. If your board is particularly clogged you can use him with IP for double removal by activating his effect first then chaining IP to make an SP with her and him which leads to the other target still being bounced by Kirins effect. One is fine because you will never want more than one and its very easy to search. Insanely bricky to have at more than one and also not very beneficial at all. When the retrain comes out I might end up running 2-3 just because it has an effect to special itself which makes it quite a good board breaker as well as being another way to make Electrumite prior to the pendulum summon, which will be less of a concern anyway with Override Dragon but sadly we have neither of those cards in MD yet so we suffer with the original 2016 Kirin for now.

 

Monkeyboard is just a free +2 when paired with Skullcrobat so three of him is good. In addition to that he's a level 6 which is why we play Baronne. If you don't draw him or have a way to him then thats why we play Savage Dragon but Baronne is just good enough that having her in like half of your endboards is worth the ED slot imo.

 

Astrograph is a three of because hard drawing him is massively beneficial for the combo. With some hands you can resolve his effect three times for a +3 in total which is pretty fun. Him plus Gate Magician does everything the deck is trying to do, and half the deck is ways to get Gate Magician. Also I'm not running Stargazer because it is just such a bad soft Garnet. If they make a card which is treated as Stargazers name in deck I'll be so happy, I really don't see why they didn't do that for his retrain in MAMO but also the retrain is a 1.5 card full combo and then some so I can't complain too much when he comes to MD.

 

Gate Zero is another soft garnet that we play pretty much just as a scale and a level 7 for Absolute Dragon. Two is good because its only a soft garnet and drawing it plus Gate Magician or a way to it is pretty much full combo. The second copy is pretty much there in case you need to pop it with Electrumite so you can get the other search although it is a debatable inclusion.

 

Now we get to Gate Magician himself which is absolutely the lynchpin of the main deck. Three is great because the basic set up just requires two gate magicians to do some fun stuff, although ideally three cards is needed for the full endboard, which is bad in the modern era but yknow if you wanna play a good deck then sadly pends isn't really the place to be.

 

Foolish and Dragon shrine are basically the same card, a starter via sending Darkwurm. This is pretty much the best starter you have so we max out on them. Foolish also has the additional utility to send Kirin to revive with Exceed if necessary.

 

Finally we have two copies of wings of light. Its a decent consistency card, make sure to use it in draw phase to avoid those pesky Drolls. Only on two because its a UR and expensive but mainly because it sucks to draw in multiples. Everything else is at least a summonable body in multiples but Wings is just completely dead at two in hand so thats why I shaved the third copy.

 

Gaze of Timaeus is kinda an engine requirement I guess so I'll put it here. Obviously we only play one because its the worst card in the main deck and is seemingly always glued to my opening hand, particularly when going second.

 

The non-engine is about as much as I can fit without constantly bricking on it due to the lack of 1 card starters. Droll is a miserable card both to use and be used on you.

 

We lose heavily to Droll so its a must have Crossout target. It can also just win games on its own, particularly against non-meta so we play the max of two copies.

 

Maxx C is just a broken horrible little insect so we play the one both to cheese the occasional win and also prevent us getting cheesed with crossout. Ash is a three of just because we can, its pretty much always live as a one for one negate and additionally stops Maxx C and the Charmies which we lost to heavily (Other than Meowls, if they use that I'd be fine letting it go through, enjoy your 0-1 draws depending on what I summon with Exceed idiot).

 

Fuwa is also run at three, sometimes bricks you going first but can also be pend summoned for Savage Dragon material and its just a generically good high impact hand trap, better than Nib in the current format because its usually an upstart/pot of greed at worse while in the same situation Nib is just a complete brick that you can't even normal summon.

 

I'm playing three triple tactics talents as a board breaker. I prefer this over everything else as it has applications being a forceful sentry when you go first and its also just versitile without needing the heavy loss of advantage that Droplet entails. Doesn't help that Droplet can't send your scales on on field pends for cost.

 

Lastly theres the single Crossout, not much to say on him other than a bad Called by is still a called by and worth playing even if it does sometimes feel bad and dead.

 

The extra deck is incredibly tight just because you typcially burn through 9-11 of the slots for your turn 1 setup which pretty much just leaves 4 tech/utility cards to play. I'll explain the combo cards first. Vortex and Absolute go together, they basically allow you to make any two level 7s into an ommni that also breaks boards with its bounce and recycles your engine cards, definitely the best endboard piece because of that utility.

 

Dragoon and DMOD also go together, not much to say here other than Pends count as spells so its always live, especially with Astrograph. This package is another reason why we run three Astrograph becuase then even if Electrumite gets negated you can still make Dragoon.

 

Savage Dragon and Baronne are also basically the same card, we run both because Baronne is better but Savage is more accessible so depending on your hand you can put either on on your endboard. Also its just good to be able to make the other one turn three after having your board broken.

 

Odd-Eyes Rebellion Xyz Dragon is just the best extra deck dimensional dragon to send with Gate Magicians effect. Hopes and prayers that we get one with a GY effect eventually but for now occasionally you maybe might summon him and get the double pop off so thats something. Literally has never come up for me though so if you wanna save the UR CP then replace him with Rune-Eyes and it will probably never make a difference.

 

Electrumite is the lynchpin of the deck, you summon it and send Astrograph, then pop to add back Astrograph and draw. Depending on how your hand was you can then make Promethean Princess to bring back Electrumite and then pop the Princess for another search. This only works though if you used Gate Magicians pend effect and don't already have all three copies of him in roatation so I suppose its a debatable win more inclusion that you could cut.

 

Masq is just still the best link 2 for your endboard, I usually try to make her with Absolute and DMOD for the value because then she's basically free or only takes 1 monster depending on how you look at it.

 

Beyond comes up like sometimes. Can make her with Astrograph and Electrumite to search Kirin or use her other effect when breaking boards, especially since its super easy to chainblock.

 

Little Knight is Little Knight, not much to say other than summon her with IP, use her effect to reset Baronne, and be careful not to mess up your OTKs with her.

 

Exceed is just a phenomenal extender, you can add back anything you send with Electrumite if you hard drew Astrograph and also use her in both turns for value so I usually end on her.

 

Then the only two real tech choices are Goddess and TY-PHON. I like to have TY-PHON because Zeus is just a few too many ED slots and I have won games because of him. Goddess is just fun to make with IP and also really useful for Crooked cooks or other dinguses that you may run into. Also good as a comeback card with the permanent negation, warning on GY summons and protection.

 

Thats pretty much it. I'm only in Gold 4 with this deck atm because uni doesn't give me much room to play Master Duel but I'm hoping to get to Plat at least and maybe Diamond. Don't think I'll make it to Master but I'll keep updating this profile as I think its the most comprehensive one of my current thoughts about playing Pendulums in Master Duel. If you are one of the three people who read this entire two thousand word rant about my ratios and techs then thank you and I hope you have a truly wonderful day. I mainly decided to write this all out because it enrages me to look through a deck profile and get to a card that I'm just thinking "Why the hell are you running this buddy?" so even if nobody ever reads the entire thing it can at least hopefully serve as a reference for the few people who might wonder why I'm running a certain card or a certain ratio.

 

Also lastly on the cost of the deck, its definitely a fairly pricy engine for how good it actually is. 600 of the 1110 UR CP are generic cards that you may already have and if not can be used in other decks, totalling 20 individual URs, then the engine itself is 510 UR CP of cards that are really only for this deck or some similar variant. Promethean Princess is kinda generic cos I know other decks play her but I still put her as an engine card cos her applications are much more narrow than Baronne, Savage, or IP. That totals 17 URs that you need to craft or pull just for it, which isn't the best or the worse in terms of cost, just relatively high for the power level. One recommendation that I have is to get the DM structure deck cos it has DMOD for 500 gems which is pretty good given that you pull an average of 2.2 URs per 10 packs (unless you're me in which case you save up for 20 Tear packs today and get one single fucking UR) so that means the cost of crafting any UR is about 1500 gems not counting pulling for packs.

deck_description: Forged over ~24 hours, my attempt at a domain format deck.
Purrely + Dark World go 1st
Purrely + Dark World go 2nd

Welcome! Previously on this deck, I discovered how to FTK with Wind-Up and Goblin archetypes together. Now, I decided to add Fusion Gate into equation and results were fruitful. Let's get into action!

 

 

Gameplan

1) Special Summon Monk with Saryuja. Then, discard Wind-Up Key via Monk to place Ferret. Use Ferret to bring forth Lilith + Diviner + Conjurer.

2) Replace Saryuja with Zealantis and reset the board via Zealantis. This actions leads into activation of following pieces...

  • Lilith >>> Chain Material
  • Diviner >>> Send Gulgolet to GY >>> Gulgolet finds Forbidden Dress
  • Conjurer >>> Magical Dimension

3) Repeat Monk by discarding Magical Dimension to place Mark and find Temple. After the activation of Temple + Chain, Link Summon Proxy F but don't use Diviner + Conjurer as materials. Then, use Proxy F to place Saurus, which places Gate onboard.

4) Synchro Summon Shenshen by using Diviner (2 to 6) + Conjurer as materials and activate Dress on Shenshen to protect it from destruction. Next, place Tomorrow and Earth Golem. Now, you have guaranteed that whenever you miss the call from Tomorrow, you won't take any damage thanks to Earth Golem. If you have board space, you can also place Electrum#1 and Five-Headed Dragon as well.

5) Pull the trigger via Tomorrow. If you got it right, good for you. Otherwise, you need to place Electrum#2 to recover your resources, including Tomorrow for repeated usages. Simply put, repeat what was explained in #4 thanks to recycle of Electrums, until your opponent is dead.

 

If you wonder how to save up some SR and UR points, I can show you:

- "Kaitoptera" + "Horned Saurus" can be found within "Desire for Change" Timed Pack to save 60 SR!

- "Dugg Charger" + "Wind-Up Magician" + "Wind-Up Shark" + "Grand Entrance" + "Zenmaity" + "Zenmaintenance" + "Big Gabonga" can be found within "Bonkers Bikers' Wild Wheels" Secret Pack to save 240 SR and 120 UR!

- "Speedroid Terrortop" can be found within "Warp-Speed Toys" Secret Pack to save 90 SR!

- "Materiactor Gigadra" can be found within "Transmigration Reactor" Secret Pack to save 90 SR!

- "Lilith, Lady of Lament" can be either found within "Illusion Beast's Roar" or "Rulers of Darkness" Secret Packs to save 30 UR!

- "Lonefire Blossom" + "Predaplant Ophrys Scorpio" can be found within "Ravenous Invasive Flora" Secret Pack to save 90 SR!

- "Summoner Monk" can be found within "True Awakening of the Oathbound Knights" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

- "The Man with the Mark" + "Temple of the Kings" can be found within "Infernal Labyrinth of No Escape" Secret Pack to save 30 SR and 30 UR!

- "Electrum" + "Five-Headed Dragon" can be found within "Legacy Pack" to save 60 SR and 30 UR!

- "Worldsea Dragon Zealantis" can be found within "Raging God of the Sea" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Primathmech Alembertian" can be found within "Supreme Strike" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Diviner of the Herald" can be found within "Miraculous Advent" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Shenshen" can be found within "Cyber City Guardians" Secret Pack to save 30 UR!

- "Proxy F Magician" can be found within "Songstress of Sorrow Song" Secret Pack to save 30 SR!

 

So, in total, you can save up to 720 SR and 330 UR, if you are willing to spend some gems. Other SR and UR cards I didn't mention are essential.

 

That's all for this one. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Have fun in Master Duel!
